knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Column Nonnegativity Is Insufficient
No-Improving-Generator Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost certificate for a finite-dimensional conic atomic master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\subset\mathbb R^n\) be the generator set and consider finite-support coefficients \(\lambda_g\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{g\in G}\lambda_gAg=b\), with objective \(\sum_{g\in G}\lambda_gc^\top g\). For a restricted-master dual vector \(y\), define \(r_y(g)=c^\top g-y^\top Ag\). A validated exact-pricing result \(\rho(y)=\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)\ge0\) certifies \(r_y(g)\ge0\) for every generator. Hence \(y\) is feasible for the full dual and \(b^\top y\) is a valid lower bound. If the restricted-master value equals \(b^\top y\), its current primal solution is globally optimal for the full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual vector and exact pricing result showing every generator has nonnegative reduced cost certify full dual feasibility and, with zero master duality gap, global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(G\subset\mathbb R^n\) and all displayed sums have finite support.
The restricted master has primal and dual solutions with equal finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(y)\ge0\Longrightarrow b^\top y\le v\), and equality with the restricted-master value certifies optimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why the sign of an inexact oracle's returned reduced cost is not itself a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\eta>0\), let \(G=\{g_1,g_2\}\), \(r_y(g_1)=0\), and \(r_y(g_2)=-\eta/2\). Returning \(\widehat g=g_1\) satisfies \(r_y(\widehat g)\le\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)+\eta\), although \(r_y(\widehat g)\ge0\) and \(\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)<0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \rho(y)=\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)=-\infty, no finite returned value r_y(\widehat g) and finite \eta\ge0 can satisfy r_y(\widehat g)\le\rho(y)+\eta. Unbounded pricing therefore requires a separate recession or unboundedness certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Pricing-Optimization Error Enclosure
Pricing-Error Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certificate for an inexact reduced-cost pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r_y(g)=c^\top g-y^\top Ag\), let \(\widehat g\in G\) be returned by a pricing oracle and let \(\eta\ge0\). The pair \((\widehat g,\eta)\) is a pricing-error certificate when a verifiable oracle bound establishes \(r_y(\widehat g)\le\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)+\eta\). Equivalently, \(\underline\rho=r_y(\widehat g)-\eta\) satisfies \(\underline\rho\le\rho(y):=\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)\le r_y(\widehat g)\). Thus \(\underline\rho\ge0\) certifies absence of improving generators; otherwise \(\underline\rho\) quantifies the worst unresolved reduced-cost violation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegative Exact Reduced Cost Certifies Full-Master Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-correction certificate after solving a restricted master and performing exact global pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a restricted-master primal-dual pair be optimal with common value \(U=b^\top y\). Assume \(y\) satisfies every full-master dual constraint other than the generator inequalities tested by pricing. If exact pricing over the full generator set gives \(\rho(y)=\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)\ge0\), then \(y\) is feasible for the full-master dual. Since the restricted-master primal solution is feasible for the full master, \(b^\top y\le v\le U\), and hence \(v=U=b^\top y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a restricted master is solved, exact nonnegative reduced costs make its dual vector full-master feasible and certify global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted-master primal and dual optima are attained with common value \(U=b^\top y\).
All nonpricing full-master dual constraints are satisfied by \(y\).
Exact pricing covers every admissible generator and returns \(\rho(y)\ge0\).
Restricted-master columns are admissible full-master columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Exact Reduced Cost Certifies Full-Master Optimality
Exact-Pricing Bound Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-master lower bound obtained from exact pricing and a coefficient-mass bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the conic atomic master with feasible finite-support coefficients \(\lambda_g\ge0\), and suppose every feasible solution under consideration satisfies \(\sum_g\lambda_g\le T\). For any restricted-master dual vector \(y\), exact pricing gives \(\rho(y)=\inf_{g\in G}(c^\top g-y^\top Ag)\). Every full-master feasible solution then has objective at least \(L(y)=b^\top y+T\min\{0,\rho(y)\}\). Consequently \(L(y)\le v\). In particular, when \(\rho(y)\ge0\), the correction vanishes and \(b^\top y\) is a full-master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact minimum reduced cost, combined with a known bound on total generator weight, yields a corrected lower bound for the full master.
assumptions_latex: Every relevant full-master feasible representation satisfies \(\sum_g\lambda_g\le T<\infty\).
Exact pricing computes \(\rho(y)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of the mass-corrected lower bound to a certified reduced-cost interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\ge0\), let \(\rho\) be the exact minimum reduced cost, and suppose \(\underline\rho\le\rho\le\underline\rho+\eta\) with \(\eta\ge0\). Define \(L(t)=b^\top y+T\min\{0,t\}\). Then \(L(\underline\rho)\le L(\rho)\) and \(0\le L(\rho)-L(\underline\rho)\le T\eta\).

Let \(y\) be restricted-master dual feasible and let pricing return \(\widehat g\) with a certified additive error \(\eta\), so \(\underline\rho=r_y(\widehat g)-\eta\le\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality test recognizing when an attained restricted-master solution is full-master optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_t\subseteq F\) be the feasible sets of a restricted and full minimization master, with values \(v_t=\inf_{x\in F_t}c^\top x\) and \(v=\inf_{x\in F}c^\top x\). If the restricted master attains \(v_t\) at \(x_t\), then \(v_t=v\) if and only if \(x_t\) is full-master optimal. In particular, if \(L_t\leq v\) is a certified lower bound and \(L_t=v_t\), then \(L_t=v=v_t\) and \(x_t\) is full-master optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attained restricted solution is globally optimal exactly when its value equals the full value; equality with a certified lower bound proves this directly.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Exactness Test
Restricted-Master Bound Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone bound ordering for nested restricted generator sets in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_t\subseteq G_{t+1}\subseteq G\), and let \(v_t\), \(v_{t+1}\), and \(v\) denote the infima of the corresponding feasible conic atomic minimization masters. Enlarging the generator set enlarges the primal feasible region, so \(v\le v_{t+1}\le v_t\), with the convention that an infeasible restricted master has value \(+\infty\). Any valid exact- or certified-inexact-pricing lower bound \(L_t\) additionally satisfies \(L_t\le v\). Thus the certified ordering is \(L_t\le v\le v_{t+1}\le v_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, adding generators cannot increase the restricted-master value; every certified pricing lower bound remains below the full-master optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(G_t\subseteq G_{t+1}\subseteq G\).
All masters use identical constraints and objective coefficients for shared generators.

notation.meaning: Generator set present at iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization ordering for nested restricted masters is standard and correctly stated, but the record supplies no source for the column-generation interpretation or certified lower-bound component.

children.title: Nonclosed Generation
children.top_down_role: Generated representations whose attainable generator combinations are not closed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional characterization of a generated cone failing to contain all limits of its finite combinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(K=\operatorname{cone}(G)\) denote its finite conic hull. Then \(K\) is nonclosed if and only if there exist \(x_k\in K\) and \(\bar x\notin K\) such that \(x_k\to\bar x\). Equivalently, \(K\subsetneq\overline K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite conic generation is nonclosed exactly when attainable finite combinations converge to a point with no attainable finite representation.
assumptions_latex: \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(\operatorname{cone}(G)\) uses finite nonnegative combinations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ is nonclosed}\iff\exists(x_k)\subseteq K,\ \bar x\notin K:\ x_k\to\bar x\iff K\subsetneq\overline K\).

notation.meaning: Finite conic hull of the generators.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Characterization of Nonclosed Generation
Nonclosed Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete generator family whose finite conic hull is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(G=\{(t,1):t>0\}\) and let \(K=\operatorname{cone}(G)\) mean finite nonnegative conic combinations. Every nonzero element of \(K\) has both coordinates strictly positive, and every pair with strictly positive coordinates belongs to \(K\). Hence \(K=\{(u,v):u>0,\ v>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\). The sequence \((1,1/k)=k^{-1}(k,1)\in K\) converges to \((1,0)\notin K\). Therefore \(K\) is not closed and \(\overline K=\mathbb R_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rays generated by points (t,1) with positive t fill the open positive quadrant plus zero, whose closure also contains the coordinate axes.
assumptions_latex: Conic hulls use finite nonnegative combinations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is self-contained, correct, and appropriate for Nonclosed Generation, but the evidence contract requires an external source or other admissible evidence.

children.title: Master Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Restricted or limiting master values lacking attaining representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of nonattainment for a generated conic master, independently of its cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v=\inf\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), finite-valued master nonattainment means that the feasible set is nonempty, \(v\in\mathbb R\), and no feasible point realizes \(v\). Equivalently, \(c^\top x>v\) for every feasible \(x\), while there exists a feasible sequence \((x_k)\) with \(c^\top x_k\to v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master is finitely nonattained when it has a finite approachable infimum but no feasible minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\).
\(v\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Cone or generated set used by the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Valued Master Nonattainment
Master Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued conic master whose infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\{(t,1):t>0\}\), \(K=\operatorname{cone}(G)\), and consider \(\inf\{v:(u,v)\in K,\ u=1\}\). Its feasible set is \(\{(1,v):v>0\}\). For every \(k\ge1\), the point \((1,1/k)=k^{-1}(k,1)\) is feasible, so the infimum is \(0\). No feasible point has second coordinate zero, however, and therefore no point attains this infimum. Thus finite objective value and feasibility alone do not guarantee attainment when the generated cone is nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slice of a nonclosed generated cone can have objective values approaching zero while containing no point that attains zero.
assumptions_latex: Conic combinations are finite and have nonnegative coefficients.

notation.meaning: Cone generated by the family (t,1), t positive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonattainment example is internally correct and fits the leaf, but it has no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Closure-Induced Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Nonattainment attributable to gaps between generated sets and their closures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion separating value preservation under closure from attainment in the generated master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=K\cap\{x:Ax=b\}\) and \(F^{\mathrm{cl}}=\overline K\cap\{x:Ax=b\}\). Suppose \(F\neq\varnothing\), \(\inf_{x\in F}c^\top x=\min_{x\in F^{\mathrm{cl}}}c^\top x=v\), and every minimizer over \(F^{\mathrm{cl}}\) belongs to \(F^{\mathrm{cl}}\setminus F\). Then the original master has value \(v\) but does not attain it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If closure preserves the value but every closure-relaxed optimizer is absent from the generated feasible set, the original master is nonattained.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\).
The closure-relaxed minimum exists and equals the original infimum.
\(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F^{\mathrm{cl}}}c^\top x\subseteq F^{\mathrm{cl}}\setminus F\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set using the generated cone.
Feasible set using the closure of the generated cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Only Optimizer Criterion
Closure-Induced Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating the generated master from its closed-cone relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{(t,1):t>0\}\). The original master \(\inf\{v:(u,v)\in K,\ u=1\}\) has value \(0\) but no minimizer. Replacing \(K\) by its closure \(\overline K=\mathbb R_+^2\) leaves the infimum unchanged, yet the closed relaxation attains it at \((1,0)\). Thus equality of the original and closure-relaxed optimal values does not imply attainment by a finite conic combination; the closure can introduce an optimal point absent from the generated cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a generated cone may preserve the optimal value while adding the missing optimizer, so closure-relaxed attainment need not imply master attainment.
assumptions_latex: The original master permits only finite conic combinations of generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(K)=v(\overline K)=0\), while attainment holds only for the problem over \(\overline K\).

notation.meaning: Infimum over the slice of cone C.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closure-induced failure distinction is correctly illustrated and the content kind fits, but the claim lacks admissible cited evidence.

children.title: Attainment Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where closure or representation changes restore attainment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A recession condition ensuring level-boundedness and attainment of the generated master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and suppose \(v=\inf_{x\in F}c^\top x\in\mathbb R\). If \(c^\top d>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(F)\), then every nonempty sublevel set \(\{x\in F:c^\top x\leq\alpha\}\) is compact, and the minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict objective increase along every nonzero feasible recession direction makes the closed convex master level-bounded and guarantees attainment.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(v=\inf_{x\in F}c^\top x\in\mathbb R\).
\(c^\top d>0\) for every \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(F)\setminus\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Direction Attainment Criterion
Attainment Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness and compact-level-set conditions sufficient for master attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the generated cone and consider \(v=\inf\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\). Attainment is recovered if \(K\) is closed, the problem is feasible with finite infimum, and some nonempty feasible sublevel set \(S_\alpha=\{x\in K:Ax=b,\ c^\top x\le\alpha\}\) is compact. Under these conditions the continuous objective attains its minimum on \(S_\alpha\), hence there exists \(x^\star\in K\) with \(Ax^\star=b\) and \(c^\top x^\star=v\). Finite polyhedral generation supplies closedness; bounded feasible sublevel sets supply compactness in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed generated cone and a nonempty compact feasible objective sublevel set guarantee that the conic master attains its finite optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed.
The master is feasible with finite infimum.
\(S_\alpha\) is nonempty and compact for some finite \(\alpha\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compact-sublevel attainment condition is mathematically standard and appropriate as a condition, but no authoritative theorem or section locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Retention Boundary for Finite Addition Counts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finiteness of the generator family does not bound repeated addition events under deletion and regeneration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be finite. A bound of at most \(|G\setminus G_0|\) generator additions requires monotone retention or duplicate control preventing a deleted generator from being counted again. Otherwise an algorithm may delete an improving generated column and later regenerate it, permitting arbitrarily many addition events despite \(|G|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite column universe bounds addition events only when generated columns cannot be repeatedly deleted and re-added.
assumptions_latex: \text{Addition events, not merely distinct first discoveries, are counted}.
\text{The deletion policy permits regeneration of deleted columns}.

notation.meaning: total addition events including regenerated columns

knowledge_statements.title: Retention Boundary for Finite Addition Counts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial bound that remains valid when generated columns may later be deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the full generator universe be a finite set \(G\), and let \(G_0\subseteq G\) be initially known. Regardless of later deletion or regeneration, the number \(N_{\mathrm{first}}\) of events at which a generator in \(G\setminus G_0\) is discovered for the first time satisfies \[N_{\mathrm{first}}\le |G\setminus G_0|.\] This does not bound total addition events without retention or duplicate control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite generator universe bounds first discoveries, even though deletion may allow arbitrarily many re-additions.
assumptions_latex: |G|<\infty.
G_0\subseteq G.
\text{Each first-discovery event is assigned to one previously unseen generator}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound on Distinct First Discoveries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient exact optimality test for a finite full-master column universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^\top\lambda:A\lambda=b,\lambda\ge0\}\) over a finite column universe \(G\). If a restricted-master primal solution \(\lambda^R\) and dual vector \(y\) have equal value and satisfy \(r_g(y):=c_g-a_g^\top y\ge0\) for every \(g\in G\), then \(y\) is feasible for the full dual, \(\lambda^R\) is feasible for the full primal, and both are full-master optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-gap restricted primal-dual pair certifies global optimality when every full-universe column has nonnegative reduced cost.
assumptions_latex: The restricted primal and dual are solved exactly with equal value.
Reduced costs use the displayed minimization convention.
Every full-universe column is covered by exact pricing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination by Distinct Column Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discovery and termination bound after quotienting duplicate column representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the finite universe have \(q\) distinct coefficient-cost classes under \(g\sim h\iff(a_g,c_g)=(a_h,c_h)\). Suppose exact pricing either certifies all reduced costs nonnegative or adds an absent improving class, and every discovered class remains represented. If \(q_0\) classes are initially represented, at most \(q-q_0\) improving additions occur before termination by the full-column reduced-cost certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact pricing and retention, termination is bounded by the number of missing distinct mathematical columns rather than duplicate encodings.
assumptions_latex: The quotient universe has \(q<\infty\) classes.
Restricted-master solves and pricing are exact.
Every nonterminal iteration adds and retains an absent improving class.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination by Distinct Column Classes
Finite Polyhedral Generation Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination bound when the full generator family is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) contain \(m<\infty\) generators. At each iteration, solve the restricted master and its dual exactly; if exact pricing finds a generator with negative reduced cost, add at least one such generator not already present, and otherwise terminate. A generator already in the restricted master cannot have negative reduced cost at a dual-feasible restricted solution. Consequently every nonterminal iteration strictly enlarges the restricted set. Starting from \(G_0\), the method performs at most \(m-|G_0|\) generator-addition iterations, after which the no-improving-generator test certifies full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many generators and exact master and pricing solves, each unsuccessful iteration adds a new generator, giving finite termination after at most all missing generators.
assumptions_latex: \(|G|=m<\infty\).
Restricted masters and pricing problems are solved exactly.
Every negative reduced-cost iteration adds a previously absent generator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{add}}\le m-|G_0|\), followed by an exact optimality certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite generator-addition bound is plausible under the exact-solve assumptions and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but the termination claim and optimality certificate lack a source locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Pricing Can Falsely Certify Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed pricing-error counterexample; deferred to the inexact-oracle sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{0\lambda_1-\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\}.\] Starting with only column 1 gives restricted value \(0\), while missing column 2 has reduced cost \(-1\) and the full value is \(-1\). An oracle with absolute error allowance \(\delta\ge1\) may miss that column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently inaccurate pricing oracle can stop a two-column master at a suboptimal restricted solution.
assumptions_latex: \text{Initially only column 1 is present}.
\delta\ge1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Finite Identification under Dense Nonpolyhedral Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense ray generation of a second-order cone whose restricted values converge without finite identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \{\theta_n\}_{n\ge1}\subset[0,2\pi) be dense with \theta_n\ne\pi, set g_n=(\cos\theta_n,\sin\theta_n,1), K_t=\operatorname{cone}\{g_1,\ldots,g_t\}, and K=\overline{\operatorname{cone}\{g_n:n\ge1\}}=\{(z_1,z_2,s):\sqrt{z_1^2+z_2^2}\le s\}. For v_t=\min\{z_1:(z_1,z_2,1)\in K_t\} and v=\min\{z_1:(z_1,z_2,1)\in K\}, one has v_t=\min_{n\le t}\cos\theta_n>-1 for every finite t and v_t\downarrow-1=v.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense finite subsets of second-order-cone rays yield restricted values converging to the full value, while no finite restricted master identifies the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The ray angles form a dense sequence on the unit circle but never equal \pi.
Restricted cones retain all rays generated so far.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Cone Generation Without Feasible-Slice Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense nested cone generation alone does not ensure convergence of equality-constrained restricted masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge1\), let \(g_n=(1,1/n)\), \(K_t=\operatorname{cone}\{g_1,\ldots,g_t\}\), and \(K=\overline{\bigcup_tK_t}\). Then \((1,0)\in K\). Under the affine equations \(x_1=1\), \(x_2=0\), the full problem over \(K\) is feasible at \((1,0)\), but every nonzero point of every finite \(K_t\) has positive second coordinate. Thus every restricted problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested generated cones can approach a feasible boundary point while no finite restricted cone meets the required affine slice.
assumptions_latex: \text{Conic combination coefficients are nonnegative}.
K_t\subseteq K_{t+1}\text{ retains all generated rays}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Identification Characterization by Optimizer Capture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for finite value identification within a nested restricted-cone sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_t\subseteq K_{t+1}\subseteq K\), let \(v_t=\inf\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\in K_t\}\), and let the full problem over \(K\) have finite value \(v\). If a full optimizer \(x^\star\) belongs to \(K_t\), then \(v_t=v\) and \(v_s=v\) for every \(s\ge t\). Conversely, if the restricted problem at stage \(t\) attains its value and \(v_t=v\), every restricted optimizer is a full optimizer contained in \(K_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested restricted master identifies the full value once it captures a full optimizer; conversely, attained value equality supplies such an optimizer.
assumptions_latex: K_t\subseteq K_{t+1}\subseteq K.
v\in\mathbb R.
The converse assumes attainment of v_t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution convergence consequence after restricted-master values are known to converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_t\subseteq K\), let \(x_t\in K_t\) satisfy \(Ax_t=b\) and \(c^\top x_t=v_t\), and suppose \(K\) is closed, \(v_t\to v\), and \(v\) is the finite optimum over \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\). If \(x_{t_j}\to\bar x\), then \(\bar x\in K\), \(A\bar x=b\), and \(c^\top\bar x=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once restricted values converge, every cluster point of restricted optimizers is a full-master optimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential formulation of restricted feasible-slice density in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nested sets \(F_t\subseteq F_{t+1}\subseteq F\) in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(F\subseteq\overline{\bigcup_tF_t}\) if and only if, for every \(x\in F\), there exist indices \(t_j\uparrow\infty\) and points \(x_j\in F_{t_j}\) with \(x_j\to x\). This slice-density property is stronger than ambient cone density \(K=\overline{\bigcup_tK_t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relevant density condition is imposed on the affine-feasible slice, not merely on the ambient generated cones.

\(F_t\subseteq F_{t+1}\subseteq F\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform feasible-slice approximation sufficient for monotone convergence of linear objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_t=\{x\in K_t:Ax=b\}\) be nonempty compact sets with \(F_t\subseteq F_{t+1}\subseteq F\), where \(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\) is nonempty and compact. If \(\sup_{x\in F}\operatorname{dist}(x,F_t)\to0\), then for every \(c\), \[v_t:=\min_{x\in F_t}c^\top x\downarrow\min_{x\in F}c^\top x=:v.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform approximation of the full affine-feasible slice by nested restricted slices implies monotone convergence of every linear objective value.

\(F_t\subseteq F_{t+1}\subseteq F\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer-Approximation Criterion for Monotone Restricted Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp value-convergence regime requiring approximation of one full-master optimizer within the affine-feasible restricted slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_t\subseteq K_{t+1}\subseteq K\), define \(F_t=\{x\in K_t:Ax=b\}\), \(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\), and let \(v_t=\inf_{x\in F_t}c^Tx\). Suppose the full problem has an optimizer \(x^\star\in F\) with finite value \(v=c^Tx^\star\), and there exist \(x_t\in F_t\) such that \(x_t\to x^\star\). Then \(v\le v_{t+1}\le v_t\le c^Tx_t\), and consequently \(v_t\downarrow v\). No finite stage need attain \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested restricted masters converge monotonically in value whenever their feasible slices contain points approaching at least one full-master optimizer; uniform density of the entire feasible slice is unnecessary.
assumptions_latex: \(K_t\subseteq K_{t+1}\subseteq K\).
The full problem attains a finite optimum at \(x^\star\).
There exist \(x_t\in K_t\) with \(Ax_t=b\) and \(x_t\to x^\star\).

Full-master optimizer approximated by restricted feasible points

knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer-Approximation Criterion for Monotone Restricted Values
Asymptotic Nonpolyhedral Generation Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value convergence for nested generator sets approximating a nonpolyhedral master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_t\subseteq G_{t+1}\subseteq G\), let \(K_t=\operatorname{cone}(G_t)\), and let \(v_t=\inf\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\in K_t\}\). Suppose the full problem over \(K=\overline{\bigcup_tK_t}\) has an optimizer \(x^\star\), and there exist \(x_t\in K_t\) with \(Ax_t=b\) and \(x_t\to x^\star\). Then restricted-master ordering gives \(v\le v_{t+1}\le v_t\), while continuity gives \(\limsup_t v_t\le c^\top x^\star=v\). Hence \(v_t\downarrow v\), although no finite \(t\) need satisfy \(v_t=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested nonpolyhedral restricted masters converge in value when they contain feasible points approaching a full-master optimizer, though finite identification may fail.
assumptions_latex: The full problem over \(K\) attains its finite optimum at \(x^\star\).
There are feasible \(x_t\in K_t\) with \(x_t\to x^\star\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Pricing Error Can Cause False Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-column master showing that nonvanishing additive pricing error does not certify exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min\{-\varepsilon\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda\ge0\} with \varepsilon>0. A restricted master containing only column 1 has value U=0, while the full value is v=-\varepsilon. The omitted column has reduced cost -\varepsilon. Under an additive pricing guarantee \widehat r\le\rho+\eta with \eta\ge\varepsilon, the oracle may return the present column with \widehat r=0, thereby satisfying the sign stopping test although U-v=\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive additive pricing error may hide an improving column and permit termination at a strictly suboptimal restricted master.
assumptions_latex: The pricing oracle need only return a reduced cost at most \eta above the true pricing minimum.
\eta\ge\varepsilon>0.

notation.meaning: improvement supplied by the omitted column

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficient-Mass Control Is Essential for a Reduced-Cost Gap Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a uniform objective-gap estimate from reduced cost alone when representation mass is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), consider \(\min\{-\varepsilon\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\varepsilon\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda\ge0\}\). The restricted master containing only column 1 has value \(U_\varepsilon=0\) and dual price \(y=0\). The omitted column has reduced cost \(-\varepsilon\), whereas the full solution \((0,1/\varepsilon)\) has value \(v_\varepsilon=-1\). Thus \(U_\varepsilon-v_\varepsilon=1\) while the reduced-cost violation tends to zero and the improving representation has mass \(1/\varepsilon\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a uniform coefficient-mass bound, a vanishing reduced-cost violation can coexist with a fixed objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
The restricted master initially contains only column 1.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-consistent definition for minimization column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a restricted-master dual vector \(y\), let \(r_y(g)\) be the reduced cost of generator \(g\in G\), and let \(\rho(y)=\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)\). A pricing oracle has certified additive error \(\eta\ge0\) at \(y\) if it returns \(\widehat g\in G\) with \[\rho(y)\le r_y(\widehat g)\le\rho(y)+\eta.\] Hence \(r_y(\widehat g)-\eta\le\rho(y)\le r_y(\widehat g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive-error pricing oracle returns a column whose reduced cost is within eta above the true minimum and thereby supplies a certified lower estimate of that minimum.
assumptions_latex: G\ne\varnothing.
\rho(y)>-\infty.
\eta\ge0.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of generator g at dual vector y

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Additive-Error Pricing Oracle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation order for additive-error pricing, stopping, and bound reporting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master to a certified primal-dual value \(U_t=b^\top y_t\). If \(\widehat r_t<-\delta_t\), admit the returned improving column and continue. Otherwise report \(\rho(y_t)\ge\underline\rho_t\); an objective-gap claim additionally requires an applicable coefficient-mass bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori objective interval from a certified pricing lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=b^\top y\) be a restricted-master primal-dual value for a minimization master. Suppose every relevant full-master feasible representation has coefficient mass at most \(T\), and pricing certifies \(\rho(y)\ge\underline\rho\). Then the full optimum \(v\) satisfies \[U+T\min\{\underline\rho,0\}\le v\le U.\] Consequently \(0\le U-v\le T\max\{-\underline\rho,0\}\). For a sequence with one uniform finite mass bound and \(\max\{-\underline\rho_t,0\}\to0\), one has \(U_t\to v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform coefficient-mass bound converts the corrected pricing estimate into a full-master value interval and convergence test.

Inexact-Oracle Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified convergence under vanishing pricing and stopping tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let the restricted master have primal-dual value \(U_t=b^\top y_t\), and assume every relevant full-master representation has coefficient mass at most \(T\). Suppose pricing returns \(\widehat g_t\) satisfying \(r_{y_t}(\widehat g_t)\le\rho(y_t)+\eta_t\), and stopping occurs only when \(r_{y_t}(\widehat g_t)\ge-\delta_t\). Then \(\underline\rho_t=r_{y_t}(\widehat g_t)-\eta_t\) is a certified pricing lower bound and \(0\le U_t-v\le T(\eta_t+\delta_t)\). Therefore, along stopped iterates for which \(\eta_t\to0\) and \(\delta_t\to0\), the certified restricted-master values converge to \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If certified pricing errors and stopping tolerances vanish, the mass-corrected optimality gap vanishes and stopped restricted-master values converge to the full optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every relevant feasible representation has coefficient mass at most \(T<\infty\).
Restricted-master primal and dual values coincide.
\(\eta_t\to0\) and \(\delta_t\to0\) along stopped iterates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of the Proximal Dual Point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Nonvanishing Weighted Drift Can Prevent Pricing-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oscillatory boundary distinguishing bounded weighted displacement from vanishing displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_k^R=0\), choose \(v\ne0\), set \(\alpha_k=\alpha\in(0,1]\), and take \(\bar y_k=(-1)^kv/\alpha\). Then \(\tilde y_k=(1-\alpha_k)y_k^R+\alpha_k\bar y_k=(-1)^kv\). Although \(\alpha_k\|\bar y_k-y_k^R\|=\|v\|\) is bounded, \(\tilde y_k\) does not converge.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \tilde y_k=(1-\alpha_k)y_k^R+\alpha_k\bar y_k, one has \tilde y_k-y_k^R=\alpha_k(\bar y_k-y_k^R). Center Drift Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary caused by persistent weight on an unbounded or inaccurate dual center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex-combination pricing \(\tilde y_k=(1-\alpha_k)y_k^{R}+\alpha_k\bar y_k\), bounded restricted-master prices do not control \(\tilde y_k\) unless the weighted center drift is controlled. Indeed, take \(y_k^{R}=0\), \(\bar y_k=kv\) for a fixed \(v\ne0\), and \(\alpha_k=\alpha>0\). Then \(\lVert\tilde y_k\rVert=\alpha k\lVert v\rVert\to\infty\). Thus a convergence argument requiring bounded pricing points fails beyond the boundary \(\sup_k\alpha_k\lVert\bar y_k-y_k^{R}\rVert<\infty\); convergence to the master price additionally requires \(\alpha_k\lVert\bar y_k-y_k^{R}\rVert\to0\).

children.title: Trust-Region Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Master stabilization through general trust-region restrictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for a Euclidean-ball restricted concave dual maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be differentiable and concave on a closed convex set \(Y\), let \(T=Y\cap\{y:\lVert y-\bar y\rVert_2\le\Delta\}\), and assume a normal-cone qualification for this intersection. A point \(y^T\in T\) maximizes \(D\) over \(T\) if and only if there exist \(n_Y\in N_Y(y^T)\) and \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \(\nabla D(y^T)=n_Y+\lambda(y^T-\bar y)\) and \(\lambda(\lVert y^T-\bar y\rVert_2^2-\Delta^2)=0\). If \(\lVert y^T-\bar y\rVert_2<\Delta\), then \(\nabla D(y^T)\in N_Y(y^T)\), so \(y^T\) is also a global maximizer of \(D\) over \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region maximizer satisfies a normal-cone condition; when the ball is inactive, the same point is optimal over the unrestricted dual domain.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is closed and convex.
\(D\) is differentiable and concave on \(Y\).
\(\Delta>0\), and a normal-cone intersection qualification holds.

children.title: Box Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Master stabilization through coordinatewise bounds around reference points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric Box as a Weighted Infinity-Norm Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent representation of a symmetric componentwise stabilization box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(W=\operatorname{Diag}(\delta_1^{-1},\ldots,\delta_m^{-1})\). Then \(B(\bar y,\delta)=\{y:\bar y-\delta\le y\le\bar y+\delta\}=\{y:\lVert W(y-\bar y)\rVert_\infty\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric coordinate box is exactly a diagonally weighted infinity-norm ball around its center.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta_i>0\) for every coordinate \(i\).
Vector inequalities are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Box as a Weighted Infinity-Norm Region
Box Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise trust-region restriction of dual prices around a maintained center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For center \(\bar y_k\in\mathbb R^m\) and nonnegative half-widths \(\delta_k^-,\delta_k^+\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \(B_k=\{y\in Y:\bar y_k-\delta_k^-\le y\le\bar y_k+\delta_k^+\}\), with componentwise inequalities. Compute \(y_k^{B}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in B_k}D_k(y)\) and use it for pricing. Bounds active repeatedly in a direction of predicted improvement are relaxed; consistently inactive bounds may be tightened. Absence of a negative reduced-cost column at \(y_k^{B}\) certifies termination only after unrestricted pricing or after establishing that the box contains a relevant unrestricted dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict dual prices componentwise around a center, adapt active bounds, and do not treat box-restricted pricing alone as a global certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is closed and \(D_k\) is proper concave.
\(\delta_k^-,\delta_k^+\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and a maximizer exists.
review_flags: The supplied sources do not document box stabilization in column generation.
A direct source is needed for canonical bound adaptation rules.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and componentwise stabilization box fit the Box Stabilization leaf.
