children.title: Adaptive Stabilization Regions
children.top_down_role: Changing trust-region or box geometry across column-generation regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exhaustive Nested Expansion Recovers the Unrestricted Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-convergence safeguard for nested expanding stabilization regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1\subseteq S_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Y\) and \(\bigcup_{k\ge1}S_k=Y\). For any \(D:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\), define \(v_k=\sup_{y\in S_k}D(y)\) and \(v=\sup_{y\in Y}D(y)\). Then \(v_k\) is nondecreasing and \(v_k\uparrow v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested stabilization regions whose union is the full dual domain have restricted supremum values increasing to the unrestricted supremum.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\subseteq S_{k+1}\subseteq Y\) for every \(k\).
\(\bigcup_{k\ge1}S_k=Y\).

notation.meaning: restricted supremum over the kth region

review_flags: This is a value-recovery result, not by itself an iterate-convergence or column-generation convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Nested Expansion Recovers the Unrestricted Value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-iteration condition under which a stabilized solve is globally conclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq Y\) be the full feasible domain and \(S_k\subseteq Y\) a stabilization region. If \(F\subseteq S_k\) and \(\widehat y_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in F\cap S_k}D(y)\), then \(\widehat y_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in F}D(y)\) and the two optimal values agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilized optimum is globally conclusive when the current region is verified to contain the entire feasible domain.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq S_k\).
\(\widehat y_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in F\cap S_k}D(y)\).
review_flags: Containment must be proved; a large region or inactive boundary alone does not establish it.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrestricted Certification from Region Containment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value-convergence condition for adaptive regions that need not be nested.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\subseteq Y\), \(v_k=\sup_{y\in S_k}D(y)\), and \(v=\sup_{y\in Y}D(y)\in\mathbb R\). Then \(v_k\to v\) if and only if, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is \(K\) such that \(S_k\cap\{y:D(y)\ge v-\varepsilon\}\ne\varnothing\) for all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moving regions recover the unrestricted value exactly when every sufficiently late region contains an approximately optimal point at every requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\subseteq Y\) for every \(k\).
\(v=\sup_YD\) is finite.
review_flags: This is a value-convergence criterion, not an iterate-convergence or finite-termination theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Convergence Criterion for Moving Regions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected shrink-retain-enlarge rule under an explicit minimization-decrease convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \eta'\le\eta implies S_k(\eta')\subseteq S_k(\eta). For predicted decrease p_k>0, verified actual decrease a_k, and q_k=a_k/p_k, choose 0\le q_-<q_+, 0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+, and 0<\eta_{\min}\le\eta_{\max}. Set \eta_{k+1}=\max\{\eta_{\min},\gamma_-\eta_k\} if q_k<q_-, set \eta_{k+1}=\eta_k if q_-\le q_k<q_+, and set \eta_{k+1}=\min\{\eta_{\max},\gamma_+\eta_k\} if q_k\ge q_+. If p_k\le0, the ratio rule is undefined and requires a separately declared safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated decrease convention, shrink after poor agreement, retain after intermediate agreement, and enlarge after good agreement.
assumptions_latex: Larger \eta means a larger stabilization region.
p_k>0 in ratio-based cases.
Actual and predicted quantities use the same minimization-decrease convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Ratio Region Adaptation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required branch when the predicted-improvement denominator is nonpositive or lacks a reliable positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_k\) denote predicted improvement and let the ratio update use \(q_k=a_k/p_k\) only when \(p_k>0\) is certified. If \(p_k\le0\) or its sign is uncertified, no ratio-based shrink, retain, or enlarge decision is valid. A sound adaptive-region protocol must instead invoke a declared fallback, such as recomputing the prediction, enlarging the region without using \(q_k\), or terminating only after an independent unrestricted optimality certificate has been verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A progress ratio may control the region only with a certified positive denominator; otherwise the method must use a declared fallback or an independent termination certificate.
assumptions_latex: The adaptive update is defined through \(q_k=a_k/p_k\).
The fallback does not infer optimality from \(p_k\le0\) alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k\le0\ \text{or an uncertified sign}\Longrightarrow q_k\text{ is not an admissible basis for the region update}.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard for Undefined Progress Ratios
Adaptive Stabilization Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress-ratio update rule for trust-region or box stabilization sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k(\eta_k)\subseteq Y\) be a stabilization region centered at \(\bar y_k\), with size parameter \(\eta_k>0\). Solve the stabilized master and compute predicted improvement \(p_k>0\) and verified actual improvement \(a_k\), then set \(q_k=a_k/p_k\). For constants \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\) and \(0\le q_-<q_+\), use \(\eta_{k+1}=\gamma_-\eta_k\) when \(q_k<q_-\), \(\eta_{k+1}=\eta_k\) when \(q_-q_k<q_+\), and \(\eta_{k+1}=\gamma_+\eta_k\) when \(q_k\ge q_+\), subject to prescribed size bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrink, retain, or enlarge the stabilization region according to the ratio of verified actual improvement to predicted improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(p_k>0\) and \(q_k=a_k/p_k\) is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{k+1}\) is selected by the displayed three-regime progress-ratio rule.

notation.meaning: stabilization region with size parameter eta

review_flags: No supplied locator identifies a canonical adaptive-region rule for column generation.
The direction of radius adaptation depends on the precise progress convention and needs source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Adaptive Stabilization Regions leaf, but the middle case is malformed as q_-q_k<q_+ and therefore does not define the intended interval, presumably q_- <= q_k < q_+. More importantly, the direction and thresholds of the progress-ratio update depend on the precise definition of predicted and actual improvement. No source is supplied to determine the reliable correction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Adaptation Can Permanently Exclude the Optimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by a maximum stabilization region that excludes every unrestricted optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Y=[0,2], D(y)=y, and S_k\subseteq[0,1] for every k. Then \sup_{S_k}D\le1<2=\sup_YD for all k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the largest permitted region excludes the optimizer, no adaptation rule can recover the unrestricted value.
assumptions_latex: Y=[0,2] and D(y)=y.
S_k\subseteq[0,1] for all k.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Adaptation Can Permanently Exclude the Optimizer

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns adaptive sizing, the corrected progress-ratio update, value-recovery criteria, and region-containment certification. Fixed trust-region geometry, box geometry, and permanent-exclusion failures were excluded to siblings; consequently the Builder's exclusion counterexample was deferred as misplaced. Full-method convergence remains open.

children.title: Overrestriction Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where stabilization regions exclude useful master movement or pricing signals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inactive-Region Test for an Unrestricted Dual Maximizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition distinguishing a harmless local restriction from boundary-induced restricted optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:Y\to\mathbb R\) be concave on a convex set \(Y\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a stabilization region, and let \(y^C\) maximize \(D\) over \(Y\cap C\). If there exists \(r>0\) such that \(Y\cap B(y^C,r)\subseteq C\), then \(y^C\) is a local maximizer of \(D\) over \(Y\), hence a global maximizer over \(Y\). If no such relative neighborhood is contained in \(C\), restricted optimality may instead be caused by the stabilization boundary and is not an unrestricted certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted maximizer is globally valid when the stabilization region is locally inactive relative to the dual domain; a boundary-constrained maximizer need not be.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is convex and \(D\) is concave on \(Y\).
\(y^C\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y\cap C}D(y)\).
For the positive conclusion, \(Y\cap B(y^C,r)\subseteq C\) for some \(r>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\exists r>0:\ Y\cap B(y^C,r)\subseteq C\bigr)\Longrightarrow y^C\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y}D(y)\).

notation.meaning: maximizer over the stabilized dual domain

review_flags: This replaces the Builder's incorrect ambient-gradient-zero claim, which fails when the dual domain is lower-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Region Test for an Unrestricted Dual Maximizer
Overrestriction Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent stabilization regions excluding every unrestricted dual optimum can invalidate termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the concave dual objective \(D(y)=-(y-1)^2\) on \(Y=\mathbb R\), whose unique maximizer is \(y^*=1\). If every stabilization region is \(S_k=[-\Delta,\Delta]\) with fixed \(0<\Delta<1\), then the stabilized maximizer is \(y_k^{S}=\Delta\) for every \(k\), and \(D(y_k^{S})<D(y^*)\). Hence a permanently restricted region that excludes the unrestricted dual solution cannot support a global optimality declaration based solely on its constrained maximizer. A safe scheme must eventually include a relevant dual optimum, let the restriction vanish, or perform an unrestricted certification step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed region excluding all unrestricted dual optima can stall at a constrained maximizer; expansion or unrestricted certification is necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k=[-\Delta,\Delta]\) with \(0<\Delta<1\).
review_flags: The counterexample is self-contained, but its column-generation termination interpretation lacks a supplied source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the Overrestriction Boundary leaf, and the scalar constrained-maximization counterexample is correct. Its conclusion about column-generation termination and the listed sufficient remedies require a direct stabilization reference and a more explicit link between the dual point and pricing certificate.

children.title: Column Selection
children.top_down_role: Policies for admitting generated columns to the restricted master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe nonselection of a column dominated by an interchangeable no-more-expensive column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a minimization master, suppose columns \(g\) and \(h\) have identical master coefficient vectors and costs \(c_g\ge c_h\). If every feasible solution remains feasible after replacing \((\lambda_g,\lambda_h)\) by \((0,\lambda_g+\lambda_h)\), then the replacement does not increase cost. Hence an optimum exists with \(\lambda_g=0\), and \(g\) may be screened while \(h\) remains available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A more expensive duplicate can be screened when all of its weight may feasibly be transferred to the cheaper identical column.
assumptions_latex: \(a_g=a_h\) and \(c_g\ge c_h\).
The transfer \((\lambda_g,\lambda_h)\mapsto(0,\lambda_g+\lambda_h)\) preserves all variable domains and side constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominated Duplicate Screening Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Pool Exhaustion Does Not Certify Global Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of terminating from candidate-pool selection alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the finite candidate pool contain one column with reduced cost \(0\), while the full admissible set also contains an unpooled column with reduced cost \(-1\) at the same dual point. Then the pool has no improving candidate although the full pricing infimum is at most \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exhausted finite candidate pool may miss an improving admissible column and therefore cannot by itself certify termination.
assumptions_latex: The candidate pool is a proper subset of the admissible column set.
Reduced costs are evaluated at one fixed dual point.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Pool Exhaustion Does Not Certify Global Pricing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguard against permanent suppression of persistently improving candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A selective admission policy is pricing-fair when every candidate that remains eligible below the active reduced-cost tolerance is eventually admitted, unless globally valid pricing supersedes the finite candidate pool before termination. Under this condition, rejection by a finite pool cannot itself justify termination or permanently suppress every persistent improving candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistently improving candidates must eventually be admitted, or termination must defer to globally certified pricing.
assumptions_latex: Eligibility and reduced costs use the prices and tolerances specified by the policy.
Termination is not inferred solely from an unexhaustive candidate subset.
knowledge_statements.title: Fair Admission or Exact-Fallback Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-best, threshold, bounded-best-batch, and constrained-diversity admission forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At price y_k let C_k=\{a\in P_k:r(a;y_k)<-\varepsilon_k\}. Single-best selection chooses one minimizer of r over C_k; threshold selection admits all of C_k; bounded-best-batch selection admits the \min\{b_k,|C_k|\} smallest-reduced-cost members under a stated tie rule; diversity-aware selection chooses S_k\subseteq C_k subject to an explicitly stated diversity constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical policies admit one best candidate, every threshold-improving candidate, a bounded best batch, or an improving subset satisfying an explicit diversity constraint.
assumptions_latex: P_k is finite when ranking or admitting all candidates is required.
A deterministic or set-valued tie convention is specified.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Column-Selection Variants
Column Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost filtering and bounded-batch selection from a generated column pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(P_k\) be the available pool, \(y_k\) the pricing dual point, \(r(a;y_k)\) each column's reduced cost, \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), and batch limit \(b_k\ge1\). Form \(C_k=\{a\in P_k:r(a;y_k)<-\varepsilon_k\}\). Select \(S_k\subseteq C_k\) containing the \(\min\{b_k,|C_k|\}\) smallest reduced costs, with deterministic tie breaking, and add \(S_k\) to the restricted master. If \(C_k\) is empty, invoke the exact pricing oracle or its valid certificate rather than concluding global optimality from the finite pool alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter pooled columns by improving reduced cost, add a bounded best batch, and call exact pricing when the pool has none.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\) is finite and every \(r(a;y_k)\) is available.
\(\varepsilon_k\ge0\) and \(b_k\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k\subseteq\{a\in P_k:r(a;y_k)<-\varepsilon_k\}\) contains at most \(b_k\) best-priced columns.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports column-pool selection rules.
The finite-pool versus exact-pricing safeguard requires a column-generation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Column Selection leaf, and the finite-pool filtering rule is coherent. The best-batch convention, deterministic tie handling, and exact-pricing fallback are implementation choices requiring direct algorithmic support, which the supplied inventory lacks.

children.title: Column Deletion
children.top_down_role: Policies for retiring inactive, redundant, or costly columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient certificate preserving the current restricted-master optimum when unused columns are deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a minimization restricted master over column set G attain value v(G) at \lambda^\star. If D\subseteq G and \lambda_g^\star=0 for every g\in D, then deleting D preserves the displayed solution and the current restricted-master value: v(G\setminus D)=v(G). This certificate does not by itself preserve future bounds, finite termination, or global column-generation convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting columns that are zero in a current optimal master solution preserves that restricted-master optimum, but does not certify future convergence.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a minimization problem and attains an optimum \lambda^\star.
Every deleted column has zero coefficient in \lambda^\star.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Coefficient Safe-Deletion Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure example for deletion of a column required by every feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the restricted master \lambda_1=1,\ \lambda_1\ge0, the sole column is required by its unique feasible solution. Deleting that column leaves the inconsistent equality 0=1. Thus arbitrary deletion need not preserve restricted-master feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a column required by every feasible master solution can make the restricted master infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The master contains a single column whose coefficient is constrained to equal one.

notation.meaning: restricted-master feasible set for pool G

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Can Destroy Restricted-Master Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for deleting columns without destroying current restricted-master feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F(G)\) be the feasible set of a restricted master over columns \(G\), and let \(D\subseteq G\). If deletion only fixes the variables indexed by \(D\) to zero, then \(\mathcal F(G\setminus D)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if some \(\lambda\in\mathcal F(G)\) satisfies \(\lambda_g=0\) for every \(g\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion preserves feasibility exactly when the current master has a feasible solution supported on the retained columns.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq G\).
Deletion removes the indexed variables without changing remaining data or constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Feasibility-Preserving Deletion Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional active-pool storage bound after feasible capacity restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every completed deletion step leaves the restricted master feasible and enforces |M_k|\le B, then active-column storage is O(Bd) when each column uses O(d) storage. This does not bound archive storage or guarantee that the cap is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successfully restoring an active-column cap B bounds active storage by O(Bd), but neither bounds archives nor guarantees that feasible deletion exists.
assumptions_latex: B\ge1.
Every completed deletion step preserves restricted-master feasibility.
Each active column uses O(d) storage.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Restoring Deletion Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient safeguard against false termination after repeated deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every iteration ending without an admitted column invokes globally valid pricing over \mathcal A at the certification price y_k; every returned a with r(a;y_k)<-\varepsilon_k remains eligible for readmission even if previously deleted; and termination requires \inf_{a\in\mathcal A}r(a;y_k)\ge-\varepsilon_k. Then deletion cannot itself create a false pricing certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion cannot invalidate termination when deleted columns remain rediscoverable and termination always uses certified full-domain pricing.
assumptions_latex: Full-domain pricing or an equivalent global certificate is available.
Previously deleted columns remain eligible for readmission.
Certification uses the required price and tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Rediscoverability Safeguard for Repeated Deletion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational deletion rule protecting the support of a displayed feasible master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \lambda^k\in\mathcal F(M_k), let S_k=\{g\in M_k:\lambda_g^k\ne0\}, choose D_k\subseteq M_k\setminus S_k, and set M_{k+1}=M_k\setminus D_k. Then the restriction of \lambda^k to M_{k+1} remains feasible. If \lambda^k is optimal and remaining data are unchanged, it remains optimal with the same value. A cap |M_{k+1}|\le B can be attained by such deletion if and only if |S_k|\le B; age, reduced cost, or storage scores may rank only eligible columns outside S_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Protect a feasible solution's support and delete only zero-coefficient columns; optional scores rank the eligible columns.
assumptions_latex: Deletion removes variables without changing remaining master data.
\lambda^k is feasible.
The optimality conclusion additionally assumes \lambda^k is optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_k\subseteq M_k\setminus S_k\Longrightarrow \lambda^k\in\mathcal F(M_k\setminus D_k),\qquad \exists D_k:\ |M_k\setminus D_k|\le B,\ D_k\cap S_k=\varnothing\iff |S_k|\le B.

notation.meaning: support of the protected feasible solution

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Preserving Deletion Step
Column Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Age-and-activity deletion rule preserving columns needed by the current master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each master column \(a\), maintain an inactivity age \(h_k(a)\). After solving iteration \(k\), set \(h_{k+1}(a)=0\) when its master coefficient satisfies \(x_k(a)>\tau_x\) or its reduced cost satisfies \(r(a;y_k)<-\tau_r\); otherwise set \(h_{k+1}(a)=h_k(a)+1\). Given age limit \(H\), delete only columns in \(D_k=\{a:h_{k+1}(a)\ge H,\ x_k(a)\le\tau_x,\ r(a;y_k)\ge-\tau_r\}\), while retaining any protected feasibility column. Store deleted columns in an archive when later reuse is permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only sufficiently old, inactive, nonimproving columns, while protecting columns required for current restricted-master feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(H\ge1\) and \(\tau_x,\tau_r\ge0\).
\(x_k(a)\) and \(r(a;y_k)\) are available for active columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\in D_k\) only if it is old, currently inactive, nonimproving, and not feasibility-protected.
review_flags: The supplied sources do not address column deletion policies.
Threshold and feasibility-protection conventions require direct algorithmic support.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Column Deletion leaf. The age, activity, and reduced-cost thresholds are an unsupported policy, and 'protected feasibility column' is not formally defined. A source is needed to validate the deletion rule and determine which columns must be retained without overstating feasibility preservation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility-Preserving Deletion Can Still Prevent Progress
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed retirement-before-evaluation cycle; canonically owned by the integrated lifecycle leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{-\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\lambda\ge0\}\). Starting with column 1, exact pricing repeatedly identifies column 2, but a policy deletes it before the augmented master is solved, so every solved restricted master retains value \(0\) although the full value is \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The example concerns transition ordering and fair evaluation across admission, solving, and retirement, rather than deletion safety alone.
assumptions_latex: Column 2 is retired after admission and before the augmented-master solve.
Deleted columns remain rediscoverable.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Preserving Deletion Can Still Prevent Progress

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory covers exact feasibility and current-value preservation tests, support-preserving deletion, conditional active-storage bounds, rediscoverability, and arbitrary-deletion failure. The proposed retirement-before-evaluation cycle is deferred because its canonical home is the integrated lifecycle sibling; admission and reuse policies are likewise excluded.

children.title: Column Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of previously generated columns across master states or related solves.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Archive Exhaustion Is Not a Pricing Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between scanning previously generated columns and solving the full pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\subseteq\mathcal A\) be the archived columns and \(\rho(y_k)=\inf_{a\in\mathcal A}r(a;y_k)\). The condition \(r(a;y_k)\ge0\) for all \(a\in A_k\) does not imply \(\rho(y_k)\ge0\). An empty improving-reuse set certifies full pricing only if the archive covers \(\mathcal A\) or another valid certificate covers its complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finding no improving archived column is not a global pricing certificate unless the scan covers the full pricing domain.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\subseteq\mathcal A\).
All reduced costs are evaluated at the same dual point \(y_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Archive Exhaustion Is Not a Pricing Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master monotonicity produced by reactivating archived columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization restricted master with active set \(M\), reactivating \(R\) gives \(M'=M\cup R\). Every solution feasible over \(M\) remains feasible over \(M'\); hence, whenever the optima are defined, \(v(M')\le v(M)\). Reactivation does not alter the full column set or full-master optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reactivation enlarges the restricted master, cannot worsen its minimization value, and does not change the full problem.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a minimization problem.
Reactivation only adds variables with their original data.
knowledge_statements.title: Reactivation Is a Master-Set Expansion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct reduced-cost rescoring cost for an archived column set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an archive A of N columns in \mathbb R^d with r(a;y)=c(a)-\langle y,a\rangle, direct rescoring at one price costs O(\sum_{a\in A}\operatorname{nnz}(a)) arithmetic, or O(Nd) for dense columns. Archive storage is the stored coefficient payload plus O(N) costs and identifiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct archive scan is linear in total stored nonzeros, or O(Nd) for dense columns.
assumptions_latex: Every archived reduced cost is evaluated directly at one fixed price.
Scalar arithmetic has unit cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Archive Rescoring Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition preserving full-pricing termination validity under archive-first reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an inconclusive archive scan always triggers globally valid pricing at the required certification price and termination is permitted only from that global certificate, archive-first reuse cannot weaken the no-improving-column certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archive-first reuse preserves valid termination when inconclusive scans always fall back to globally certified pricing.
assumptions_latex: Archive evidence and fallback certification use the required current pricing point.
An inconclusive archive scan cannot terminate the method.
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Fallback Preservation Principle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized reuse pass with validity filtering, ranking, batching, and certified fallback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At price y_k, let A_k^{\rm val} contain archived columns whose stored data remain valid. Form R_k=\{a\in A_k^{\rm val}:r(a;y_k)<-\varepsilon_k\}. If R_k\ne\varnothing, move to the active master a batch B_k\subseteq R_k of at most b_k columns having smallest reduced costs and resolve the restricted master. If R_k=\varnothing, invoke full-domain certified pricing; an archive scan alone cannot authorize termination. An invalid payload is ineligible until recomputed and revalidated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescore valid archived columns, reactivate a best improving batch, and use certified full pricing when the archive is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: A_k^{\rm val} is finite or has a terminating exact scan.
All reduced costs use the same required price y_k.
b_k\ge1 and \varepsilon_k\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_k\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow 1\le|B_k|\le b_k,\ B_k\subseteq R_k;\qquad R_k=\varnothing\Longrightarrow\text{invoke certified full-domain pricing}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Archive-First Reuse Pass

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound on consecutive successful reuse batches when the counted archive receives no new entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a reuse pass begins with N<\infty valid archived columns, every successful batch removes at least one archived column, and no column enters the archive during the counted pass, then at most N successful batches occur before the archive is empty or a scan invokes full pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without rearchiving, an archive of N columns can support at most N consecutive nonempty reuse batches.
assumptions_latex: |A_0^{\rm val}|=N<\infty.
Each successful batch removes at least one archived column.
No rearchiving occurs during the pass.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Fixed-Archive Delay Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of fixed-archive reuse bounds when archived columns may reenter the archive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An archive of initial size one can support arbitrarily many reuse passes if its sole column is repeatedly reactivated and later returned to the archive. Thus \(N_{\rm reuse}\le |A_0|\) fails once rearchiving is permitted; without a bound on entries, reentries, or consecutive archive-only transitions, neither total reuse passes nor delay between full-pricing calls is bounded by the initial archive size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated rearchiving can replenish the archive indefinitely, so initial archive size does not bound total reuse work or full-pricing delay.
assumptions_latex: Reactivated columns may later be archived again.
No independent reentry or oracle-delay limit is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Rearchiving Destroys Fixed-Archive Delay Bounds
Column Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reactivation of archived columns before invoking a new exact pricing solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) be an archive of previously generated columns not currently in the restricted master. At pricing point \(y_k\), evaluate \(r(a;y_k)\) for eligible \(a\in A_k\), form \(R_k=\{a\in A_k:r(a;y_k)<-\varepsilon_k\}\), and reactivate up to \(b_k\) columns of smallest reduced cost. Remove reactivated columns from the archive and solve the augmented restricted master. If \(R_k=\varnothing\), or if reuse yields no accepted progress, call the original pricing oracle; failure of the archive scan alone does not certify absence of improving columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scan archived columns for negative reduced cost, reactivate the best batch, and use the original oracle when reuse is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) is finite or admits a terminating eligibility scan.
\(\varepsilon_k\ge0\) and \(b_k\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k=\{a\in A_k:r(a;y_k)<-\varepsilon_k\}\) supplies reusable columns but not a global pricing certificate.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports archived-column reuse.
A direct column-generation implementation source is needed for acceptance and fallback rules.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Column Reuse leaf, and archive scanning by reduced cost is mathematically coherent. The eligibility scan, bounded reactivation batch, accepted-progress condition, and fallback to original pricing are source-dependent lifecycle conventions with no supporting locator.

children.title: Column-Pool Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Interactions among admission, retention, retirement, and reactivation policies.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absent Canonical Identity Permits Unbounded Duplicate Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pool-growth failure caused by treating repeated generation of one mathematical column as distinct lifecycle objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a pricing oracle returns the same mathematical column \(a\) at every iteration, but each return receives a fresh identity and is inserted without duplicate detection. After \(k\) iterations the stored pool contains \(k\) copies of \(a\), although its generated cone or convex hull is unchanged from that of one copy. Storage therefore grows as \(\Theta(k)\) without enlarging master geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without canonical identity or duplicate detection, repeated generation of one column causes linear storage growth without new master geometry.
assumptions_latex: The oracle returns the same coefficient-and-cost column at every iteration.
Each return is stored under a distinct identity.
No duplicate aggregation or deletion occurs.
knowledge_statements.title: Absent Canonical Identity Permits Unbounded Duplicate Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive storage accounting under the disjoint state invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each retained payload uses at most s storage units and each canonical identifier uses O(1), then lifecycle storage is at most s(|M_k|+|P_k|+|A_k|)+O(|G_k|). Consequently an active-set cap alone does not bound total memory when P_k, A_k, or G_k can grow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total memory includes active, candidate, and archive payloads plus identifiers; an active-pool cap is not a total-memory bound.
assumptions_latex: Each retained column payload uses at most s storage units.
Canonical identifiers have constant-size storage.

notation.meaning: maximum retained payload storage per column

knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle Storage Accounting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit state model for canonically identified generated columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G_k be the canonically identified columns known at iteration k. A lifecycle state is a disjoint exhaustive decomposition G_k=M_k\dot\cup P_k\dot\cup A_k\dot\cup X_k, where M_k is active, P_k awaits admission, A_k is retained but inactive, and X_k retains only discarded identities. A transition removes a column from its old state before inserting it into one new state; regeneration of an existing canonical column updates that object rather than creating a duplicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every known canonical column occupies exactly one active, candidate, archived, or discarded state, and transitions preserve that partition.
assumptions_latex: Mathematically identical columns have a canonical identity.
Discarded identifiers may remain after coefficient payloads are removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjoint Lifecycle-State Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated transition interface over disjoint canonical lifecycle states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given G_k=M_k\dot\cup P_k\dot\cup A_k\dot\cup X_k, a lifecycle iteration may validate archived payloads, reactivate selected members of A_k, admit selected members of P_k, solve the restricted master, choose the support S_k of a feasible master solution, retire only members of M_k\setminus S_k, and invoke certified full-domain pricing when neither reuse nor admission supplies a column. Each move removes the canonical object from its old state before inserting it into exactly one new state, preserving the disjoint exhaustive invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate validation, reuse, admission, support-protected retirement, and pricing fallback while keeping each canonical column in exactly one state.
assumptions_latex: The initial states are pairwise disjoint and exhaustive over G_k.
Each mathematical column has one canonical identity.
S_k supports a feasible restricted-master solution.
Termination requires certified full-domain pricing.

notation.meaning: protected support of a feasible master solution

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Preserving Lifecycle Transition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage requirement for termination in the presence of known and unknown lifecycle states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal A be the full admissible column set and y_k the certification price. Bounds obtained from lifecycle-state scans authorize termination only when their certified domains jointly cover M_k\cup P_k\cup A_k\cup X_k and \mathcal A\setminus G_k. Equivalently, a full-domain certificate must establish \inf_{a\in\mathcal A}r(a;y_k)\ge-\varepsilon_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination must cover every lifecycle state and all not-yet-known columns, or use an equivalent full-domain certificate.
assumptions_latex: All component bounds use the same certification price and reduced-cost convention.
The certified domains cover \mathcal A.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle-Wide Termination Coverage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling condition excluding retirement-before-evaluation cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lifecycle schedule has fair opportunity if every admitted or reactivated column is retained through at least one exact solve of the augmented restricted master, unless a certified dominance or redundancy test removes it without changing that master's feasible set and optimum. This excludes retirement-before-evaluation cycles but does not by itself imply finite termination for an infinite column universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every admitted or reactivated column survives until one augmented-master solve unless exact redundancy makes its removal harmless.
assumptions_latex: The stated augmented restricted-master solves are exact.
Early removal requires a certified feasible-set-and-optimum preserving test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\text{ admitted or reactivated at }k\Longrightarrow a\text{ is evaluated in an augmented solve or certified redundant}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fair-Opportunity Lifecycle Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Capacity Alone Does Not Ensure Lifecycle Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state cycling under a bounded active pool without fair evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{-\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\lambda\ge0\}\), impose active capacity \(B=1\). A policy may keep column 1 active, repeatedly admit or reactivate improving column 2, retire column 2 before resolving the augmented master, and return to the same state. Capacity is respected and the active master remains feasible, but its solved value stays \(0\) while the full value is \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded active pool can cycle forever when improving columns are retired before receiving an opportunity to affect a master solve.
assumptions_latex: The policy may retire a newly admitted improving column before the augmented master is solved.
No fair-opportunity or repeated-state prohibition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B=1\text{ and a finite column universe do not imply lifecycle convergence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Alone Does Not Ensure Lifecycle Convergence
Column-Pool Lifecycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated state transition for active, pooled, archived, and discarded columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition generated columns at iteration \(k\) into active master set \(M_k\), candidate pool \(P_k\), and archive \(A_k\). First reactivate improving archived columns, then select a bounded improving batch from \(P_k\) and add it to \(M_k\). Solve the restricted master, update each column's activity and age, and move deletion-eligible unprotected columns from \(M_k\) to \(A_k\). Remove duplicates using a canonical column identifier. Invoke exact pricing whenever neither reuse nor pool selection produces accepted progress; terminate only upon its valid no-improving-column certificate, then output the current master solution and retained pool state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycle columns through active, candidate, and archived states, using exact pricing whenever reuse and selection fail to make progress.
assumptions_latex: Each generated column has a canonical identifier.
Restricted-master feasibility columns are protected from deletion.
Exact pricing provides a valid improvement or termination result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M_k,P_k,A_k)\) evolves by reuse, selection, solving, aging, deletion, and exact-pricing transitions.
review_flags: The supplied source inventory contains no column-pool lifecycle reference.
State transitions and exact-pricing fallback need direct algorithmic sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Column-Pool Lifecycle leaf. The statement calls M_k, P_k, and A_k a partition but does not specify the universe or explicitly require pairwise disjointness and complete coverage. Its transition order, accepted-progress rule, deletion protection, duplicate handling, and exact-pricing fallback also require a direct implementation or algorithm source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient global completion test when pricing is divided among finitely many oracle domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\bigcup_{i=1}^qG_i\), let \(\rho_i=\inf_{g\in G_i}r_y(g)\), and let \(L_i\le\rho_i\) be a certified lower bound for every nonempty partition. Then \(\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)=\min_i\rho_i\), and \(L_i\ge-\varepsilon\) for every nonempty partition implies \(\inf_{g\in G}r_y(g)\ge-\varepsilon\). Certification of only a proper subset of the partitions is not sufficient in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioned pricing is globally complete when every relevant partition has a certified lower bound excluding reduced costs below the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(G=\bigcup_{i=1}^qG_i\) with finite \(q\).
Each \(L_i\) is a valid lower bound on \(\inf_{g\in G_i}r_y(g)\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).

notation.meaning: pricing subdomain assigned to oracle i
reduced cost at current master price y
certified lower bound for partition i

review_flags: The Builder's phrase 'exactly when' was removed: lower-bound tests are sufficient but need not be necessary when the bounds are loose.
knowledge_statements.title: Partitioned-Pricing Completion Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case work for one round-fair certification pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each unresolved domain is queried at most once in a round and certified call i costs at most T_i, then a completed no-improvement round makes at most q calls and costs at most \sum_{i=1}^qT_i. Discovery of an improving column may terminate the round earlier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One fair certification round uses at most one certified call per domain and at most the sum of their call-cost bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each unresolved domain is queried at most once in the round.
T_i bounds certified call i.

notation.meaning: worst-case cost of certified oracle i

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Round Oracle Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fairness condition for finitely partitioned certified pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For required domains G_1,\ldots,G_q, a scheduler is round-fair if, unless an improving column is accepted first, every domain unresolved at the start of a round is queried by a certified oracle before the round ends. If each call returns a column below -\varepsilon or certifies its domain lower bound at least -\varepsilon, and the domains cover G, then a completed round returns an improving column or a global partitioned-pricing certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fair round visits every unresolved pricing domain unless improvement is found, yielding either a column or complete certification.
assumptions_latex: q<\infty.
The domains cover the full admissible column set.
Every certified call terminates with an improving column or a valid domain bound.

notation.meaning: pricing domain assigned to oracle i

knowledge_statements.title: Round-Fair Pricing Schedule

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unfair Scheduling Can Miss a Persistent Improving Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of domain fairness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=G_1\cup G_2 with \inf_{g\in G_1}r_y(g)=0 and \inf_{g\in G_2}r_y(g)=-1. A scheduler querying only G_1 forever finds no improving column while permanently postponing G_2, so repeated accurate calls on a proper subset neither discover the improvement nor certify global pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduler can fail forever by repeatedly querying a nonimproving domain and never visiting another domain containing an improving column.
assumptions_latex: G_1 and G_2 are both required to cover G.
The price y is fixed in the example.
knowledge_statements.title: Unfair Scheduling Can Miss a Persistent Improving Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-tier schedule separating inexpensive discovery from authoritative certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each required pricing domain G_i, run a finite-budget sequence of heuristic or inexact discovery calls. Accept a returned column only after verifying r_y(g)<-\varepsilon. If discovery produces no accepted column, invoke a certified oracle for G_i. A certified improving column ends the round; otherwise retain a valid bound L_i\le\inf_{g\in G_i}r_y(g). Unless improvement is accepted, visit every unresolved covering domain and terminate only when every retained bound satisfies L_i\ge-\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try finite-budget discovery first, verify proposed improvements, escalate inconclusive domains, and terminate only after complete certified coverage.
assumptions_latex: The finitely many required domains cover the admissible columns.
Each discovery phase has a finite call budget.
Each certified oracle returns an improving column or a valid domain lower bound.
All calls use the required certification price.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for domain i

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic-First Certified Escalation Schedule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-round work bound with finite discovery budgets and one certified fallback per domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If domain i receives at most h_i heuristic calls costing at most H_i each and at most one certified call costing at most T_i, then a completed no-improvement round makes at most \sum_i(h_i+1) calls and costs at most \sum_i(h_iH_i+T_i).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite heuristic budgets plus one certified fallback per domain give an additive per-round work bound.
assumptions_latex: h_i<\infty for every domain.
H_i and T_i are valid per-call cost bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Escalation-Round Work Bound
Pricing-Oracle Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling rule for exact and inexact pricing oracles in stabilized conic column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a restricted master dual point \(z_k\), an ordered family of pricing oracles \(\mathcal O_1,\ldots,\mathcal O_m\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), and oracle lower bounds \(L_{k,j}\) on the minimum reduced cost, query inexpensive oracles first. Accept any returned column \(a\) satisfying \(\bar c(a;z_k)<-\varepsilon_k\), insert it into the master, and begin the next master iteration. If oracle \(\mathcal O_j\) returns no such column but \(L_{k,j}< -\varepsilon_k\), escalate to \(\mathcal O_{j+1}\). Terminate pricing only when a certified oracle establishes \(L_{k,j}\ge-\varepsilon_k\); output the current restricted-master solution as \(\varepsilon_k\)-pricing-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Query cheaper pricing oracles first, accept a sufficiently negative reduced-cost column, escalate inconclusive calls, and stop only after a certified lower bound excludes improving columns.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_k>0\) and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\).
Each reported \(L_{k,j}\) is a valid lower bound on global minimum reduced cost.
At least one scheduled oracle can provide a global pricing certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{k,j}\ge-\varepsilon_k\) certifies the absence of columns with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon_k\).

notation.meaning: reduced cost of column a at the current dual point
certified pricing lower bound from oracle j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is internally coherent and fits the scheduling leaf, but no citation supports this particular escalation and termination policy or its epsilon-pricing-optimal label.

children.title: Conic Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Projection and outer-approximation methods organized around complicating variables and conic subproblem dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Recourse-Value Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued region of a right-hand-side-parametric conic recourse function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone and define \(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\) and \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:y\in F(x)\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). The finite recourse-value region is
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{x\in X:-\infty<Q(x)<+\infty\}.
\]
Equivalently, it consists of parameters for which the recourse system is feasible and its linear objective is bounded below. Membership does not assert that the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite-value region contains precisely the first-stage parameters having feasible recourse and a finite lower-bounded recourse objective, whether or not an optimizer exists.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone, and all data are finite-dimensional.
\(Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:y\in C,\ Wy=h-Tx\}\) with the extended-real convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Recourse Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter region where the conic recourse fiber is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\) and \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:y\in F(x)\}\), using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), the infeasible recourse region is
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{inf}}:=\{x\in X:F(x)=\varnothing\}=\{x\in X:Q(x)=+\infty\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{inf}}\) exactly when \(h-Tx\notin W(C)\). This region is independent of the recourse objective vector \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse is infeasible exactly when its right-hand side is outside the conic image of the recourse map; the extended value is then positive infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a convex cone and \(W:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
The empty-infimum convention is \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: linear image of the recourse cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry of the Infeasible Parameter Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity of the feasible-recourse parameter set and failure of convexity for its infeasible complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}:=\{x\in X:h-Tx\in W(C)\}\), where \(X\) and \(C\) are convex and \(W,T\) are linear. Then \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}\) is convex, whereas \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{inf}}=X\setminus\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}\) need not be convex. For \(X=\mathbb R^2\), \(C=\mathbb R_+^2\), \(W=I\), \(h=0\), and \(T=-I\), one has \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}=\mathbb R_+^2\); the infeasible points \((-1,1)\) and \((1,-1)\) have the feasible midpoint \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected recourse feasibility is convex under convex data, but its infeasible complement need not be convex.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(C\) are convex.
\(W\) and \(T\) are linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}\text{ is convex, while }\mathcal R_{\mathrm{inf}}\text{ need not be convex}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry of the Infeasible Parameter Region

children.title: Recourse Recession Geometry
children.top_down_role: Recession directions and recession cones of parameterized recourse systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Recession Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession cone of each feasible fiber in fixed-recourse conic Benders form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\), where \(C\) is a closed convex cone. Whenever \(F(x)\ne\varnothing\), its recession cone is
\[
\operatorname{rec}F(x)=\{d\in C:Wd=0\}=C\cap\ker W.
\]
Thus the feasible fibers share a parameter-independent recession cone. Moreover, if \(y\in F(x)\) and \(d\in C\cap\ker W\), then \(y+td\in F(x)\) for every \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty fixed-recourse fiber has recession cone equal to the recourse cone intersected with the nullspace of the recourse map.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
\(F(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(F(x)=C\cap\{y:Wy=h-Tx\}\).

notation.meaning: recession cone of the feasible recourse fiber

children.title: Unbounded-Recourse Regions
children.top_down_role: Master-parameter regions associated with unbounded recourse behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Recourse Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Region where feasible conic recourse has value minus infinity, with the recession-direction implication stated without an invalid converse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the extended-real recourse value \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:y\in C,\ Wy=h-Tx\}\), define the unbounded-recourse region by
\[
\mathcal R_{-\infty}:=\{x\in X:Q(x)=-\infty\}.
\]
Let \(D=C\cap\ker W\). If there exists \(d\in D\) with \(q^\top d<0\), then every parameter \(x\in X\) with \(F(x)\ne\varnothing\) belongs to \(\mathcal R_{-\infty}\). For a general nonpolyhedral cone, the absence of such a direction alone does not establish that \(\mathcal R_{-\infty}\) is empty; an additional recession-completeness condition, such as polyhedrality of the feasible fibers, is needed for that converse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unbounded-recourse region contains the parameters whose recourse value is minus infinity. A common negative-cost recession direction makes every feasible fiber unbounded below, but the converse can fail for general nonpolyhedral conic fibers.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone and \(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\).
The recourse objective is the fixed linear functional \(q^\top y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists d\in C\cap\ker W\) with \(q^\top d<0\Longrightarrow\{x\in X:F(x)\ne\varnothing\}\subseteq\mathcal R_{-\infty}\).

children.title: Recession-Induced Unboundedness
children.top_down_role: Connections between recourse recession directions and unbounded recourse values.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Induced Unboundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A negative-cost recession direction certifies unbounded recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\) and suppose \(y_0\in F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\). A vector \(d\) satisfying
\[
d\in C,\qquad Wd=0,\qquad q^\top d<0
\]
is an unboundedness certificate. Indeed, \(y_0+td\in F(x)\) for every \(t\ge0\), while \(q^\top(y_0+td)=q^\top y_0+tq^\top d\to-\infty\). Consequently \(Q(x)=-\infty\). The certificate is directly verifiable using conic membership, a linear equality, and a strict scalar inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point together with a negative-cost recession direction certifies that the recourse objective decreases without bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a convex cone and the recourse objective is linear.

children.top_down_role: Transitions between finite recourse-value regions and unbounded-recourse regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-to-Unbounded Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of an internal finite-to-unbounded boundary for polyhedral fixed recourse, where recession directions completely characterize unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the fixed-recourse model \(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\) with objective \(q^\top y\), and assume that \(C\) is polyhedral. Its common recession cone is \(D=C\cap\ker W\). If \(q^\top d\ge0\) for every \(d\in D\), every nonempty fiber is bounded below. If some \(d\in D\) satisfies \(q^\top d<0\), every nonempty fiber has value \(-\infty\). Consequently, relative to the feasible parameter region \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}:=\{x\in X:F(x)\ne\varnothing\}\), the unbounded-recourse region is either empty or all of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}\), so it has no relative finite-to-unbounded boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For polyhedral fixed recourse, the common recession cone completely determines boundedness: either all feasible fibers are bounded below or all are unbounded below, so no finite-to-unbounded boundary occurs within the feasible parameter region.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedral convex cone.
\(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\) with fixed \(C\), \(W\), and \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_{-\infty}\in\{\varnothing,\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}\}\), and hence \(\operatorname{bd}_{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{feas}}}(\mathcal R_{-\infty})=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: common recession cone equal to the intersection of C with the nullspace of W

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A rotated-second-order-cone fixed-recourse family with a relative boundary between finite and unbounded recourse values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C=\{(u,v,s)\in\mathbb R^3:2vs\ge u^2,\ v\ge0,\ s\ge0\}, F(x)=\{(u,v,s)\in C:s=x\}, and Q(x)=\inf\{u:(u,v,s)\in F(x)\} for x\ge0. Then Q(0)=0, whereas Q(x)=-\infty for every x>0; for the latter regime, (-t,t^2/(2x),x)\in F(x) for all t\ge0. Thus \mathcal R_{\mathrm{fin}}=\{0\}, \mathcal R_{-\infty}=(0,\infty), and 0 lies on their relative boundary in [0,\infty).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rotated-cone recourse can be finite at zero and unbounded below at every positive parameter, unlike the polyhedral all-or-nothing regime.
assumptions_latex: C is the three-dimensional rotated second-order cone.
The parameter fixes s=x\ge0 and the objective minimizes u.

children.title: Recourse Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Recourse values or bounds lacking attaining subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a finite recourse infimum to have a feasible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\) and \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\in F(x)}q^\top y\), recourse is nonattained at \(x\) when
\[
-\infty<Q(x)<+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
\{y\in F(x):q^\top y=Q(x)\}=\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, there exists a minimizing sequence \((y_k)\subset F(x)\) with \(q^\top y_k\to Q(x)\), but no feasible point realizes the limiting objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse is nonattained when its value is finite and approachable by feasible solutions but no feasible solution realizes that value.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
The extended recourse value \(Q(x)\) is finite.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed semidefinite recourse fiber with a finite but unattained linear infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[F=\left\{(a,c)\in\mathbb R^2:\begin{pmatrix}a&1\\1&c\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\] Then \[\inf_{(a,c)\in F}a=0,\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{(a,c)\in F}a=\varnothing,\] while \((1/k,k)\in F\) and \(1/k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed two-by-two semidefinite recourse fiber can have finite value zero approached by feasible points but no minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The feasible cone is \(\mathbb S_+^2\).
The off-diagonal entry is fixed at one.
The objective minimizes the upper-left entry.

children.title: Nonclosed Recourse Images
children.top_down_role: Projected recourse sets or value epigraphs that fail to be closed.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Recourse Images
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonclosedness property of the linear image encoding feasible right-hand sides and objective upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the augmented recourse image
\[
\mathcal E:=\{(Wy,q^\top y+s):y\in C,\ s\in\mathbb R_+\}\subseteq\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R.
\]
The image is nonclosed when \(\mathcal E\ne\operatorname{cl}\mathcal E\). For any parameter \(x\), the recourse epigraph satisfies
\[
\{(x,\eta):\exists y\in C,\ Wy=h-Tx,\ q^\top y\le\eta\}
=
\{(x,\eta):(h-Tx,\eta)\in\mathcal E\}.
\]
Thus a point of \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal E\setminus\mathcal E\) is a limiting right-hand-side/value pair that is not represented by an actual recourse decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented conic image records attainable right-hand sides and objective upper bounds. Nonclosedness produces limiting pairs that have no representing recourse decision.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
\(W:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(q\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E\ne\operatorname{cl}\mathcal E\) if and only if \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal E\setminus\mathcal E\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: topological closure of the augmented image

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural regime excluding nonclosed augmented recourse images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C\) is a finite-dimensional polyhedral cone, then \(C\times\mathbb R_+\) is polyhedral and its linear image \[\mathcal E=\{(Wy,q^\top y+s):y\in C,\ s\ge0\}\] is polyhedral and closed. Hence the nonclosed augmented-image pathology cannot occur under polyhedral fixed recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral fixed recourse has a closed augmented image, so this pathology requires nonpolyhedral geometry or departure from the stated closed finite-dimensional model.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite-dimensional polyhedral cone.
\(W\) is linear and \(q\) is finite-dimensional.

children.title: Closure-Induced Recourse Gaps
children.top_down_role: Gaps between attainable recourse outcomes and their limiting closures.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Induced Recourse Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap between attainable recourse epigraph points and their closure relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(b(x)=h-Tx\) and let \(\mathcal E\) be the augmented recourse image. Define the closure-relaxed value
\[
\bar Q(x):=\inf\{\eta:(b(x),\eta)\in\operatorname{cl}\mathcal E\}.
\]
Since \(\mathcal E\subseteq\operatorname{cl}\mathcal E\), one has \(\bar Q(x)\le Q(x)\). A closure-induced recourse gap occurs when \(\bar Q(x)<Q(x)\), including the extended-real case \(\bar Q(x)<+\infty=Q(x)\). If \(\mathcal E\) is closed, then \(\bar Q(x)=Q(x)\) for every \(x\); hence nonclosedness is necessary for such a strict gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the attainable recourse image by its closure can lower the value or create artificial feasibility; no such gap occurs when the image is closed.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E=\{(Wy,q^\top y+s):y\in C,\ s\ge0\}\).
Infima use extended-real conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar Q(x)\le Q(x)\), and \(\bar Q(x)<Q(x)\) is possible only if \(\mathcal E\) is nonclosed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-by-two semidefinite recourse image whose closure admits an unattainable limiting right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\mathbb S_+^2\), write \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}\), let \(W(Y)=(a,b)\), and use the zero recourse objective. Then \[W(C)=\{(a,b):a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\},\qquad (0,1)\in\operatorname{cl}W(C)\setminus W(C),\] with \(W(Y_k)=(1/k,1)\to(0,1)\) for \(Y_k=\begin{pmatrix}1/k&1\\1&k\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). At right-hand side \((0,1)\), actual recourse has value \(+\infty\), while the closure-relaxed zero-objective problem has value \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a nonclosed semidefinite recourse image can turn an infeasible right-hand side into an artificially feasible zero-cost one.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\mathbb S_+^2\).
The recourse objective is identically zero.
The relaxation replaces \(W(C)\) by \(\operatorname{cl}W(C)\).

children.title: Attained-Recourse Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where recourse attainment or image closedness is restored.

knowledge_statements.title: Attained-Recourse Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness or level-boundedness conditions restoring attainment of finite recourse values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\) with finite recourse value and choose \(\alpha>Q(x)\). If the lower level set
\[
L_\alpha(x):=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx,\ q^\top y\le\alpha\}
\]
is nonempty and compact, then the recourse infimum is attained. More generally in finite dimensions, it suffices that \(F(x)\) be closed and the objective be level-bounded on \(F(x)\). For the conic fiber, the recession condition
\[
q^\top d>0\quad\text{for every }d\in(C\cap\ker W)\setminus\{0\}
\]
ensures bounded lower level sets and therefore attainment whenever \(F(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(Q(x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite recourse is attained when an appropriate lower level set is compact; strict positivity on every nonzero recession direction supplies a useful sufficient condition.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is closed and all spaces are finite-dimensional.
\(F(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(Q(x)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compactness of some nonempty \(L_\alpha(x)\), or the stated strict recession inequality, implies \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in F(x)}q^\top y\ne\varnothing\).
