knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral fixed recourse as a structural regime excluding finite primal nonattainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a polyhedral cone and fix \(x\) such that \(F(x)=\{y\in C:Wy=h-Tx\}\ne\varnothing\). If \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:y\in F(x)\}>-\infty\), then there exists \(y^*\in F(x)\) satisfying \(q^\top y^*=Q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible polyhedral recourse problem with a finite lower value has an optimal recourse solution.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite-dimensional polyhedral cone.
\(F(x)\ne\varnothing\).
\(Q(x)>-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Finite-Value Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Extreme-Cut Termination in the Polyhedral Case
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exactness bound when recourse is the maximum of finitely many affine dual functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[Q(x)=\max_{u\in E}\ell_u(x)\qquad(x\in X),\] where \(E\) is finite. Consider exact separation that, whenever \(L_k(x^k)<Q(x^k)\), adds an unretained maximizer \(u^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in E}\ell_u(x^k)\). After at most \(|E|\) distinct additions, every function indexed by \(E\) is retained if needed and the resulting master represents \(\operatorname{epi}Q\) exactly over \(X\). Closedness of an infinite nonpolyhedral dual set alone gives no analogous finite bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When recourse is the maximum of finitely many dual affine functions, exact separation needs at most one distinct cut per function.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite and \(Q(x)=\max_{u\in E}\ell_u(x)\) on \(X\).
Every inexact evaluated point is separated by an unretained maximizing function.
Repeated cuts are not counted as additions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(|E|\) distinct optimality-cut additions suffice for exact representation over \(X\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of relevant dual multipliers
New maximizing multiplier returned by exact separation

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Extreme-Cut Termination in the Polyhedral Case

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite affine-cut exactness for smooth conic-representable recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]\), let \[Q(x)=x^2=\sup_{u\in\mathbb R}\{2ux-u^2\}.\] For every finite \(U_0\subset\mathbb R\), \[L_{U_0}(x)=\max_{u\in U_0}(2ux-u^2)\] is piecewise affine and therefore cannot equal the strictly convex quadratic \(Q\) throughout \([-1,1]\). Thus no finite family of these valid dual cuts globally represents \(\operatorname{epi}Q\) on the interval, although enlarging \(U_0\) tightens the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic recourse epigraph is curved, so no finite family of its affine dual cuts is globally exact on an interval.
assumptions_latex: \(U_0\subset\mathbb R\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Curved-Epigraph Finite-Cut Failure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Refinement and Pointwise Exactness Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of adding valid cuts and the local test for exact recourse representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(D_k\subseteq D_{k+1}\subseteq D\), then \[L_k(x)\le L_{k+1}(x)\le Q(x)\qquad(x\in X).\] Hence the relaxed epigraphs are nested in the reverse direction, \[\operatorname{epi}Q\subseteq\operatorname{epi}L_{k+1}\subseteq\operatorname{epi}L_k,\] and the corresponding minimization lower bounds are nondecreasing. At a point \(\bar x\) with finite \(Q(\bar x)\), the retained optimality cuts are exact precisely when \(L_k(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid cuts monotonically tightens the master; sampled-point exactness occurs exactly when the retained cut envelope equals recourse there.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\subseteq D_{k+1}\subseteq D\).
Every retained function is a valid lower bound for \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le L_{k+1}\le Q\), with exactness at \(\bar x\) equivalent to \(L_k(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Refinement and Pointwise Exactness Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite affine-cut relaxation of a conic recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the first-stage domain, let \(Q:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and let \(D\) be a set of dual-feasible certificates inducing affine functions \(\ell_u(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). For a finite set \(D_k\subseteq D\), define \[L_k(x)=\max_{u\in D_k}\ell_u(x).\] The outer-approximation master replaces \(\theta\ge Q(x)\) by \[\theta\ge\ell_u(x)\qquad(u\in D_k).\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{epi}Q\subseteq\operatorname{epi}L_k,\] and minimizing \(c^\top x+\theta\) over the relaxed master gives a lower bound on the corresponding exact master. If \(Q(x)=\sup_{u\in D}\ell_u(x)\), the full family represents \(\operatorname{epi}Q\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer-approximation master replaces the recourse epigraph by finitely many valid affine dual cuts, producing a relaxation and a minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\subseteq D\) is finite.
Every \(u\in D\) induces an affine lower bound \(\ell_u(x)\le Q(x)\) on \(X\).
Exactness of the full family requires \(Q(x)=\sup_{u\in D}\ell_u(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}Q\subseteq\operatorname{epi}L_k\), so the finite-cut master is a valid lower relaxation.

notation.meaning: Dual-certificate set inducing valid affine lower bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Cut Outer-Approximation Master
Outer-Approximation Master Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite dual-cut relaxation of a conic Benders recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose conic recourse has the dual representation
\[
Q(x)=\sup_{u\in U}(h-Tx)^\top u,
\qquad
U:=\{u\in K^*:W^\top u\preceq_{C^*}q\},
\]
with strong duality at the parameters considered. For a finite set \(U_k\subseteq U\), the outer-approximation master is
\[
\min_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R} c^\top x+\theta
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\theta\ge(h-Tx)^\top u\quad(u\in U_k).
\]
Its feasible set contains the true epigraph of \(Q\), and its optimum is a lower bound on the full two-stage minimization value. Adding a violated dual optimizer or ray refines the approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master replaces the conic recourse epigraph by finitely many valid dual cuts, yielding a lower bound that is tightened by newly generated multipliers or rays.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) and \(C\) are closed convex cones and \(U_k\subseteq U\).
Strong conic duality gives \(Q(x)=\sup_{u\in U}(h-Tx)^\top u\) on the relevant domain.
The first-stage feasible set is \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}Q\subseteq\{(x,\theta):\theta\ge(h-Tx)^\top u\ \forall u\in U_k\}\), so the master optimum is a valid lower bound.

notation.meaning: finite set of multipliers currently represented by cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-cut master idea fits the leaf, but the displayed dual introduces an undefined cone K and restricts the equality multiplier to K* without specifying a primal conic constraint that justifies this domain. The role of added rays is also unclear. An authoritative conic Benders source and a fully specified primal-dual pair are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-size growth when at most one aggregate optimality cut is retained per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If at most one aggregated optimality inequality is added and retained per iteration, then after \(t\) iterations the recourse approximation contains one scalar epigraph variable \(\theta\) and at most \(t\) aggregated optimality rows, independently of the number \(m\) of scenario blocks. Thus its incremental recourse-row count is \(O(t)\); retaining one row per scenario per iteration can require \(O(mt)\) rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-cut master uses one aggregate epigraph variable and grows by at most one aggregate optimality row per iteration.
assumptions_latex: At most one aggregated optimality cut is retained from each iteration.
Feasibility cuts and unrelated master constraints are excluded from the count.

notation.meaning: number of scenario or recourse blocks

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut Master Size Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-scenario witness that a single aggregate envelope can be strictly weaker than separate envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed \(x\), take \(p_1=p_2=1/2\) and synchronized cut values \[(\ell_1^1,\ell_2^1)=(1,0),\qquad(\ell_1^2,\ell_2^2)=(0,1).\] Then \[L_{\mathrm{single}}(x)=\max\{1/2,1/2\}=1/2,\qquad L_{\mathrm{multi}}(x)=\tfrac12\max\{1,0\}+\tfrac12\max\{0,1\}=1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different scenarios can have different best cuts, making synchronized aggregation strictly weaker.
assumptions_latex: \text{The displayed values arise from valid scenario lower cuts at the fixed point}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Loss from Synchronized Aggregation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison between synchronized aggregation and independently selectable scenario cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_i\ge0\) and let \(\ell_i^k(x)\) be scenario lower cuts indexed by a common finite set \(\mathcal I\). Define \[L_{\mathrm{single}}(x)=\max_{k\in\mathcal I}\sum_i p_i\ell_i^k(x),\qquad L_{\mathrm{multi}}(x)=\sum_i p_i\max_{k\in\mathcal I}\ell_i^k(x).\] Then \(L_{\mathrm{single}}(x)\le L_{\mathrm{multi}}(x)\). Equality holds whenever one common index maximizes every positive-weight scenario term; strict inequality can occur when maximizing indices differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronized aggregate envelope is no stronger than allowing every scenario to select its best retained cut independently.
assumptions_latex: p_i\ge0.
\mathcal I\text{ is the same finite synchronized component-cut family in both envelopes}.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Envelope Versus Scenario-Wise Envelope

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient componentwise exactness condition for a nonnegative weighted aggregate cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_i\ge0\), let \(\ell_i(x)\le Q_i(x)\), and define \(Q(x)=\sum_i p_iQ_i(x)\) and \(\ell(x)=\sum_i p_i\ell_i(x)\). At a point \(\bar x\) where all positive-weight terms are finite, \[Q(\bar x)-\ell(\bar x)=\sum_i p_i\bigl(Q_i(\bar x)-\ell_i(\bar x)\bigr)\ge0.\] Therefore the aggregate cut is exact at \(\bar x\) if and only if every positive-weight component cut is exact there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted aggregate cut is exact exactly when every positive-weight scenario cut is exact at the same point.
assumptions_latex: p_i\ge0.
\ell_i(x)\le Q_i(x).
Q_i(\bar x)\text{ and }\ell_i(\bar x)\text{ are finite for every }i\text{ with }p_i>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\iff \ell_i(\bar x)=Q_i(\bar x)\ \text{for every }i\text{ with }p_i>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness of an Aggregated Cut

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Master-Only Form of Scenario Feasibility Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of aggregate recourse epigraph rows from feasibility restrictions in a single-cut master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let scenario \(i\) have feasible-recourse domain \(D_i\subseteq X\), and suppose \(D_i\subseteq\{x:a_i^\top x\le\beta_i\}\). In a single-cut master, \(a_i^\top x\le\beta_i\) is imposed directly on \(x\) and contains no aggregate epigraph variable \(\theta\). Only affine lower bounds on finite aggregate recourse enter rows of the form \(\theta\ge\ell(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario infeasibility produces a direct restriction on the master decision, not an aggregate recourse-value row involving the single epigraph variable.
assumptions_latex: D_i\subseteq\{x:a_i^\top x\le\beta_i\}.
\theta\text{ represents finite aggregate recourse value}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i^\top x\le\beta_i\text{ is a master-only feasibility row, whereas }\theta\ge\ell(x)\text{ is an optimality row}.

notation.meaning: master points having feasible recourse in scenario i

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Only Form of Scenario Feasibility Cuts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-complete aggregate master with explicit optimality and feasibility row families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{q_i}\) be a closed convex cone, \(A_i:\mathbb R^{q_i}\to\mathbb R^{r_i}\), \(B_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{r_i}\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}\), \(d_i\in\mathbb R^{q_i}\), and \(Q_i(x)=\inf\{d_i^\top y:A_i y=b_i-B_i x,\ y\in K_i\}\). Let \(p_i\ge0\). For synchronized tuples \((u_i^k)_i\) satisfying \(d_i-A_i^\top u_i^k\in K_i^*\), the single-cut master is \[\min_{x\in X,\theta\in\mathbb R}c^\top x+\theta\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\theta\ge\sum_i p_i(b_i-B_i x)^\top u_i^k\quad(k\in\mathcal I),\] together with retained feasibility rows \((b_i-B_i x)^\top w_i^s\ge0\), where \(A_i^\top w_i^s\in K_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One scalar represents aggregate recourse; synchronized dual bounds form aggregate optimality rows and conic separators form master-only feasibility rows.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\) is closed and convex.
All retained multipliers satisfy the displayed dual-cone conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i p_i(b_i-B_i x)^\top u_i^k\le\sum_i p_iQ_i(x),\qquad x\in\operatorname{dom}Q_i\Longrightarrow(b_i-B_i x)^\top w_i^s\ge0.

notation.meaning: scenario component of synchronized optimality cut k

knowledge_statements.title: Typed Single-Cut Conic Master
Single-Cut Master Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregated epigraph model for finitely many separable conic recourse functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(p_i\geq0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1\), and define \(Q_i(x)=\inf\{d_i^\top y:A_i y=b_i-B_i x,\ y\in K_i\}\). Given dual-feasible points \(u_i^k\) satisfying \(d_i-A_i^\top u_i^k\in K_i^*\), the single-cut master is
\[\min_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R}\ c^\top x+\theta\quad\text{subject to}\quad \theta\geq\sum_{i=1}^m p_i(b_i-B_i x)^\top u_i^k\quad(k\in\mathcal I).\]
Each inequality is a valid lower bound on \(\sum_i p_iQ_i(x)\); one scalar \(\theta\) represents the aggregate recourse value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single epigraph variable represents total recourse, and each iteration adds one probability-weighted aggregation of scenario dual bounds.

\(u_i^k\) is dual feasible for scenario \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampled-point exactness test for a multi-cut recourse approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_i(x)=\max_{k\in I_i}\ell_{ik}(x)\le Q_i(x)\), let \(p_i\ge0\), and suppose \(Q_i(\bar x)\) is finite. Then \[\sum_i p_iQ_i(\bar x)-\sum_i p_iL_i(\bar x)=\sum_i p_i\bigl(Q_i(\bar x)-L_i(\bar x)\bigr)\ge0.\] The weighted approximation is exact at \(\bar x\) if and only if \(L_i(\bar x)=Q_i(\bar x)\) for every scenario with \(p_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregate multi-cut gap is the weighted sum of scenario gaps and vanishes exactly when every positive-weight scenario approximation is exact.
assumptions_latex: \(L_i(x)\le Q_i(x)\) for every scenario.
\(p_i\ge0\) and \(Q_i(\bar x)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weighted exactness at \(\bar x\) is equivalent to scenario exactness for every \(i\) with \(p_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multi-Cut Dominance under Common Component Cut Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise comparison between scenario-disaggregated and synchronized aggregated approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_i\ge0\) and let \(\ell_{ik}\le Q_i\) for \(k\in I_i\). Define \[M(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\max_{k\in I_i}\ell_{ik}(x).\] For any \(T\subseteq\prod_i I_i\), define \[A_T(x)=\max_{t\in T}\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\ell_{i,t_i}(x).\] Then \[A_T(x)\le M(x)\le\sum_{i=1}^m p_iQ_i(x)\] for every \(x\). Thus independent scenario-wise selection is at least as strong as any synchronized aggregation formed from the same component cut pools.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting the strongest retained cut independently in every scenario dominates any synchronized aggregation made from the same scenario cut pools.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i\ge0\) for all \(i\).
\(\ell_{ik}(x)\le Q_i(x)\) on the master domain.
\(T\subseteq\prod_i I_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_T(x)\le M(x)\le\sum_i p_iQ_i(x)\) for every master point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Cut Dominance under Common Component Cut Pools

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario conic Benders master with a separate epigraph approximation for each separable recourse term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(Y_i,Z_i\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K_i\subseteq Y_i\) be a closed convex cone, and define \[Q_i(x)=\inf\{\langle d_i,y_i\rangle:A_i y_i=b_i-B_i x,\ y_i\in K_i\}.\] Let \[D_i=\{u_i\in Z_i:A_i^*u_i+s_i=d_i\text{ for some }s_i\in K_i^*\},\qquad \ell_{i,u_i}(x)=\langle b_i-B_i x,u_i\rangle.\] Given nonnegative weights \(p_i\) and finite cut sets \(U_i^k\subseteq D_i\), the multi-cut master uses variables \(\theta_i\) and constraints \[\theta_i\ge \ell_{i,u}(x)\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m,\ u\in U_i^k),\] with objective contribution \(\sum_i p_i\theta_i\). Each constraint is valid by weak duality, so the master is a relaxation of the weighted recourse epigraph. If \(Q_i(x)=\sup_{u\in D_i}\ell_{i,u}(x)\) on the master domain, retaining all relevant multipliers gives an exact representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-cut master maintains a separate epigraph variable and separate dual-cut pool for each scenario before weighting and summing the scenario approximations.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_i,Z_i\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces and \(K_i\subseteq Y_i\) is a closed convex cone for every \(i\).
\(p_i\ge0\) and \(U_i^k\subseteq D_i\) are finite.
Exact full representation additionally requires \(Q_i(x)=\sup_{u\in D_i}\ell_{i,u}(x)\) on the stated master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite multi-cut master is a valid lower relaxation of \(\sum_i p_iQ_i(x)\), and the full scenario-wise dual families represent it exactly under value equality.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Disaggregated Multi-Cut Master
Multi-Cut Master Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-disaggregated epigraph model for finitely many separable conic recourse functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q_i(x)=\inf\{d_i^\top y:A_i y=b_i-B_i x,\ y\in K_i\}\) and weights \(p_i\geq0\), introduce one variable \(\theta_i\) per scenario. Given dual-feasible points \(u_i^k\) with \(d_i-A_i^\top u_i^k\in K_i^*\), the multi-cut master is
\[\min_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R^m}c^\top x+\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\theta_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad \theta_i\geq(b_i-B_i x)^\top u_i^k\quad(i=1,\ldots,m;\ k\in\mathcal I_i).\]
Thus each scenario epigraph is approximated independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separate epigraph variable and separate accumulated dual cuts model each scenario’s recourse value before weighted summation.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\) is a closed convex cone for every \(i\).
\(u_i^k\) is dual feasible for scenario \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_i\geq(b_i-B_i x)^\top u_i^k\) is a valid scenario-wise epigraph cut.

If \(\mathcal P'\) refines \(\mathcal P\), then \[L_{\mathcal P}(x)\le L_{\mathcal P'}(x)\le\sum_{i=1}^m p_iQ_i(x).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) contain \(q\) nonempty scenario groups. A partially disaggregated master has one recourse epigraph variable \(\theta_G\) per group. If at most one group optimality row is added and retained for every group in each of \(t\) iterations, then the recourse approximation contains \(q\) epigraph variables and at most \(qt\) retained group rows. Its incremental row count is therefore \(O(qt)\), interpolating between \(O(t)\) for one group and \(O(mt)\) for \(m\) singleton groups.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-complete groupwise master with independent optimality rows and master-only feasibility rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). For scenario \(i\), let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{q_i}\) be a closed convex cone, \(A_i:\mathbb R^{q_i}\to\mathbb R^{r_i}\), \(B_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{r_i}\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}\), \(d_i\in\mathbb R^{q_i}\), and \(Q_i(x)=\inf\{d_i^\top y:A_i y=b_i-B_i x,\ y\in K_i\}\). Let \(p_i\ge0\) and let \(\mathcal P\) partition the scenarios. For each \(G\in\mathcal P\), retain tuples \((u_i^{G,r})_{i\in G}\) satisfying \(d_i-A_i^\top u_i^{G,r}\in K_i^*\). The master is \[\min_{x\in X,\theta}\ c^\top x+\sum_{G\in\mathcal P}\theta_G\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\theta_G\ge\sum_{i\in G}p_i(b_i-B_i x)^\top u_i^{G,r}\quad(r\in\mathcal I_G),\] together with retained feasibility rows \((b_i-B_i x)^\top w_i^s\ge0\), where \(A_i^\top w_i^s\in K_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scenario group has one epigraph variable and an independent optimality-cut stream; infeasibility certificates constrain only the master decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Optimality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality cuts for a fixed-cone, right-hand-side-parametric conic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(Q(x)=\inf\{d^\top y:Ay=b-Bx,\ y\in K\}\), where \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is a closed convex cone. If \(u\) satisfies \(d-A^\top u\in K^*\), then conic weak duality gives
\[Q(x)\geq(b-Bx)^\top u\qquad(x\in X).\]
Consequently, every \((x,\theta)\) satisfying \(x\in X\) and \(\theta\geq Q(x)\) satisfies the conic optimality cut
\[\theta\geq(b-Bx)^\top u.\]
If, at an evaluated point \(\bar x\in X\), a dual-feasible multiplier \(\bar u\) satisfies \((b-B\bar x)^\top\bar u=Q(\bar x)\), then its cut is exact at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every dual-feasible multiplier supplies an affine lower bound on conic recourse. A multiplier whose dual value equals the recourse value at the evaluated point produces a cut exact there.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is a closed convex cone.
\(d-A^\top u\in K^*\).
For the exactness assertion, \(\bar x\in X\) and \((b-B\bar x)^\top\bar u=Q(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq(b-Bx)^\top u\) is valid for \(\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\geq Q(x)\}\), and it is exact at \(\bar x\) under the stated value-equality condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Feasibility Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative-system cut for infeasible conic right-hand-side systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the feasibility system \(Ay=b-Bx\), \(y\in K\), with \(K\) a closed convex cone. If \(u\) satisfies
\[A^\top u\in K^*,\qquad (b-B\bar x)^\top u<0,\]
then no feasible \(y\) exists at \(\bar x\). Moreover, every parameter \(x\) for which the system is feasible satisfies
\[(b-Bx)^\top u\geq0.\]
Hence this inequality is a verifiable conic feasibility cut excluding \(\bar x\). Existence of such a certificate requires an applicable conic alternative theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-cone separating multiplier proves infeasibility at the trial point and yields a linear inequality valid for every parameter having feasible recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A^\top u\in K^*\) and \((b-B\bar x)^\top u<0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-recession certificate generating a feasibility cut for parametric conic recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual family
\[\sup_u\ (b-Bx)^\top u\quad\text{subject to}\quad d-A^\top u\in K^*,\]
let \(\bar u\) be dual feasible and let \(v\) satisfy \(-A^\top v\in K^*\). Then \(\bar u+t v\) is dual feasible for every \(t\geq0\). If \((b-B\bar x)^\top v>0\), its dual objective tends to \(+\infty\) at \(\bar x\). By weak duality, every parameter \(x\) having feasible finite primal recourse must satisfy the recession cut
\[(b-Bx)^\top v\leq0,\]
which excludes \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a dual-feasible base point, a dual recession direction with positive trial-point slope certifies that finite feasible recourse is impossible there and yields a linear cut requiring nonpositive slope.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(d-A^\top\bar u\in K^*\).
\(-A^\top v\in K^*\) and \((b-B\bar x)^\top v>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(x\) with feasible finite primal recourse satisfies \((b-Bx)^\top v\leq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Parametric Unboundedness Cut
Unboundedness Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-ray cut for objective-parametric conic subproblems with a fixed recession cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q(x)=\inf\{q(x)^\top y:Ay=b-Bx,\ y\in K\}\), where \(q(x)=q_0+Q_xx\). If \(r\in K\), \(Ar=0\), and \(q(\bar x)^\top r<0\), then from any feasible \(yar{}\) at \(\bar x\), the points \(yar{}+tr\) are feasible and their objectives tend to \(-\infty\). Thus finiteness of recourse requires the unboundedness cut
\[q(x)^\top r\geq0.\]
Because \(q\) is affine, this is a linear master inequality excluding \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-cost primal recession ray proves unbounded recourse and yields a linear parameter cut requiring that ray’s cost to be nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified verification conditions for primal and dual conic ray cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For conic recourse with affine right-hand side \(h(x)=b-Bx\) and affine cost \(q(x)\), either ray type is directly checkable. knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified-Recession Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where infeasibility lies in the closure of a nonclosed conic image and has no strict classical ray certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone and let \(A K=\{Ay:y\in K\}\). Suppose the system \(Ay=h(\bar x)\), \(y\in K\), satisfies
\[h(\bar x)\in\operatorname{cl}(A K)\setminus A K.\]
The system is infeasible, but every \(u\) satisfying \(A^\top u\in K^*\) also satisfies \(h(\bar x)^\top u\geq0\). Hence there is no strict classical certificate with
\[A^\top u\in K^*,\qquad h(\bar x)^\top u<0.\]
Accordingly, the associated strict ray-based Benders feasibility cut is unavailable at this boundary; a strengthened certificate system, such as an appropriate facial-reduction or extended-dual construction, may be needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an infeasible right-hand side lies in the closure of a nonclosed conic image, no strict classical separating ray exists, so an ordinary ray-based feasibility cut is unavailable.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A K=\{Ay:y\in K\}\).
\(h(\bar x)\in\operatorname{cl}(A K)\setminus A K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(u\) can satisfy both \(A^\top u\in K^*\) and \(h(\bar x)^\top u<0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and sampled-point exactness of affine cuts induced by an exact extended-dual certificate system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts obtained from weakly valid affine objectives of an exact extended conic dual.

knowledge_statements.title: Facially Reduced Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual cuts formed over a common face containing all relevant primal recourse points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\unlhd K\) be a face such that every feasible recourse point under consideration lies in \(F\). For
\[Q_F(x)=\inf\{d^\top y:Ay=b-Bx,\ y\in F\},\]

\[Q_F(x)\geq(b-Bx)^\top u.\]
If replacing \(K\) by \(F\) preserves the feasible sets and values on \(X\), then
\[\theta\geq(b-Bx)^\top u\]
is a valid facially reduced cut for the original recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After restricting recourse to a value-preserving face, dual feasibility in that face’s dual cone yields a valid affine master cut.

children.title: Extended-Dual Cut Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Regimes where extended-dual cuts correspond to cuts from facially reduced subproblems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient criterion for equality of extended-dual and facially reduced affine cut families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\) and \(\mathcal D_F\) be the feasible certificate sets of an extended dual and a facially reduced dual, producing affine functions \(g_z:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(h_u:X\to\mathbb R\). If maps \(T:\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\to\mathcal D_F\) and \(S:\mathcal D_F\to\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\) satisfy \[g_z(x)=h_{Tz}(x)\quad(z\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}},\ x\in X),\qquad h_u(x)=g_{Su}(x)\quad(u\in\mathcal D_F,\ x\in X),\] then \[\{g_z:z\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\}=\{h_u:u\in\mathcal D_F\}\quad\text{as functions on }X.\] Thus the representations generate identical Benders cut families on \(X\). This is a sufficient certificate-level correspondence, not a claim that a distinguished pair of maps is necessary for equality of the function families.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-way feasible-certificate maps preserving every affine function over the master domain are sufficient for equality of the generated cut families.
assumptions_latex: Both maps send feasible certificates to feasible certificates.
Both function-preservation identities hold for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: extended-dual and facially reduced feasible certificate sets

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Two-Way Cut-Family Correspondence
Extended-Dual Cut Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of cut families under objective-preserving correspondence of extended and facially reduced dual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\) be an extended-dual feasible set and \(\mathcal D_F=\{u:d-A^\top u\in F^*\}\) a facially reduced dual set. Suppose maps \(T:\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\to\mathcal D_F\) and \(S:\mathcal D_F\to\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ext}}\) satisfy, for every \(x\in X\),
\[\phi(x,z)=(b-Bx)^\top Tz,\qquad \phi(x,Su)=(b-Bx)^\top u.\]
Then the extended-dual and facially reduced constructions generate exactly the same affine cut family on \(X\). Equality can fail if either correspondence loses feasible certificates or preserves values only at one parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two constructions yield identical cuts precisely when feasible certificates map both ways while preserving their affine objectives throughout the master domain.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(S\) map feasible certificates into the stated feasible sets.
Both displayed objective identities hold for every \(x\in X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Value Representation With Unequal Affine Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract coefficient-family counterexample showing that exact value representation does not determine the represented cut set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(Q(x)=|x|\), \(\mathcal C_1=\{x\mapsto x,\ x\mapsto -x\}\), and \(\mathcal C_2=\mathcal C_1\cup\{x\mapsto0\}\). Every member is a global affine lower bound for \(Q\), and \[\sup_{\ell\in\mathcal C_1}\ell(x)=\sup_{\ell\in\mathcal C_2}\ell(x)=Q(x)\quad\forall x,\] with attainment, while \(\mathcal C_1\ne\mathcal C_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two attained affine representations can have the same value function while one contains an additional redundant cut.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup\mathcal C_1=\sup\mathcal C_2=Q\) pointwise, but \(\mathcal C_1\ne\mathcal C_2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Duality Cut Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attained strong duality for a finite-dimensional parametric conic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces; let \(K\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Z\) and \(B:Y\to Z\) be linear, and let \(c\in X\) and \(b\in Z\). Define \[Q(y)=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b-By,\ x\in K\}\] and \[D=\{z\in Z:A^*z+s=c\text{ for some }s\in K^*\}.\] For every \(z\in D\), weak duality gives \(Q(y)\ge\langle b-By,z\rangle\). If \(Q(\bar y)\) is finite and some \(\bar z\in D\) satisfies \[Q(\bar y)=\langle b-B\bar y,\bar z\rangle,\] then \(\theta\ge\langle b-By,\bar z\rangle\) is valid for the epigraph of \(Q\) and is exact at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional conic recourse problem, an attained dual optimum with zero duality gap produces a globally valid Benders lower cut that is exact at the sampled parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Z\) and \(B:Y\to Z\) are linear, and \(c\in X\), \(b\in Z\).
At \(\bar y\in Y\), \(Q(\bar y)\) is finite and the dual supremum equals \(Q(\bar y)\) and is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An attaining dual multiplier \(\bar z\) yields the valid cut \(\theta\ge\langle b-By,\bar z\rangle\), with equality at \(y=\bar y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Facially Reduced Cut Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut generation from a face that is valid uniformly over the stated master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone, and define \(Q(y)=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b-By,\ x\in K\}\). Suppose a face \(F\unlhd K\) contains every feasible \(x\) for every \(y\in Y\), and put \(L=\operatorname{span}F\), \(A_F=A|_L\), and \(c_F=P_Lc\). Define \[D_F=\{z_F\in Z:A_F^*z_F+s_F=c_F\text{ for some }s_F\in F^*\},\] where \(F^*\) is the dual cone in \(L\). Every \(z_F\in D_F\) satisfies \(Q(y)\ge\langle b-By,z_F\rangle\) for all \(y\in Y\). If some \(\bar z_F\in D_F\) attains \(Q(\bar y)\), then \(\theta\ge\langle b-By,\bar z_F\rangle\) is valid on \(Y\) and exact at \(\bar y\), even if the unreduced dual is nonattained or has a gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When one facial reduction is valid for every parameter under consideration, an attained reduced-dual optimizer yields a globally valid Benders cut that is exact at the sampled parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, \(K\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone, and the conic data have compatible dimensions.
A face \(F\unlhd K\) contains every feasible point of every subproblem indexed by \(y\in Y\).
At \(\bar y\in Y\), the reduced primal-dual pair has zero gap and the reduced dual optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reduced-dual feasible multiplier gives a valid cut on \(Y\), and an attaining optimizer gives a cut exact at \(\bar y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Face Reduction Does Not Ensure Global Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of uniform face validity over the domain on which a reduced-dual cut is asserted.

Weak-Duality Cut Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity based solely on conic weak duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces; let \(K\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone, \(A:X\to Z\) and \(B:Y\to Z\) be linear, and let \(c\in X\) and \(b\in Z\). Define \[Q(y)=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b-By,\ x\in K\}.\] If \(z\in Z\) satisfies \(A^*z+s=c\) for some \(s\in K^*\), then \[Q(y)\ge\langle b-By,z\rangle\] for every \(y\in Y\). Hence \(\theta\ge\langle b-By,z\rangle\) is a valid lower cut. Weak duality alone does not imply equality at a sampled parameter \(\bar y\), attainment of the best dual bound, or that the cut supports the epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every dual-feasible multiplier gives a valid lower cut by weak duality, but the cut need not be exact or supporting at the sampled parameter.

\(z\) is feasible for the ordinary conic dual; neither strong duality nor dual attainment is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\theta\ge\langle b-By,z\rangle\) is valid on \(Y\), but it need not be exact or supporting at \(\bar y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive conic duality gap as a boundary for exact ordinary cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sampled parameter \(\bar y\), let \(D\) be the ordinary dual feasible set, let \(\ell_z(y)\) denote the affine lower bound induced by \(z\in D\), and define \[D(\bar y)=\sup_{z\in D}\ell_z(\bar y).\] Suppose \(Q(\bar y)\) and \(D(\bar y)\) are finite and \[\delta=Q(\bar y)-D(\bar y)>0.\] Then every \(z\in D\) satisfies \[Q(\bar y)-\ell_z(\bar y)\ge\delta.\] Thus no ordinary-dual cut \(\theta\ge\ell_z(y)\) is exact at \(\bar y\), regardless of whether the dual supremum is attained. Exactness can be recovered only through a representation or certificate system that closes the gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive duality gap, every ordinary-dual cut misses the true recourse value at the sampled parameter by at least that gap and cannot be exact there.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(\bar y)\) and \(D(\bar y)=\sup_{z\in D}\ell_z(\bar y)\) are finite.
The positive gap \(\delta=Q(\bar y)-D(\bar y)>0\) occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every ordinary-dual cut misses \(Q(\bar y)\) by at least \(\delta\), so none is exact at \(\bar y\).

children.title: Multiplier-Attainment Failure
children.top_down_role: Failure of multiplier attainment despite finite or otherwise meaningful dual values.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Attainment Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment and the loss of an optimal ordinary-dual cut certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(D\subseteq Z\) be a nonempty dual feasible set, and let \(\ell_z(\bar y)\in\mathbb R\) be the dual objective at a fixed parameter \(\bar y\). Multiplier attainment fails when \[\sup_{z\in D}\ell_z(\bar y)<+\infty\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in D}\ell_z(\bar y)=\varnothing.\] A maximizing sequence \((z_k)\subset D\) then exists, but it need not have a subsequence converging to a point of \(D\). Consequently, no optimal ordinary multiplier certificate or exact cut associated with an attained dual optimum is available. Each finite dual-feasible multiplier still supplies its weak-duality cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite dual supremum can fail to be attained: maximizing multipliers may have no subsequence converging to a feasible maximizer, so no optimal ordinary multiplier certificate is available.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space and \(D\subseteq Z\) is nonempty.
The supremum of \(z\mapsto\ell_z(\bar y)\) over \(D\) is finite but is not attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A maximizing sequence exists, but no member of \(D\) is an optimal multiplier and convergence to a feasible maximizer is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: Dual objective value at the sampled parameter

children.title: Gap-Induced Cut Invalidity
children.top_down_role: Cut-validity limitations attributable to unresolved duality gaps.

assumptions_latex: A positive gap \(Q(\bar y)>D(\bar y)\) separates the primal recourse value from the ordinary dual value.
An algorithm treats an ordinary dual bound as exact at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting equality claim or termination certificate is invalid; dual-feasible lower inequalities themselves remain valid by weak duality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarifies what a duality gap invalidates in Benders reasoning.

source_refs.locator: 4 Duality and Optimality Conditions p. 67
source_refs.source_title: Handbook of Semidefinite Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(Q(\bar y)>D(\bar y)\), then replacing \(Q(\bar y)\) by \(D(\bar y)\) in an exactness test understates recourse by
\[Q(\bar y)-D(\bar y)>0.\]
Accordingly, a claimed supporting equality \(\theta=D(\bar y)\) at \(\bar y\), or a termination decision based on that equality, is not a certificate for the true epigraph. However, for every dual-feasible \(z\), the inequality \(\theta\ge \ell_z(y)\) remains valid. The gap destroys exactness and associated optimality conclusions, not weak-duality validity of the lower cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A duality gap invalidates claims that a dual cut is exact or certifies termination, but it does not invalidate the underlying weak-duality lower inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Induced Cut Invalidity

source_witnesses.locator: 4 Duality and Optimality Conditions p. 67
source_witnesses.source_title: Handbook of Semidefinite Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of dominance on the comparison domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Y_1\subseteq Y_2, pointwise weak dominance on Y_2 implies weak dominance on Y_1, but strictness may disappear on Y_1; dominance on Y_1 need not extend to Y_2. Pareto status can therefore change when the comparison domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking or enlarging the master domain can change which cuts are Pareto-optimal.
assumptions_latex: The same admissible cut family is compared on both domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain Dependence of Pareto Efficiency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic equivalent formulation of Pareto-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For valid affine lower cuts \mathcal L on Y, define \ell_2\preceq_Y\ell_1 when \ell_1(y)\ge\ell_2(y) for every y\in Y. After identifying cuts equal on Y, \preceq_Y is a partial order. A cut is Pareto-optimal precisely when its equivalence class is maximal in this order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise cut dominance is a preorder, and Pareto-optimal cuts are its maximal equivalence classes.
assumptions_latex: Y is the comparison domain and every member of \mathcal L is a valid lower cut there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell\text{ is Pareto-optimal}\iff [\ell]\text{ is maximal in }\mathcal L/\!\sim_Y.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Preorder Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a Pareto-Optimal Dominator Under Compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal-dominator existence for a compact continuously parameterized family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Y and U be compact, let (u,y)\mapsto\ell_u(y) be continuous, and let \mu be a finite positive measure with support Y. For u_0\in U, maximize \int_Y\ell_u\,d\mu over u satisfying \ell_u\ge\ell_{u_0} on Y. Every maximizer dominates \ell_{u_0} and is Pareto-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a compact continuous cut family, every cut has a Pareto-optimal dominator obtained by full-support scalarization of its upper dominance set.
assumptions_latex: Y and U are compact.
The cut parameterization is jointly continuous.
\mu is finite, positive, and has support Y.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall u_0\in U\ \exists u^*\in U:\ \ell_{u^*}\succeq_Y\ell_{u_0}\text{ and }\ell_{u^*}\text{ is Pareto-optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence of a Pareto-Optimal Dominator Under Compactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noncompact Cut Family Without a Pareto-Maximal Member
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of maximal-cut existence when the admissible family omits its limiting supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=[0,1]\), let \(Q(y)\equiv1\), and consider
\[
\mathcal L=\{\ell_a:\ell_a(y)=a,\ 0\le a<1\}.
\]
Every member is a valid affine lower cut. For each \(a<1\), any \(b\in(a,1)\) gives \(\ell_b(y)>\ell_a(y)\) on all of \(Y\). Hence \(\mathcal L\) has no Pareto-optimal member, although its pointwise supremum is the omitted valid cut \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An open chain of constant valid cuts improves toward a missing supremum and has no Pareto-optimal member.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\equiv1\).
The admissible parameter interval is \([0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L\text{ has no maximal equivalence class under }\preceq_Y.

notation.meaning: Constant affine lower cut with value a.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Cut Family Without a Pareto-Maximal Member

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is the master feasible set and \(\mathcal L\) is a family of valid affine lower cuts for \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cut is Pareto-optimal exactly when no other cut in \(\mathcal L\) dominates it on \(Y\).

notation.meaning: Family of valid affine lower functions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dominance definition for Benders cuts is mathematically unambiguous
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto efficiency under pointwise dominance on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\ell_1,\ell_2\in\mathcal L\), say that \(\ell_1\) dominates \(\ell_2\) on \(Y\) when
\[\ell_1(y)\ge \ell_2(y)\quad\text{for all }y\in Y,\]
with strict inequality for at least one \(y\in Y\). A valid cut \(\theta\ge \ell(y)\) is Pareto-optimal relative to \((Y,\mathcal L)\) if no \(\tilde\ell\in\mathcal L\) dominates \(\ell\). A Pareto-optimal cut is therefore undominated within the specified family; the designation depends on both the comparison domain \(Y\) and the admissible cut family \(\mathcal L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut is Pareto-optimal when no admissible cut is at least as strong everywhere on the master set and strictly stronger somewhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Optimal Cut Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance definition is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Core Points Need Not Select an Undominated Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the core-point selection guarantee when the chosen point is outside the relative interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=[0,1]\), choose the boundary point \(y^0=0\), and let \(\bar y=0\). For \(Q(y)=y\), both \(\ell_1(y)=0\) and \(\ell_2(y)=y\) are valid lower functions exact at \(\bar y\). They tie at \(y^0\), so auxiliary maximization may return \(\ell_1\), although \(\ell_2\ge\ell_1\) on \(Y\) with strict inequality for \(y>0\). Thus a boundary evaluation point does not ensure undominated selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the core point is placed on the boundary, the auxiliary objective can tie a dominated cut with its dominator.
assumptions_latex: Candidate cuts are the valid exact lower functions \(\ell_1(y)=0\) and \(\ell_2(y)=y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Maximization at \(y^0\notin\operatorname{ri}Y\) may select a dominated cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Core Points Need Not Select an Undominated Cut

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is convex, \(y^0\in\operatorname{ri}(Y)\), and \(\bar y\in Y\).
The set of dual-feasible cuts exact at \(\bar y\) is nonempty and the auxiliary maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Maximizing the cut value at \(y^0\) among cuts exact at \(\bar y\) returns an undominated cut within that family.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: core-point auxiliary optimization is the classical Pareto-cut selection rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core-point selection among dual cuts exact at the current parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(y^0\in\operatorname{ri}(Y)\), the sampled parameter \(\bar y\), and the recourse value \(Q(\bar y)\). Solve
\[\max_{z}\ \ell_z(y^0)\quad\text{subject to}\quad z\in D,\qquad \ell_z(\bar y)=Q(\bar y).\]
If an optimizer \(z^*\) exists, output \(\theta\ge \ell_{z^*}(y)\). Every feasible candidate is valid and exact at \(\bar y\). Moreover, no other candidate cut exact at \(\bar y\) can dominate the output on \(Y\): strict dominance somewhere would imply a strictly larger value at the relative-interior point \(y^0\), contradicting optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a core point in the relative interior and maximize the value there among dual cuts exact at the current parameter; the selected cut is undominated.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-Point Cut Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The core-point auxiliary selection rule and its undominated-cut conclusion require an inspectable source, particularly for the stated conic extension. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Cut Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Combination of multiple subproblem or scenario cuts into aggregate master constraints.

assumptions_latex: Each inequality \(\theta_i\ge \ell_i(y)\) is valid on \(Y\).
Weights satisfy \(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i w_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate inequality \(\sum_i w_i\theta_i\ge\sum_i w_i\ell_i(y)\) is valid but generally does not imply its constituent inequalities.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative aggregation of valid inequalities preserves validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex aggregation of componentwise Benders inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given valid component cuts
\[\theta_i\ge \ell_i(y),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m,\]
and weights \(w_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i=1\), their weighted aggregate is
\[\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\theta_i\ge \sum_{i=1}^m w_i\ell_i(y).\]
Validity follows for every \(y\in Y\) by nonnegative summation. The aggregate uses one inequality in place of the active component inequalities. Unless additional structure makes the component violations proportional, satisfaction of the aggregate does not imply satisfaction of every constituent cut, so aggregation can weaken the master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of valid component cuts is valid and reduces constraint count, but it generally loses information because it does not enforce each component cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonnegative aggregation preserves validity and the representation fits the leaf, but the record has no inspectable citation for its Benders aggregation interpretation and strength claim.

children.title: Cut Disaggregation
children.top_down_role: Separation of aggregate cut information into blockwise or scenario-specific constraints.

assumptions_latex: The recourse value decomposes as \(Q(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m Q_i(y)\).
For each component, \(\ell_i(y)\le Q_i(y)\) on the master set \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disaggregated system \(\theta_i\ge\ell_i(y)\) implies the aggregate cut and is generally strictly stronger in the extended master space.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise epigraph inequalities imply their sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate epigraph variables and cuts for decomposable recourse components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Introduce component epigraph variables satisfying
\[\theta_i\ge \ell_i(y),\qquad i=1,ldots,m,\]
and represent total recourse by \(\theta=\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i\). Summation yields the aggregate inequality
\[\theta\ge \sum_{i=1}^m\ell_i(y).\]
Hence the disaggregated system implies its aggregate projection. The converse generally fails: an aggregate inequality can be satisfied while some component inequality is violated and compensated by slack in another component. Disaggregation therefore preserves componentwise information and can strengthen the extended master relaxation, at the cost of additional variables and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate cuts for decomposable recourse components imply the summed cut and usually strengthen the master formulation, while requiring more epigraph variables and constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Disaggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disaggregation claim is plausible, but no inspectable source is supplied. The statement also contains the malformed index text i=1,ldots,m, which must be repaired to i=1,\ldots,m inside math delimiters before acceptance.

children.title: Partial Aggregation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Intermediate groupings between fully aggregate and fully disaggregate cut systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength ordering of retained-cut approximations indexed by block partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(S\), define \[m_{\mathcal P}(x)=\sum_{G\in\mathcal P}\max_{j\in J}\sum_{s\in G}p_s\phi_{sj}(x).\] If \(\mathcal P_f\) refines \(\mathcal P_c\), then \(m_{\mathcal P_f}(x)\ge m_{\mathcal P_c}(x)\) for every \(x\). Hence the finer-partition retained-cut epigraph formulation is at least as strong as the coarser formulation. The inequality may be strict because fine groups may attain their maxima at different retained indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refining the aggregation partition cannot weaken the retained-cut approximation and may strengthen it by allowing different groups to activate different cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(J\) are finite and nonempty.
\(p_s>0\), and each \(\phi_{sj}\) is a valid block minorant.
\(\mathcal P_f\) refines \(\mathcal P_c\).

notation.meaning: retained-cut lower model for partition P

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Under Partition Refinement
Partial Aggregation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-block Benders cuts aggregated according to a fixed partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite block set, \(p_s>0\), and \(\mathcal P\) a partition of \(S\). At iteration \(j\), suppose block \(s\) supplies the valid affine minorant \(q_s(x)\ge a_{sj}^{\mathsf T}x+b_{sj}\). Partial aggregation represents the recourse approximation using variables \(\theta_G\), \(G\in\mathcal P\), and constraints \[\theta_G\ge \sum_{s\in G}p_s\bigl(a_{sj}^{\mathsf T}x+b_{sj}\bigr),\qquad G\in\mathcal P,\ j\in J.\] The master minimizes its first-stage objective plus \(\sum_{G\in\mathcal P}\theta_G\). Singleton groups give full disaggregation, while \(\mathcal P=\{S\}\) gives full aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition of scenario blocks determines which valid block cuts are summed. Singleton groups are fully disaggregated, and one group containing every block is fully aggregated.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and the retained cut-index set \(J\) are finite.
Each affine function is a valid global minorant of its block recourse function.
The weights satisfy \(p_s>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P\) interpolates between fully disaggregated and fully aggregated Benders master representations.

notation.meaning: finite set of scenario or conic subproblem blocks
master epigraph variable for group G

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite blockwise Benders cuts may be summed over partition cells because positive weighted sums preserve validity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Partial Aggregation Regimes leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no citation is supplied for the partition-based Benders formulation or its interpretation. Standard-field rationale alone does not satisfy the citation requirement.

children.title: Aggregation-Loss Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of useful cut information caused by coarse aggregation.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation-Loss Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pointwise loss caused by forcing block cuts to share one iteration index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite index set \(J\), define \(u_s(x)=\max_{j\in J}\phi_{sj}(x)\). The disaggregated and aligned-aggregate bounds are \[D(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_su_s(x),\qquad A(x)=\max_{j\in J}\sum_{s\in S}p_s\phi_{sj}(x).\] Then \(A(x)\le D(x)\). If every \(p_s>0\), equality holds exactly when \(\bigcap_{s\in S}\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in J}\phi_{sj}(x)\ne\varnothing\). Thus aggregation loses strength precisely at points where no retained iteration index simultaneously maximizes every block approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aligned aggregate cut model is weaker exactly when different blocks require different retained cuts to attain their individual maxima.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(J\) are finite and nonempty.
\(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x)-A(x)>0\) if and only if the blockwise maximizing-index sets have empty intersection.

notation.meaning: retained affine cut for block s and index j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the boundary follows from comparing a maximum of weighted sums with a weighted sum of maxima

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum-of-sums comparison and common-maximizer equality condition are mathematically plausible and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf. However, no inspectable source supports its identification as the Benders aggregation-loss boundary; the sets and functions also require authoritative contextualization.

children.title: Cut-Pool Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of active cuts from a larger retained pool.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fairness condition needed by convergence arguments that require persistent separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the parent cutting-plane convergence argument requires a separating cut for every recurrent nonoptimal trial point. Active-pool selection preserves that argument if every such required cut is selected, regenerated, or reactivated after finitely many subsequent visits and is enforced whenever the argument uses it. Validity of the selected subset alone does not imply this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selection rule must eventually enforce cuts needed at recurrent bad points whenever the parent convergence proof relies on them.
assumptions_latex: The stated parent convergence proof relies on repeated separation at recurrent nonoptimal points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{eventual required-cut enforcement}\Longrightarrow\text{the selection rule does not remove that proof premise}.
knowledge_statements.title: Eventual-Enforcement Safeguard

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant and order relation for selecting from a valid retained pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P be a pool of valid inequalities and A_1\subseteq A_2\subseteq P. For a minimization master, M(A_2)\subseteq M(A_1) and v(A_1)\le v(A_2). Selection therefore changes master size and strength but not the validity of any selected inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting fewer valid cuts weakens a minimization master but does not invalidate the cuts retained.
assumptions_latex: Every cut in P is valid.
The compared masters have identical objectives and non-cut constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_1\subseteq A_2\Longrightarrow M(A_2)\subseteq M(A_1),\quad v(A_1)\le v(A_2).

notation.meaning: Master feasible region using active set A

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Subset Validity and Strength Order

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Budget Starvation of a Required Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-pool witness that validity and a fixed active-set budget do not imply eventual enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master domain be \(X=\{0,1\}\), minimize \(x\), and let the valid pool contain \(c_1:x\ge0\) and \(c_2:x\ge1\), where the true feasible set is \(\{1\}\). If the active-cut budget is one and a fixed ranking always selects \(c_1\), every selected master returns \(x^k=0\). The separating cut \(c_2\) is starved indefinitely, although enforcing it yields the true solution \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-budget ranking can enforce a harmless cut forever while starving the only cut excluding a recurrent invalid point.
assumptions_latex: The active-cut budget is one.
The ranking always selects \(c_1\) ahead of \(c_2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Budget Starvation of a Required Cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract selection rule separating validity, priority, protection, and capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite pool of valid cuts, \(H\subseteq P\) a protected set, \(w_i\in\mathbb R\) declared priorities, and \(B\ge |H|\). Select \[A\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{H\subseteq S\subseteq P,\ |S|\le B}\sum_{i\in S\setminus H}w_i.\] Equivalently, retain \(H\) and up to \(B-|H|\) nonprotected cuts having the largest positive priorities, using a fixed tie rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep protected cuts and fill remaining capacity with the highest positive-priority cuts; priority affects selection, not validity.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is finite and every member of }P\text{ is valid}.
B\ge |H|.
\text{Ties use a declared deterministic rule}.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Weight Budgeted Active-Set Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct standard attributes for ranking valid stored cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stored inequality \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) and trial point \(x^k\), define violation \(v_i^k=[a_i^\top x^k-b_i]_+\) and normalized efficacy \(e_i^k=v_i^k/\|a_i\|_*\) when \(a_i\ne0\). Inactivity age counts consecutive selection rounds since a declared activity event. Diversity may be measured by a declared distance or angular separation from already selected normals. Violation, efficacy, activity or recency, diversity, and estimated processing cost are distinct selection attributes and need not induce the same ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violation, normalized efficacy, activity or recency, geometric diversity, and processing cost are distinct cut-ranking attributes.
assumptions_latex: \text{The norm and dual norm used for efficacy are fixed}.
a_i\ne0\text{ whenever normalized efficacy is evaluated}.
\text{The activity event and diversity metric are declared by the policy}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Violation, efficacy, recency, diversity, and cost need not induce identical rankings}.

notation.meaning: violation of cut i at the current point

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Cut-Selection Measures
Cut-Pool Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted selection of valid cuts for the next Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a valid cut pool \(P_k\), current master point \(x_k\), activity ages \(d_i^k\), scores \(\sigma_i^k\), and budget \(B\), retain every protected cut and choose at most \(B\) further cuts with largest scores, where a permissible score is \[\sigma_i^k=\alpha\,[g_i(x_k)]_+ +\beta\,(1+d_i^k)^{-1},\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge0.\] Here \(g_i(x)\le0\) is cut \(i\). Solve the master with the selected active set, place unselected cuts in an inactive pool without changing their coefficients, and return the new master point and updated activity metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Protect mandatory cuts, rank the remaining valid cuts by violation and recency, enforce a budget, and archive rather than destroy unselected cuts.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(P_k\) is a valid Benders inequality.
The budget accommodates all protected cuts.
Ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a budget-feasible active set together with an unchanged inactive archive of valid cuts.

notation.meaning: available cut pool at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Cut-Pool Selection, but the particular violation-recency score, protected-cut policy, and budget semantics define one noncanonical policy. No source establishes this variant or its intended lifecycle guarantees.

children.title: Cut Deletion
children.top_down_role: Removal of inactive, dominated, redundant, or costly cuts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Redundancy Certificate for Safe Cut Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deletion test relative to the retained master and its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_{-i}=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le0\ (j\ne i)\}. Then cut i is redundant relative to the retained master exactly when \sup_{x\in M_{-i}}g_i(x)\le0. In that case deleting it leaves the master feasible set unchanged; any x\in M_{-i} with g_i(x)>0 certifies nonredundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is safely redundant exactly when it cannot be violated over the master formed by the remaining cuts.
assumptions_latex: The retained master and redundancy supremum are interpreted exactly.
All compared models use the same domain and non-cut constraints.

notation.meaning: Master feasible set after omitting cut i

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Certificate for Safe Cut Deletion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set and bound order under deletion alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For active cut sets A'\subseteq A, let v(A)=\inf\{F(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0\ (i\in A)\}. Then M(A)\subseteq M(A') and v(A')\le v(A). If every deleted cut is redundant relative to M(A'), both feasible sets and values are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting cuts enlarges a minimization master and cannot improve its lower bound; deleting only redundant cuts changes neither set nor value.
assumptions_latex: The objective, domain, and non-cut constraints are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A'\subseteq A\Longrightarrow M(A)\subseteq M(A'),\quad v(A')\le v(A).

notation.meaning: Master optimum with active cut set A

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Relaxes a Minimization Master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact termination safeguard for a master whose valid deleted cuts remain in an inactive archive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the active valid-cut set, \(I\) the inactive archive, and \(x_k\) an exact optimizer of the active master. Certification relative to the complete retained pool additionally requires \[g_i(x_k)\le0\qquad\text{for every }i\in I.\] If an archived cut has \(g_i(x_k)>0\), then \(x_k\) is infeasible for the retained-pool master and cannot support termination relative to that pool; the cut must be restored or otherwise enforced. Passing every archived cut certifies feasibility for the retained pool, but says nothing about ungenerated cuts and does not restore intermediate bounds weakened by deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate from the active master is feasible for the complete retained cut pool exactly when it also satisfies every archived cut.
assumptions_latex: Every archived inequality remains globally valid.
\(x_k\) is feasible for the active master.
Certification is relative to the finite retained pool \(A\cup I\), not ungenerated cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\in M(A\cup I)\iff g_i(x_k)\le0\ \forall i\in I\), given active-master feasibility.

notation.meaning: master feasible set using the complete retained pool

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Pool Validation after Cut Deletion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary-Solve Cost of Exact Redundancy Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-sweep solve count for certified redundancy screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m\) active cuts are each screened at most once using one violation-maximization problem, a deletion sweep formulates at most \(m\) auxiliary master-class optimization problems. Early discovery of a violating feasible point may terminate an individual screen without an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Screening each of m active cuts once requires at most m auxiliary redundancy problems.
assumptions_latex: Each active cut is screened at most once during the sweep.
At most one auxiliary violation-maximization problem is formulated per screened cut.

notation.meaning: number of active cuts at the start of the sweep

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Solve Cost of Exact Redundancy Screening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parent-method guarantee when every deletion preserves the generated-cut master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a Benders method whose no-deletion version has a stated convergence guarantee. Suppose every deleted cut is exactly implied, at its deletion time, by the unchanged master domain, non-cut constraints, and then-retained cuts. Sequentially applying such deletions preserves the feasible region and value of the master containing all cuts generated to that time; later addition of constraints preserves every established implication. Consequently, the deletion method inherits any convergence or finite-termination guarantee that depends only on these master regions, values, and the same oracle responses. Equality of iterates additionally requires identical optimizer selection and oracle choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact redundant-only deletion preserves every generated-cut master and inherits applicable guarantees of the corresponding no-deletion method.
assumptions_latex: Each deletion has an exact implication certificate relative to the then-retained master.
The underlying domain and non-cut constraints do not change.
Later iterations add constraints.
Any claim of identical iterates uses identical optimizer selection and oracle choices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Discrete Termination with Rejection-Cover Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-memory safeguard for an exact cutting-plane method over a finite master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master domain \(X\) be finite. Suppose an exact oracle either terminates at an accepted trial point or returns a globally valid cut violated by the rejected point. If deletion always retains at least one active cut excluding every previously rejected point, no rejected point can be generated again as a master-feasible trial. The method therefore terminates after at most \(|X|\) distinct oracle evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite domain, retaining one active excluding cut for every rejected point prevents cycling and gives finite termination.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite.
The oracle is exact and acceptance terminates the method.
Every rejection returns a globally valid cut violated by the rejected point.
An active excluding cut is retained for every previously rejected point.

notation.meaning: number of distinct oracle evaluations before termination

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Discrete Termination with Rejection-Cover Deletion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion sweep separating heuristic age nomination from exact set- or value-preservation certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an exact minimizer \(x^k\) of the active master, define \(\sigma_i^k=-g_i(x^k)\) and update \(d_i^{k+1}=0\) when \(\sigma_i^k\le\tau_{\rm act}\), and \(d_i^{k+1}=d_i^k+1\) otherwise. Fix \(D\ge1\) and one attained exact optimal master-dual certificate. Protect permanent cuts, the sole active rejection cut for any stored rejected point, and cuts having positive multiplier in that chosen certificate. An unprotected cut with \(d_i^{k+1}\ge D\) may be deleted if exact redundancy is certified, or if its multiplier in the chosen certificate is zero. Redundancy preserves the master feasible set; zero-multiplier deletion preserves only the current optimal value. Archive the cut coefficients, creation and last-active iterations, age, deletion reason, and certificate. Validate a termination candidate against every archived cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Age and slack nominate deletion candidates, while exact redundancy or a zero multiplier in a fixed exact dual certificate justifies deletion; all deleted cuts are archived and checked before termination.
assumptions_latex: The active master is solved exactly whenever value preservation is claimed.
The multiplier test uses one attained exact optimal dual certificate and strong duality.
\(\tau_{\rm act}\ge0\) and \(D\) is a positive integer.
Archived cuts remain globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Redundancy deletion preserves the master set; zero-multiplier deletion preserves the current value; archive validation restores retained-pool feasibility testing.}

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Age-and-Slack Cut Deletion Sweep
Cut Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Age-and-slack deletion rule with protected-cut safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each active valid cut \(g_i(x)\le0\), update its inactivity age by \[d_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}0,&-g_i(x_k)\le\tau_{\mathrm{act}},\\ d_i^k+1,&-g_i(x_k)>\tau_{\mathrm{act}}.\end{cases}\] Given an age threshold \(D\), remove cut \(i\) from the active master only if \(d_i^{k+1}\ge D\) and it is neither protected nor required to support the current certified lower bound. Store every removed cut and its metadata in an inactive archive. The output is the reduced active master and the archive; deletion does not invalidate any remaining inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only sufficiently old, slack cuts that are neither protected nor needed by the certified bound, and retain deleted cuts in an archive.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_{\mathrm{act}}\ge0\) and \(D\) is a positive integer.
Cut validity is independent of whether the cut is active.
The algorithm can identify protected and bound-supporting cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only eligible inactive cuts leave the active master, and each removed cut remains available for reactivation.

children.title: Cut Reactivation
children.top_down_role: Return of retained inactive cuts to the active master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reactivation from a fixed finite archive without budget or tolerance ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I be a finite archive. Repeatedly solve the current master globally; if its optimizer violates any archived cut, reactivate at least one such cut and retain it for the remainder of the closure loop. Stop when no archived cut is violated. The loop has at most |I| reactivation rounds, and its terminal optimizer is optimal for the master containing the original active cuts together with every cut in I.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact separation over a fixed finite archive restores full-pool feasibility after at most one reactivation round per archived cut.
assumptions_latex: Archived coefficients are unchanged.
Every intermediate master is solved globally.
At least one violated archived cut is permanently reactivated in each nonterminal closure round.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Finite-Archive Reactivation Closure
Cut Reactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation-based return of archived cuts to the active master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an inactive archive \(I_k\), candidate point \(x_k\), and tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{viol}}\ge0\), evaluate every archived cut \(g_i(x)\le0\) or call an exact archive-separation oracle. Form \[R_k=\{i\in I_k:g_i(x_k)>\tau_{\mathrm{viol}}\}.\] Move all cuts in \(R_k\), or the most violated budget-feasible subset, into the active master, reset their inactivity ages to zero, and resolve the master. Repeat separation and resolution until no archived cut exceeds the tolerance. Return the resulting point and updated active and inactive pools.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each candidate, restore archived cuts that are violated beyond tolerance and resolve until the archive contains no detectably violated cut.
assumptions_latex: Archived cuts retain their original valid coefficients.
Archive separation is exact if all violated archived cuts must be recovered.
Any reactivation budget preserves the most violated cuts for later checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(g_i(x_k)\le\tau_{\mathrm{viol}}\) for every exactly checked archived cut \(i\).
