children.title: Premature-Deletion Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of master strength or progress caused by removing useful cuts too early.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Permanent Deletion Can Destroy Model Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric family exhibiting the loss caused by permanently deleting a nonredundant support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a>0, let Q_a(x)=\max\{x,a-x\} on [0,a]. The two-cut model is exact and has minimum a/2. Permanently deleting a-x leaves m_D(x)=x, whose minimum is 0 at x=0 although Q_a(0)=a. Thus the retained model remains a valid lower model but loses exactness and yields a strictly weaker lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting one necessary support from a two-piece value function preserves validity but can make the master choose a point with a strict model gap.
assumptions_latex: The deleted cut is neither regenerated nor reactivated.
The master domain is [0,a] with a>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Permanent Deletion Can Destroy Model Exactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional safeguard for parent methods whose proofs require recurrent separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Validity of all retained cuts guarantees only that the retained master remains a lower model. It does not guarantee monotone lower bounds across deletions, exactness at trial points, or convergence. For a parent convergence proof that requires separation of recurrent nonoptimal trial points, a sufficient lifecycle safeguard is that each cut needed for such separation is retained, regenerated, or reactivated after finitely many subsequent visits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retained validity alone is insufficient; eventual enforcement is a sufficient safeguard when the parent proof relies on recurrent separation.
assumptions_latex: The parent convergence argument uses separation at recurrent nonoptimal trial points.
knowledge_statements.title: Eventual-Enforcement Sufficiency Boundary
Premature-Deletion Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-cut model showing loss of exactness after deleting a necessary cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=|x|=\max\{x,-x\}\) on \([-1,1]\). With both supporting cuts, the master model \(m(x)=\max\{x,-x\}\) is exact and has minimum \(0\) at \(x=0\). If the cut \(-x\) is deleted permanently, the retained model becomes \(m_D(x)=x\), whose minimum is \(-1\) at \(x=-1\), while \(f(-1)=1\). Hence permanent deletion before a cut is globally redundant can destroy model exactness and the certified lower-bound sequence; deletion is safe only with a redundancy certificate or a reactivation mechanism that detects later violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting one of the two supports of the absolute-value function makes the master select the wrong endpoint and destroys exactness.
assumptions_latex: The master domain is \([-1,1]\).
The deleted cut cannot be regenerated or reactivated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Permanent age-based deletion alone does not preserve exactness of a cutting-plane master.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit absolute-value model directly exhibits the failure mechanism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar example is correct and counterexample is an appropriate kind for this boundary leaf. Nevertheless, the retained model still supplies a valid but weaker lower bound, so the phrase about destroying the certified lower-bound sequence needs precise interpretation, and no source connects the example to Benders cut-pool convergence.

children.title: Proximal Master Regularization
children.top_down_role: Master regularization based on proximity to a reference solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Proximal Trial Point and Optimality System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometry of a quadratically regularized Benders master, independent of center-update policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex with \(X\cap\operatorname{dom}m\ne\varnothing\). For \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\rho>0\), the problem \[\min_{x\in X}\left\{m(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x-z\|_2^2\right\}\] has a unique minimizer \(x_\rho\), characterized by \[0\in\partial m(x_\rho)+\rho(x_\rho-z)+N_X(x_\rho).\] If \(m(x)=g^\top x+\beta\), then \(x_\rho=\Pi_X(z-g/\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic stabilization gives a unique trial point, an exact normal-cone optimality condition, and a projection formula for an affine model.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, with \(X\cap\operatorname{dom}m\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to X at x

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Proximal Trial Point and Optimality System

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical quantities deciding whether a proximal trial replaces the current center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the true convex objective and let \(m_k\le F\) satisfy \(m_k(z_k)=F(z_k)\). For a proximal-master trial \(x^{k+1}\), define \[\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}=F(z_k)-m_k(x^{k+1}),\qquad \Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}=F(z_k)-F(x^{k+1}).\] When \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\), declare a serious step at threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\) if \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}\ge\eta\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\); otherwise declare a null step. A serious step may set \(z_{k+1}=x^{k+1}\); a null step retains \(z_{k+1}=z_k\) while refining the model at the trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The serious-step test compares actual objective decrease with decrease predicted by an exact-at-center lower model.
assumptions_latex: m_k(x)\le F(x)\quad\forall x\in X.
m_k(z_k)=F(z_k).
\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Predicted Decrease and Serious-Step Ratio

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Well-Posedness Without Positive Proximal Weight
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for the positive quadratic weight in the proximal master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(z=0\), and \(\rho=0\). If \(m(x)=0\), every \(x\in\mathbb R\) minimizes \(m(x)+\frac\rho2|x-z|^2\), so the trial point is not unique. If instead \(m(x)=x\), the same master has infimum \(-\infty\). Thus the general existence-and-uniqueness conclusions supplied by quadratic stabilization need not hold when \(\rho>0\) is dropped.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero proximal weight, a convex master can have many minimizers or be unbounded.
assumptions_latex: X=\mathbb R.
\rho=0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho=0\ \not\Longrightarrow\text{existence and uniqueness of a proximal-master trial point}.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Well-Posedness Without Positive Proximal Weight

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Firm Nonexpansiveness of the Fixed-Model Proximal Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of the proximal-master trial to its center for a fixed model and weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=m+\delta_X\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, let \(\rho>0\), and define \(P_\rho(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x-z\|^2\}\). Then for all \(z,w\), \[\|P_\rho(z)-P_\rho(w)\|^2\le \langle P_\rho(z)-P_\rho(w),z-w\rangle.\] Consequently \(P_\rho\) is single-valued and nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed model and positive proximal weight, the trial-point map is firmly nonexpansive in its center.
assumptions_latex: \(f=m+\delta_X\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: proximal-master solution map for a fixed model and weight
convex indicator of the master domain

knowledge_statements.title: Firm Nonexpansiveness of the Fixed-Model Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-oracle protocol with explicit model, center, bounded weight, certification, and stopping updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z_0\in X\), an exact-at-center lower model \(m_0\le F\), and \(\rho_0>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(x^{k+1}=\arg\min_{x\in X}\{m_k(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|x-z_k\|^2\}\). Evaluate \(F(x^{k+1})\), add an exact supporting cut to form \(m_{k+1}\), and compute predicted and actual decreases relative to \(z_k\). If the actual decrease is at least \(\eta\in(0,1)\) times the predicted decrease, set \(z_{k+1}=x^{k+1}\); otherwise set \(z_{k+1}=z_k\). Choose \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\) by a declared update rule. Compute \(L_{k+1}=\inf_Xm_{k+1}\), retain the best evaluated incumbent value \(U_{k+1}\), and stop only when \(U_{k+1}-L_{k+1}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stabilized master selects a unique trial, the oracle refines the model, the serious-step ratio updates the center, the positive weight remains bounded, and only the unregularized model supplies the lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Each \(m_k\) is a proper closed convex lower model exact at \(z_k\).
Oracle evaluations return exact objective values and supporting cuts.
\(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_k\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\).

children.title: Level Master Regularization
children.top_down_role: Master regularization based on controlled objective or bound levels.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bound update certified by model-level infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let m_k\le F on X. If \{x\in X:m_k(x)\le\ell\}=\varnothing, then F(x)>\ell for every x\in X and consequently \inf_{x\in X}F(x)\ge\ell. Thus \ell may be installed as a certified lower bound when level-set infeasibility is certified exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If no point reaches the tested lower-model level, that level is a valid lower bound for the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: m_k(x)\le F(x) for every x\in X.
Level-set infeasibility is certified exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Model-Level Set Lower-Bound Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and variational characterization of the level-master projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If X is closed and convex, m_k is lower semicontinuous and convex, and C_k=\{x\in X:m_k(x)\le\ell_k\}\ne\varnothing, then every ambient-space center z_k has a unique projection x_{k+1}=\operatorname{proj}_{C_k}(z_k), characterized by \langle z_k-x_{k+1},x-x_{k+1}\rangle\le0 for every x\in C_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty closed convex model level set has a unique nearest point to the center.
assumptions_latex: The space is finite-dimensional Euclidean.
X is closed and convex.
m_k is lower semicontinuous and convex.
C_k is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Unique Level Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: False Empty-Level Report Invalidates a Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness for the need to certify model-level infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{0\}\) and \(F(0)=m(0)=0\). For \(\ell=1\),
\[
\{x\in X:m(x)\le\ell\}=\{0\}
\]
is nonempty. If a numerical procedure falsely declares it empty and installs \(\ell\) as a lower bound, the claimed inequality \(1\le\inf_XF=0\) is false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mistakenly declaring a nonempty model level set empty can raise the reported lower bound above the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: The level oracle incorrectly reports infeasibility at \(\ell=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: False Empty-Level Report Invalidates a Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Model Levels and Projection-Distance Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of changing the tested level while holding the model and center fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex model \(m\) on a closed convex set \(X\), define \(C(\ell)=\{x\in X:m(x)\le \ell\}\). If \(\ell_1\le\ell_2\), then \(C(\ell_1)\subseteq C(\ell_2)\). Consequently, whenever \(C(\ell_1)\ne\varnothing\), \[\operatorname{dist}(z,C(\ell_2))\le \operatorname{dist}(z,C(\ell_1))\] for every ambient-space center \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raising a model level enlarges its feasible level set and cannot increase the center's distance to that set.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is closed and convex}.
m\text{ is convex}.
\ell_1\le\ell_2.
C(\ell_1)\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: model sublevel set at level ell

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Model Levels and Projection-Distance Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete level protocol with fixed phase center, exact empty-level response, incumbent improvement, and model refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a convex lower model \(m\le F\), bounds \(L\le F^*\le U\), an incumbent center \(z\in X\), and \(\lambda,\kappa\in(0,1)\). At a phase start set \(\ell=L+\lambda(U-L)\) and keep \(z\) fixed. Repeatedly compute \(x=\operatorname{proj}_{\{v\in X:m(v)\le\ell\}}z\). If the set is certified empty, set \(L\leftarrow\ell\) and restart the phase. Otherwise evaluate \(F(x)\), add an exact supporting cut to \(m\), and, if \(F(x)\le U-\kappa(U-\ell)\), set \(U\leftarrow F(x)\), \(z\leftarrow x\), and restart. Stop when \(U-L\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each phase fixes a target and center, projects onto the evolving model level set, raises the lower bound on certified emptiness, or restarts after sufficient incumbent improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m\le F\) on \(X\), and each oracle call supplies an exact supporting cut.
Projection and empty-level decisions are exact.
\(\lambda,\kappa\in(0,1)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gap Contraction and Inner-Projection Bound for the Phased Level Protocol
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase convergence and projection count under bounded diameter and bounded subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the phased protocol, \(\operatorname{diam}X\le R\), and returned subgradients of norm at most \(G\). In a phase with starting gap \(\Delta=U-L\), each unsuccessful projection evaluation is separated from the next level set by at least \((1-\kappa)(1-\lambda)\Delta/G\). Therefore the phase has at most \(1+R^2G^2/((1-\kappa)^2(1-\lambda)^2\Delta^2)\) unsuccessful projection evaluations. At phase termination, \(\Delta_{p+1}\le q\Delta_p\), where \(q=\max\{1-\lambda,1-\kappa(1-\lambda)\}<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded subgradients and domain diameter make every level phase finite, and each phase contracts the certified gap by a fixed factor.
assumptions_latex: The specified phased level protocol is used.
\(\operatorname{diam}X\le R<\infty\).
Every oracle subgradient has norm at most \(G<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta_{p+1}\le q\Delta_p\text{ with }q<1,\quad\text{and every phase contains finitely many projections}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be a convex Benders lower model on a closed convex set \(X\), let \(L_k\le U_k\) be valid lower and upper bounds, and choose \(\lambda_k\in(0,1)\). Set \(\ell_k=L_k+\lambda_k(U_k-L_k)\) and compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\frac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_2^2:m_k(x)\le\ell_k\right\}.\] If the level set is empty, raise the lower bound consistently with the master model; otherwise evaluate the true recourse value at \(x_{k+1}\), add a valid cut, and update the center according to the level-method acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a target between valid bounds and project the current center onto the master-model sublevel set at that target.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(L_k\le U_k\) are valid bounds and \(\lambda_k\in(0,1)\).
\(m_k\) is a convex lower model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point is the nearest feasible point to \(z_k\) satisfying \(m_k(x_{k+1})\le\ell_k\), unless that level set is empty.

notation.meaning: current certified lower and upper bounds

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the usual level-bundle projection template specialized to a Benders model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and projection template fit Level Master Regularization. However, the statement does not explicitly require z_k to lie in an appropriate ambient space, and the instruction to raise the lower bound consistently does not specify the update. A source is needed to select and state the intended level-method variant.

children.title: Hybrid Proximal-Level Regimes
children.top_down_role: Combined regimes using both proximity control and level restrictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-independent geometry for hybrids using a metric projection onto a model level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C_k=\{x\in X:m_k(x)\le\ell_k\} be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let H_k\succ0. Then \min_{x\in C_k}\tfrac12\|x-z_k\|_{H_k}^2 has a unique solution. This trial-point selection property does not make the stabilized objective a valid lower bound on the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric projection onto a nonempty closed convex model level set is unique, but its stabilization term is not a certified objective bound.
assumptions_latex: C_k is nonempty, closed, and convex.
H_k is positive definite.
z_k belongs to the ambient finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posed Hybrid Level Projection
Hybrid Proximal-Level Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous quadratic stabilization and restriction to a certified model level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\), lower model \(m_k\), center \(z_k\), valid bounds \(L_k\le U_k\), parameters \(\rho_k>0\) and \(\lambda_k\in(0,1)\), set \(\ell_k=L_k+\lambda_k(U_k-L_k)\) and solve \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert x-z_k\rVert_2^2:m_k(x)\le\ell_k\right\}.\] If the level constraint is inactive, the step is proximal; as \(\rho_k\) decreases while the constraint governs the solution, it approaches level stabilization. Evaluate the true subproblem, add its valid cut, and retain unregularized bound accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid master applies a quadratic proximity penalty while restricting trial points to a chosen lower-model level set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(m_k\) is convex.
\(L_k\le U_k\), \(\rho_k>0\), and \(\lambda_k\in(0,1)\).
The selected level set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update combines proximal selection with the certified level restriction \(m_k(x_{k+1})\le\ell_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the hybrid-regime leaf, but hybrid proximal-level methods have non-equivalent master formulations. Moreover, decreasing rho_k in the displayed objective suppresses the proximity term and does not generally approach the stated projection-style level stabilization. An authoritative source is required before choosing the correct formulation and parameter interpretation.

children.title: Regularization-Bias Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where master regularization excessively distorts useful search behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative sufficient condition for regularized minimizers to become unbiased in original objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) attain its minimum at \(x^*\), and let \(r:X\to\mathbb R\) have finite oscillation \(\omega_r:=\sup_Xr-\inf_Xr<\infty\). If \(x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda r(x)\}\) for \(\lambda\ge0\), then \[0\le f(x_\lambda)-f(x^*)\le\lambda\bigl(r(x^*)-\inf_Xr\bigr)\le\lambda\omega_r.\] Hence \(\lambda_k\to0\) implies \(f(x_{\lambda_k})\to\min_Xf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the regularizer has bounded oscillation, original-objective bias is bounded by its weight times that oscillation and vanishes with the weight.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) attains a finite minimum on \(X\).
\(r\) has finite oscillation on \(X\).
\(x_\lambda\) is a minimizer of the regularized objective.

notation.meaning: oscillation of the regularizer over X

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Regularization-Bias Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact distinction between stabilized trial selection and original-problem certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\le F\) on \(X\), let \(r\ge0\), and define
\[
L=\inf_Xm,\qquad \widehat L=\inf_X(m+r).
\]
Then \(L\le\inf_XF\), while \(\widehat L\ge L\) and \(\widehat L\le\inf_XF\) need not hold. Regularization is therefore selection-only when trial points may minimize \(m+r\), but lower bounds and stopping tests use \(L\), the true objective, or another separately valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularizer may select trial points, but its stabilized value is not automatically a valid original-problem bound.
assumptions_latex: \(m(x)\le F(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(r(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\le\inf_XF;\quad\widehat L\le\inf_XF\text{ requires an additional certificate}.

notation.meaning: Unregularized and regularized master optimum values.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Only Regularization Certificate Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Quadratic Regularization Shifts a Unique Optimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth family showing optimizer bias under a fixed nonvanishing regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), and \(r_a(x)=\tfrac12(x-a)^2\) for fixed \(a\ne0\). The original minimizer is \(x^*=0\). For every fixed \(\lambda>0\), the regularized objective \(f+\lambda r_a\) has the unique minimizer
\[
x_\lambda=\frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}a\ne0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed quadratic pull toward a nonoptimal center shifts the optimizer of a smooth strongly convex objective.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Quadratic Regularization Shifts a Unique Optimizer
Regularization-Bias Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias arises when a stabilization objective is mistaken for the original master objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the original problem \(\min_{0\le x\le1}x\), whose solution is \(x^*=0\). With fixed center \(z=1\) and weight \(\rho>1\), the permanently regularized objective \[x+\frac{\rho}{2}(x-1)^2\] has the unique minimizer \(x_\rho=1-\rho^{-1}>0\). Thus a nonvanishing regularizer changes the optimizer if its value is used as the master objective for certification. Regularization is selection-only, and hence unbiased, when original lower bounds and stopping tests use the unregularized model; otherwise asymptotic exactness requires the regularization influence to vanish or an equivalent correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed quadratic stabilizer shifts even a one-dimensional linear optimum unless certification uses the unregularized model or the stabilizer vanishes.
assumptions_latex: The proximal center remains fixed at \(1\).
The regularization weight satisfies \(\rho>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\rho=1-\rho^{-1}\ne x^*\), so persistent uncorrected regularization can bias the reported solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed scalar example directly establishes regularization bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar bias example is correct and failure_boundary is appropriate. The broader assertion that unregularized bounds and stopping tests make regularization unbiased requires algorithmic convergence and center-update conditions not stated here; no source supports those Benders-specific conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex KKT correspondence between a Euclidean trust-region master and a penalized proximal master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, let \(m\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, and suppose \(X\cap\operatorname{dom}m\cap\{x:\|x-z\|_2<\Delta\}\ne\varnothing\). A point \(x^*\) solves \[\min\left\{m(x):x\in X,\ \frac12\|x-z\|_2^2\le\frac12\Delta^2\right\}\] if and only if there is \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[0\in\partial m(x^*)+\lambda(x^*-z)+N_X(x^*),\qquad \lambda(\|x^*-z\|_2^2-\Delta^2)=0.\] For such \(\lambda\), \(x^*\) minimizes \(m(x)+\frac\lambda2\|x-z\|_2^2\) over \(X\); an inactive trust region has \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Slater’s condition, a trust-region master solution is a proximal-master solution for the multiplier of the squared-radius constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is closed and convex, and \(m\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
The restricted master attains its minimum.
A point in \(X\cap\operatorname{dom}m\) lies strictly inside the trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) satisfies the trust-region KKT system and minimizes the proximal objective with weight \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region and Proximal Multiplier Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A specified serious-step trust-region stabilization rule without an independent convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\le F\) on \(X\), \(z_k\in X\) with \(F(z_k)<+\infty\), and \(\Delta_k>0\). Compute \[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{m_k(x):x\in X,\ \|x-z_k\|\le\Delta_k\}.\] If \(p_k:=F(z_k)-m_k(x_k)>0\), evaluate \(F(x_k)\), set \(a_k:=F(z_k)-F(x_k)\) and \(\rho_k:=a_k/p_k\), and add globally valid cuts to form \(m_{k+1}\le F\). For \(0<\eta_1\le\eta_2<1\) and \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\), set \(z_{k+1}=x_k\) if \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), and \(z_{k+1}=z_k\) otherwise. Shrink the radius by \(\gamma_-\) if \(\rho_k<\eta_1\); enlarge it by \(\gamma_+\) if \(\rho_k\ge\eta_2\) and \(\|x_k-z_k\|=\Delta_k\); otherwise leave it unchanged. If \(p_k\le0\), do not form the ratio; termination requires a separately certified global gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the master near a center, compare actual and predicted improvement, accept sufficiently successful trials, and update the radius by fixed thresholds.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k(x)\le F(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
The restricted master attains a solution and the trial objective can be evaluated.
All added Benders cuts are globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rules specify trial selection, the reduction ratio, serious-step updates, and radius updates while excluding an undefined nonpositive-denominator ratio.

notation.meaning: predicted reduction, actual reduction, and their ratio

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Trust-Region Benders Master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted-Master Value Is Not a Global Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-bound convention for a trust-region-restricted Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m_k\le F\) on \(X\), then \[L_k:=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\le\inf_{x\in X}F(x).\] By contrast, \[L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}:=\inf\{m_k(x):x\in X,\ \|x-z_k\|\le\Delta_k\}\] need not lower-bound the unrestricted optimum. For \(X=\mathbb R\), \(F(x)=m_k(x)=x^2\), \(z_k=1\), and \(\Delta_k=1/10\), one has \(L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}=81/100>0=\inf_XF\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unrestricted lower model gives a global lower bound; its trust-region-restricted value generally does not.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a globally valid lower model of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\) is globally valid, whereas \(L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}\) is only a restricted trial-master value in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Value Is Not a Global Lower Bound
Trust-Region Master Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders master stabilization by an adaptive neighborhood around a center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be the current Benders lower model on \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), with center \(z_k\) and radius \(\Delta_k>0\). Compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{m_k(x):\lVert x-z_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\}.\] Evaluate the true objective \(F(x_{k+1})\), add the resulting valid cut, and compare actual reduction with predicted model reduction. Accept a serious step and possibly enlarge \(\Delta_k\) when the ratio meets a prescribed threshold; otherwise keep \(z_k\) and shrink \(\Delta_k\). Compute global lower bounds from the unrestricted master, not from the trust-region-restricted value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict each trial master to a neighborhood of a center, then adapt the radius using agreement between actual and predicted improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and closed, and each restricted master has a solution.
\(m_k\) is a valid lower model of \(F\).
Acceptance and radius-update thresholds are fixed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method stabilizes trial-point selection while preserving valid global bounds through the unrestricted master.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard trust-region stabilization pattern applied to a cutting-plane master

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Trust-Region Master Regularization, but actual and predicted reductions, the serious-step center update, and radius thresholds are not defined precisely. No authoritative source is cited for this stabilized-Benders variant or its global-bound convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certification requirements after a warm-started solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:Wy=h-Tx,\ y\in K\},\] a returned tuple \((y,u,s)\) is an exact current-parameter optimality certificate only if \[Wy=h-Tx,\qquad y\in K,\qquad s=q-W^\top u\in K^*,\qquad \langle y,s\rangle=0.\] These conditions imply \(q^\top y=(h-Tx)^\top u=Q(x)\), so \(\theta\ge(h-T\xi)^\top u\) is valid for every \(\xi\) and exact at \(x\). A tuple certified only for the preceding parameter is not thereby certified at \(x\); nonzero residuals require explicit error analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm-started result must be revalidated against the new right-hand side, cones, dual stationarity, and complementarity before certifying a cut.
assumptions_latex: The displayed primal-dual sign convention is used.
Exact certification is claimed; approximate residuals require separate error bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Current-parameter primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and zero complementarity certify the cut; warm-start status alone does not.

notation.meaning: returned primal variable, equality multiplier, and dual slack

knowledge_statements.title: Current-Parameter Revalidation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm starting as initialization without a solver-independent repair claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For consecutive conic subproblems \(P(x_k)\) and \(P(x_{k+1})\) having the same variable spaces, cone blocks, and solver representation, a stored primal-dual state \(w_k=(y_k,u_k,s_k)\) may initialize the solve at \(x_{k+1}\). Any projection, scaling, or interior displacement required by the chosen solver belongs to its initialization map \(R_{k+1}\), so the new solve starts from \(R_{k+1}(w_k)\). No universal map is implied, and the transferred state need not be feasible or optimal for \(P(x_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm starting transfers a compatible old solver state as initialization; solver-specific repair does not automatically preserve certification.
assumptions_latex: The consecutive problems use compatible variables, cone blocks, and solver representations.
The chosen solver accepts an initialization map for the transferred state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{k+1}(w_k)\) is an initial iterate, not a certificate for the new subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatible Solver-State Transfer
Warm-Started Conic Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of nearby conic primal-dual states without relaxing certification requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider successive conic subproblems parameterized by master points \(x_k\), with primal-dual solutions or iterates \((y_k,s_k)\). When solving the problem at \(x_{k+1}\), a warm start may initialize the conic solver from a repaired or interiorized transformation of \((y_k,s_k)\). Regardless of initialization, a Benders cut may be certified only after the returned primal-dual point satisfies the required feasibility, cone-membership, and duality-gap tolerances for the new parameter. Thus warm starting can reduce numerical work, but it does not by itself establish cut validity or permit reuse of an old dual certificate without revalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearby conic solves may reuse repaired primal-dual iterates, but every new cut still requires feasibility and gap validation for the new parameter.
assumptions_latex: Successive subproblems share compatible cone and variable structure.
The solver can repair or interiorize the transferred state.
Cut construction uses a certificate validated for the current parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Warm starting changes initialization and computational effort, not the mathematical conditions required for a valid Benders cut.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solver initialization cannot replace validation of a current primal-dual certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the topic and the distinction between initialization and current-parameter certification is plausible. However, conic warm-start repair, interiorization, and the feasibility and duality-gap conditions needed for a valid Benders cut are solver- and formulation-dependent, and no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reusable Dual Feasibility under Right-Hand-Side Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cut-reuse fact for right-hand-side-parametric recourse, not a warm-start method for conic solver states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:Wy=h-Tx,\ y\in K\},\] the dual feasible set \[D=\{\pi:q-W^\top\pi\in K^*\}\] is independent of \(x\). Thus every stored \(\pi\in D\) yields \[Q(x')\ge(h-Tx')^\top\pi\] for every new parameter \(x'\). Equality at \(x'\) additionally requires attainment of the dual optimum there and zero duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An old dual-feasible multiplier remains a valid cut generator when only the right-hand side changes, but this is cut reuse rather than solver-state warm starting.
assumptions_latex: The cone, recourse matrix, and cost do not change between parameters.
\(q-W^\top\pi\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Dual Feasibility under Right-Hand-Side Changes

intermediate_metadata.reason: The Builder’s sole new record is mathematically sound but misplaced: reusable dual feasibility is cut reuse, not the defining warm-start operation. The leaf therefore lacks accepted core content on state transfer and revalidation. Master stabilization and parallel scheduling are excluded as sibling methods.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized per-round wall time and work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With one worker per block, block times t_s, communication time t_{\mathrm{comm}}, and master-update time t_{\mathrm{master}}, a synchronous round takes \max_s t_s+t_{\mathrm{comm}}+t_{\mathrm{master}} under the stated cost accounting, while block-solution work is \sum_s t_s.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous wall time is governed by the slowest block, while total block work remains additive.
assumptions_latex: At least S workers are available.
The stated communication and master times include synchronization overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Parallel Evaluation Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness invariant for a common broadcast master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluating every independent block at the same master point x^k and then collecting all returned valid block cuts produces the same block values, certificates, and updated master as evaluating those blocks serially at x^k, provided collection order does not alter cut coefficients or the master formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel evaluation at one common master point changes execution order, not the mathematical Benders update.
assumptions_latex: All blocks receive the same x^k.
Block solves are independent and deterministic up to equivalent valid certificates.
All returned cuts are collected before the next master solve.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Parallel–Serial Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block representation enabling concurrent evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Q(x)=\inf\{\sum_{s=1}^S q_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s-h_s+T_sx\in K_s\ (s=1,\ldots,S)\}, with no cross-block recourse constraints, then Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S Q_s(x) whenever the extended-real sum is well defined. The block values and their certificates may therefore be computed concurrently at a common master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncoupled conic recourse equals the sum of independent block values and permits concurrent evaluation.
assumptions_latex: Recourse variables and constraints are uncoupled after fixing x.
The extended-real sum has no indeterminate form.

notation.meaning: Value function of recourse block s

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Recourse Decomposition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled Recourse Does Not Equal the Sum of Independent Block Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit separability boundary for independent parallel evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
Q=\min\{y_1+y_2:y_1\ge0,\ y_2\ge0,\ y_1+y_2\ge1\}.
\]
Then \(Q=1\). If the coupling inequality is omitted and the variables are optimized as independent blocks, then
\[
Q_1=\min_{y_1\ge0}y_1=0,\qquad Q_2=\min_{y_2\ge0}y_2=0,
\]
so \(Q_1+Q_2=0\ne Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-block constraint can make the sum of separately optimized block values strictly smaller than the true recourse value.
assumptions_latex: Independent block evaluation omits the coupling constraint \(y_1+y_2\ge1\).

notation.meaning: Coupled recourse value and independently computed block values.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Recourse Does Not Equal the Sum of Independent Block Minima

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous admission of globally valid cuts computed at tagged earlier master points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At master version \(k\), broadcast \((k,x^k)\) to available block workers. Worker \(s\) returns a globally valid cut \(\theta_s\ge\ell_s(x)\) tagged by its evaluation version \(\tau\le k\). Admit it only when its coefficients and validity certificate correspond to \(x^\tau\). Because \(\ell_s(x)\le Q_s(x)\) globally, it may be installed at a later version. Re-solve after a declared batch, timeout, or arrival event; never use a stale local value as an unverified value at the current point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous workers return globally valid version-tagged cuts; stale cuts remain admissible, but stale values are not current incumbent values.
assumptions_latex: \ell_s(x)\le Q_s(x)\quad\forall x.
\text{Returned coefficients correspond to the tagged evaluation}.
\text{Stale block values are not used as an unverified current upper bound}.

notation.meaning: master version at which the block was evaluated
returned affine lower cut for block s

knowledge_statements.title: Tagged Asynchronous Block-Cut Admission

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination certificate using complete block values at one common incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k\) be the globally solved value of a Benders master containing only valid cuts. If \(\bar x\in X\) has finite certified values \(Q_s(\bar x)\) for every block, set \(U_k=c^\top\bar x+\sum_sQ_s(\bar x)\). Then \(L_k\le v^\star\le U_k\), so \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of \(\bar x\). Values evaluated at different tagged points cannot generally be combined into this upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid master lower bound and complete block evaluation of one common incumbent give an optimality-gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: \text{The master is solved globally and contains only valid cuts}.
\text{Every block value in }U_k\text{ is certified at the same feasible point }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le v^\star\le U_k,\qquad U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow\bar x\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Master–Incumbent Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling condition for asynchronous or partial-batch parallel Benders protocols.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An asynchronous protocol is \(D\)-fair if every block is dispatched infinitely often and each dispatch made at version \(k\) is resolved by an admissible cut or certified terminal block status no later than version \(k+D\). If every exact evaluation of a persistently violated block returns a separating cut, this condition prevents that block's separation from being postponed indefinitely solely by scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every block is revisited, and every dispatched result is resolved within a bounded number of master versions.
assumptions_latex: D<\infty.
\text{Exact evaluation of a persistently violated block returns an admissible separating cut}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Persistent block violation}\Longrightarrow\text{a corresponding result is processed after finitely many versions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Delay Fairness Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Domain Convergence of Fair Asynchronous Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of tagged asynchronous block-cut admission on a finite master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite. Suppose all admitted block cuts are globally valid and retained, every master is solved globally, and a \(D\)-fair scheduler processes each dispatched block result within finitely many master versions. Assume that whenever a selected \(x\in X\) is nonoptimal, some exact block evaluation dispatched at \(x\) eventually returns a cut after whose admission \(x\) cannot solve any subsequent retained-cut master. Then only finitely many nonoptimal master points are selected. Eventually every selected master point is globally optimal; a complete common-point block evaluation then permits the master–incumbent gap test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite master domain, retained separating cuts and fair bounded-delay processing prevent endless reselection of nonoptimal points.
assumptions_latex: \(|X|<\infty\).
\text{All admitted cuts are globally valid and retained}.
\text{Every master is solved globally}.
\text{Scheduling is }D\text{-fair}.
\text{Every selected nonoptimal point is eventually permanently excluded from master optimality by an admitted cut}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k_0<\infty\ \text{such that every master point selected after }k_0\text{ is globally optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Convergence of Fair Asynchronous Benders

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous round with status collection, common-point incumbent construction, master update, and stopping order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a globally solved master point \(x^k\), broadcast it to every block and wait for certified statuses. For each feasible finite block, collect its exact value and an attained dual cut; for each certifiably infeasible block, collect and add a valid feasibility cut. An unbounded or indeterminate block status precludes an unsupported incumbent or gap certificate and must be reported or resolved. If all blocks are feasible and finite, form \(U(x^k)=c^Tx^k+\sum_sQ_s(x^k)\) and update the incumbent. Install all returned valid cuts, solve the updated master globally to obtain \(L_{k+1}\), and stop only if the stored common-point incumbent satisfies \(U_k-L_{k+1}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous round waits for every certified block status, forms an incumbent only from complete common-point values, installs all valid cuts, resolves the master, and then tests the gap.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible finite block supplies a certified value and valid cut.
Every block declared infeasible supplies a valid feasibility certificate.
The master is solved globally.
Indeterminate or unbounded statuses are not treated as finite values.

notation.meaning: Certified incumbent upper bound and master lower bound

knowledge_statements.title: Status-Complete Synchronous Multi-Subproblem Benders Round

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Retained-Cut Asynchronous Benders on a Compact Convex Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-domain convergence under exact supporting cuts, bounded delay, fairness, retention, and compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact and convex and \(F(x)=c^Tx+\sum_{s=1}^SQ_s(x)\), where each \(Q_s\) is finite, convex, and continuous on \(X\). Suppose every exact block evaluation returns a supporting affine minorant, all admitted cuts are retained, every master is solved globally, scheduling is bounded-delay fair, and every selected master point is eventually completely evaluated. With best-incumbent upper bounds formed only from complete common-point evaluations, the master lower bounds converge upward to \(F^*=\min_XF\), every accumulation point of completely evaluated master points is optimal, and the incumbent–master gap converges to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact convex domain, exact retained supporting cuts and fair bounded-delay processing yield convergence of asynchronous multi-block Benders.

If a subproblem is infeasible, add the feasibility cut supplied by a dual improving ray. Re-solve the master minimizing \(c^\top x+\sum_s\theta_s\) over \(x\in X\). Stop when its lower bound and a feasible incumbent upper bound differ by at most the prescribed tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination under an exact finite cut library and strict cut-generation progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the original feasible epigraph has an exact description by a finite library \(\mathcal C\) of globally valid feasibility and optimality cuts. A Benders method starts with \(\mathcal C_0\subseteq\mathcal C\), retains every generated cut, globally solves each well-posed master, and at every nonterminal master optimizer adds at least one violated cut in \(\mathcal C\) not already retained. If the original problem has an attained finite optimum and every intermediate master has a global optimizer, the method terminates at a global optimum after at most \(|\mathcal C\setminus\mathcal C_0|\) cut-adding iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact Benders method cannot make more strict cut-generation steps than the number of omitted cuts in its finite exact library.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infinite-Support Boundary for Exact Global Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why finite affine outer approximations cannot reproduce genuinely nonpolyhedral recourse globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every finite maximum \(m(x)=\max_{1\le i\le N}(a_ix+b_i)\) is piecewise affine. Therefore \(Q(x)=x^2\) on \([-1,1]\) cannot equal such an \(m\) throughout the interval. Consequently, finitely many affine supporting cuts cannot globally complete the epigraph of \(Q\), even though valid lower and upper bounds may approach one another to a prescribed positive tolerance under additional convergence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A genuinely curved recourse function cannot be represented globally by finitely many affine supporting cuts, so exact epigraph completion may require infinitely many cuts.
assumptions_latex: The outer approximation contains finitely many affine supporting cuts.
Exact global completion means equality with \(Q\) throughout the master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)=x^2\) on \([-1,1]\) has no finite maximum-of-affine representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kelley-type convergence under conditions ensuring a certified positive-tolerance gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(F(x)=c^\top x+Q(x)\), and suppose \(Q\) is finite, convex, and Lipschitz on an open neighborhood of \(X\). Initialize \(m_0\) with at least one exact affine support of \(Q\). At iteration \(k\), let \(m_k\) be the maximum of all retained supports, choose \[x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+m_k(x)\},\] evaluate \(Q(x^k)\), retain an exact supporting cut at \(x^k\), and set \[L_k=c^\top x^k+m_k(x^k),\qquad U_k=\min_{0\le i\le k}F(x^i).\] If every master is solved globally, then \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\), \(L_k\to v^*\), and \(U_k\to v^*\). Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some finite iteration satisfies \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, exact retained supports and globally solved masters reach every positive certified tolerance for locally Lipschitz convex recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and compact.
\(Q\) is finite, convex, and Lipschitz on an open neighborhood of \(X\).

The initial model contains at least one exact affine support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\to v^*,\qquad U_k\to v^*,\qquad \forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists k<\infty:\ U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound lower cuts and incumbent upper evaluations obtained from certified inexact recourse oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each scenario \(s\), suppose an oracle queried at \(x^k\) returns \((\widetilde q_{s,k},g_{s,k},\eta_{s,k},\delta_{s,k})\), with \(\eta_{s,k},\delta_{s,k}\ge0\), such that for every master point \(x\), \[Q_s(x)\ge \widetilde q_{s,k}+g_{s,k}^\top(x-x^k)-\eta_{s,k},\qquad Q_s(x^k)\le\widetilde q_{s,k}+\delta_{s,k}.\] The shifted affine function is a valid master cut, and \(\widetilde q_{s,k}+\delta_{s,k}\) is a valid scenario upper evaluation at the incumbent. Aggregation gives \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\); hence \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified lower-oracle errors shift approximate cuts downward, while certified upper errors inflate incumbent evaluations; together they give a sound completion gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: False Completion from an Invalid Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Premature termination when an overestimated master value is treated as a certified lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{0\le x\le1}x\), whose value is \(v^*=0\). The feasible incumbent \(\bar x=1\) gives the valid upper bound \(U=1\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with a valid incumbent upper bound, an overestimated master lower bound can create a false zero gap and return a suboptimal point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: False Completion from an Infeasible Incumbent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalid upper-bound mechanism caused by an infeasible reported incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:x\ge1\}\), whose value is \(v^*=1\). If the infeasible point \(\bar x=0\) is treated as an incumbent with reported value \(U=0\), while the valid relaxation \(x\ge0\) supplies \(L=0\), then \(U-L=0\) declares completion although \(\bar x\) is infeasible and \(U<v^*\).

False-Completion Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Premature termination caused by treating an uncertified estimate as an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{0\le x\le1}Q(x)\) with \(Q(x)=(x-1)^2\). Its optimum is \(0\) at \(x=1\). At \(x^0=0\), suppose an inexact oracle incorrectly reports \(\widetilde Q(0)=0\) with zero error, although \(Q(0)=1\). The valid constant lower cut \(Q(x)\ge0\) gives master bound \(L_0=0\), while the reported value is used as \(U_0=0\). A zero reported gap then declares completion and may return \(x^0=0\), whose true suboptimality is \(1\). Thus completion fails precisely when an uncertified evaluation is admitted as a feasible upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero reported gap can be false when an underestimated, uncertified recourse value is used as the incumbent upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The stopping rule accepts \(\widetilde Q(x^k)\) as an upper bound without a certified error enclosure.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the block problem \[v^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in C_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\right\},\] associate \(\lambda\in Y\) with the linking equality. The Lagrangian dual function separates as \[g(\lambda)=-\langle\lambda,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in C_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_i x_i\rangle\bigr),\] and the Lagrangian dual problem is \(\sup_{\lambda\in Y}g(\lambda)\). Weak duality gives \(g(\lambda)\le v^*\) for every \(\lambda\in Y\). If \(v^*\) is finite and \(b\in\operatorname{ri}\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i(\operatorname{dom}h_i)\bigr)\), where \(h_i=f_i+\delta_{C_i}\), then there is no duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the linking equality separates the problem into independent block infima. Every multiplier gives a lower bound, and the stated finite-dimensional relative-interior condition yields equality of the primal and dual optimal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Variable Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent block formulation using local copies and consensus constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original problem be \(\inf_z\sum_{i=1}^mf_i(z)\) over \(z\in\bigcap_iC_i\). Introduce a global variable \(z\) and local copies \(z_i\). Dualizing the equalities \(z_i=z\) produces independent local infima; minimization over the unrestricted global variable additionally imposes \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\) on the consensus multipliers.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[v^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x_i):\sum_iA_{i,R}x_i=b_R,\ \sum_iA_{i,N}x_i=b_N\right\}.\] Retain \(\sum_iA_{i,N}x_i=b_N\) and dualize only \(\sum_iA_{i,R}x_i=b_R\). For \(\lambda_R\in Y_R\), define \[g_R(\lambda_R)=\inf_{\sum_iA_{i,N}x_i=b_N}\left\{\sum_i h_i(x_i)+\left\langle\lambda_R,\sum_iA_{i,R}x_i-b_R\right\rangle\right\}.\] Then \(g_R(\lambda_R)\le v^*\). Let \(G_N\) have one vertex for each block and join two blocks when some retained row has a nonzero coefficient in both blocks. Because no retained row connects distinct connected components of \(G_N\), the infimum defining \(g_R\) decomposes into one independent subproblem per connected component. If \(b_R\) belongs to the relative interior of \[\left\{\sum_iA_{i,R}x_i:x_i\in\operatorname{dom}h_i,\ \sum_iA_{i,N}x_i=b_N\right\},\] then \(\sup_{\lambda_R\in Y_R}g_R(\lambda_R)=v^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Block Dual Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable oracle for a Lagrangian dual value and supergradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a supplied multiplier \(\lambda\), block \(i\) independently computes \[\phi_i(\lambda)=\inf_{x_i\in C_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_ix_i\rangle\bigr)\] and returns a minimizer \(x_i(\lambda)\). The coordinator forms \(g(\lambda)=-\langle\lambda,b\rangle+\sum_i\phi_i(\lambda)\) and \(r(\lambda)=\sum_iA_ix_i(\lambda)-b\). If every infimum is attained, \(r(\lambda)\) is a supergradient of the concave dual function: for every \(\mu\), \(g(\mu)\le g(\lambda)+\langle r(\lambda),\mu-\lambda\rangle\).

The coupling has the form \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\).

Parallel Block Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel evaluation of all separable Lagrangian blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a common multiplier \(\lambda^k\) and dispatch it to all \(m\) block workers. Worker \(i\) solves its local Lagrangian problem and returns \((\phi_i(\lambda^k),x_i^k)\). After all required replies arrive, reduce the results by summation to obtain \[g(\lambda^k)=-\langle\lambda^k,b\rangle+\sum_i\phi_i(\lambda^k),\qquad r^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b.\] Output the dual value and supergradient pair \((g(\lambda^k),r^k)\). The synchronized evaluation is mathematically identical to serial evaluation because no block input depends on another block's result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast one multiplier, solve every independent block concurrently, and sum their values and residual contributions into the same oracle result as serial evaluation.
assumptions_latex: All blocks receive the same multiplier \(\lambda^k\).
Every local solve is exact and returns before aggregation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-path and work costs for exact synchronous evaluation of separable Lagrangian blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If broadcast completes before all block evaluations begin, reduction begins after every block evaluation finishes, worker \(i\) takes time \(T_i\), and enough workers execute all blocks simultaneously, then \[T_{\mathrm{par}}=T_{\mathrm{broadcast}}+\max_{1\le i\le m}T_i+T_{\mathrm{red}}(m).\] The aggregate work is \(\sum_{i=1}^m W_i+W_{\mathrm{red}}(m)\). Thus parallel scheduling reduces critical-path time but does not change the exact oracle or its aggregate work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With enough workers and sequential broadcast, evaluation, and reduction phases, latency is governed by the slowest block plus communication and reduction, while work remains additive.
assumptions_latex: All exact block evaluations are independent after receiving the common multiplier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified additive-error condition for a separable dual oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At multiplier \(\lambda\), let block \(i\) return \(\widetilde x_i\in C_i\) satisfying \[f_i(\widetilde x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_i\widetilde x_i\rangle\le\phi_i(\lambda)+\varepsilon_i,\qquad \varepsilon_i\ge0.\] Define \(\widetilde g=-\langle\lambda,b\rangle+\sum_i(f_i(\widetilde x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_i\widetilde x_i\rangle)\), \(\widetilde r=\sum_iA_i\widetilde x_i-b\), and \(E=\sum_i\varepsilon_i\). Then \(g(\lambda)\le\widetilde g\le g(\lambda)+E\), and for every \(\mu\), \(g(\mu)\le g(\lambda)+\langle\widetilde r,\mu-\lambda\rangle+E\). Thus \(\widetilde r\) is an \(E\)-supergradient.

assumptions_latex: Every local approximate point \(\widetilde x_i\) is block-feasible.
Each error bound \(\varepsilon_i\) is finite and certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate oracle error is at most \(E=\sum_i\varepsilon_i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected supergradient ascent on a concave Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\lambda^0\in D\), where \(D\) is the closed convex multiplier domain. At iteration \(k\), evaluate the block oracle to obtain a dual supergradient \(r^k\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\), and update \[\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_D(\lambda^k+\alpha_kr^k).\] Record the best dual value and any recovered primal feasible incumbent. Stop when a verified primal-dual gap meets tolerance or another prescribed budget is exhausted. If the dual optimum is attained, supergradients are bounded, \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then the best dual values converge to the dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate block residuals, take projected multiplier-ascent steps, and use diminishing nonsummable steps to obtain convergence of best dual values.
assumptions_latex: The dual optimum is finite and attained on \(D\).
Oracle supergradients are uniformly bounded.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon objective guarantee for projected supergradient coordination on a concave Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be closed and convex, let \(g:D\to\mathbb R\) be concave, and let \(\lambda^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\lambda\in D}g(\lambda)\). If \(r^k\in\partial^+g(\lambda^k)\), \(\|r^k\|\le G\), and \(\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_D(\lambda^k+\alpha_k r^k)\) with \(\alpha_k>0\), then for every \(N\ge1\), \[g(\lambda^\star)-\max_{0\le k<N}g(\lambda^k)\le\frac{\|\lambda^0-\lambda^\star\|^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k}.\] If a horizon \(N\) and a bound \(R\ge\|\lambda^0-\lambda^\star\|\) are known, the choice \(\alpha_k=R/(G\sqrt N)\) gives an upper bound \(RG/\sqrt N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected supergradient coordination has the standard weighted best-iterate guarantee and an order-one-over-square-root-of-N dual-objective rate under a horizon-tuned constant step.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is closed and convex and \(g\) is concave on \(D\).
A dual maximizer \(\lambda^\star\in D\) exists.
\(r^k\in\partial^+g(\lambda^k)\) and \(\|r^k\|\le G\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let [1m[0m\(\bar\lambda_k=\bar\lambda\) for all sufficiently large [1m[0m\(k\), and suppose the proximal trials satisfy [1m[0m\(t_k\downarrow0\). Consequently continuity of [1m[0m\(q\) at [1m[0m\(\bar\lambda\) implies [1m[0m\(q(\lambda^{k+1})-q(\bar\lambda)\to0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Augmentation Generally Destroys Original Block Separability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary of direct augmented-Lagrangian coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=\sum_iA_ix_i-b\), \[\frac\rho2\|r(x)\|^2=\frac\rho2\sum_i\|A_ix_i\|^2+\rho\sum_{i<j}\langle A_ix_i,A_jx_j\rangle-\rho\sum_i\langle A_ix_i,b\rangle+\frac\rho2\|b\|^2.\] Hence the augmented primal minimization is block-separable only when the cross terms vanish on the relevant domains or an additional splitting reformulation is introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared aggregate residual creates cross-block terms, so ordinary augmented-Lagrangian minimization is generally not separable across the original blocks.
assumptions_latex: All \(A_ix_i\) lie in a common Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle A_ix_i,A_jx_j\rangle\not\equiv0\) for some \(i\ne j\) prevents additive block separability of the quadratic penalty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable stationarity certificate induced by an exact or controlled-inexact inner solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be proper closed convex, \(r(x)=Ax-b\), and
\[
L_\rho(x,\lambda)=F(x)+\langle\lambda,r(x)\rangle+\frac\rho2\|r(x)\|_2^2.
\]
If \(x^+\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial_xL_\rho(x^+,\lambda)\right)\le\eta
\]
and \(\lambda^+=\lambda+\rho r(x^+)\), then
\[
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial F(x^+)+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda^+\right)\le\eta.
\]
Consequently, this stationarity distance together with \(\|r(x^+)\|\) gives a reproducible approximate KKT test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After the multiplier update, the augmented inner-solve stationarity residual is the ordinary Lagrangian stationarity residual up to the declared inner error.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper closed convex.
\(r(x)=Ax-b\), \(\rho>0\), and the quadratic penalty uses the Euclidean norm.
The distance is evaluated in the same primal stationarity norm used for the certified inner error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex equality-constrained convergence with a fixed positive penalty and exact inner solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper closed convex and consider \(\min\{F(x):Ax=b\}\). Assume primal and dual solutions exist. Fix \(\rho>0\), choose
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x L_\rho(x,\lambda^k),\qquad
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b),
\]
and assume every inner minimum is attained. Then \(\lambda^k\) converges to a dual solution, \(Ax^{k+1}-b\to0\), and every cluster point of \(x^{k+1}\) is primal optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact inner minimization, fixed positive penalty, and nonempty primal and dual solution sets, multipliers converge, feasibility residuals vanish, and all primal cluster points are optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper closed convex on a finite-dimensional space.
The primal and dual solution sets are nonempty.
\(\rho>0\) is fixed and every augmented-Lagrangian inner minimum is attained exactly.

Then \lambda^k converges to a dual maximizer and r(x^{k+1})\to0.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian lower-bound certificate for a decomposed convex minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(X_i\) be a nonempty set, let \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(A_i\) be a linear map into a common finite-dimensional real inner-product space containing \(b\). Define \(p^\star=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m A_ix_i=b\}\). For any multiplier \(\lambda\), define \(q(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_ix_i\rangle\}-\langle\lambda,b\rangle\). If finite numbers \(\beta_i\) satisfy \(\beta_i\le\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_ix_i\rangle\}\), then \(B(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m\beta_i-\langle\lambda,b\rangle\le q(\lambda)\le p^\star\). Thus \((\lambda,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)\) is a global lower-bound certificate whenever the component inequalities are independently verifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a decomposed equality-constrained minimization problem, a multiplier and verified lower bounds for all Lagrangian subproblems combine into a valid global lower bound on the primal optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\) is nonempty for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
Each \(\beta_i\in\mathbb R\) is independently verified as a lower bound for its displayed Lagrangian subproblem.
The inner products and linear maps \(A_i\) are defined in compatible finite-dimensional real spaces.

Thus its objective value is generally an upper bound on \(\phi_i(\lambda)\), not a valid certified lower bound \(\beta_i\). knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Duality Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real duality gap for a primal minimization problem and its Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\). Define \(p^\star=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0\}\), \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle\}\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(d^\star=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}q(\lambda)\). Whenever \(p^\star-d^\star\) is defined in extended-real arithmetic, the Lagrangian duality gap is \(g=p^\star-d^\star\). Weak duality gives \(d^\star\le p^\star\), hence \(g\in[0,+\infty]\). The gap is zero when \(p^\star=d^\star\in\mathbb R\), and it is positive and finite when \(p^\star,d^\star\in\mathbb R\) and \(p^\star>d^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian duality gap is the defined extended-real difference between the primal optimal value and the best dual value. Weak duality makes it nonnegative; equality of finite optimal values gives zero gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\).
The extended-real difference \(p^\star-d^\star\) is defined; in particular, the indeterminate forms \((+\infty)-(+\infty)\) and \((-\infty)-(-\infty)\) are excluded.
