knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrary Dual-Optimal Minimizer Need Not Recover a Primal Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of last-iterate recovery despite zero gap and an attained optimal multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{0:x=0,\ -1\le x\le1\}\). Its Lagrangian is \(L(x,\lambda)=\lambda x\), and \(q(\lambda)=-|\lambda|\). Thus \(p^\star=d^\star=0\) and \(\lambda^\star=0\) is dual optimal. Nevertheless, every \(x\in[-1,1]\) minimizes \(L(\cdot,0)\). Therefore the valid selection \(x^k=1\) at \(\lambda^k=0\) is Lagrangian-minimizing for every \(k\) but never satisfies the coupling equality \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero gap and an attained optimal multiplier do not make an arbitrary Lagrangian minimizer primal feasible; a valid constant selection can defeat last-iterate recovery forever.
assumptions_latex: The recovery rule may select any minimizer of \(L(\cdot,\lambda^k)\).
The multiplier sequence is fixed at the dual optimum \(\lambda^k=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Dual-Optimal Minimizer Need Not Recover a Primal Point
Primal-Recovery Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual optimality alone does not make arbitrary Lagrangian subproblem minimizers primal feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider [1m[0m\(\min\{0:x=0,\ -1\le x\le1\}\). Its Lagrangian is [1m[0m\(L(x,\lambda)=\lambda x\), and the dual function is [1m[0m\(q(\lambda)=\inf_{|x|\le1}\lambda x=-|\lambda|\). Hence [1m[0m\(p^\star=d^\star=0\) and [1m[0m\(\lambda^\star=0\) is dual optimal. Nevertheless, [1m[0m\(L(x,0)=0\) for every [1m[0m\(x\in[-1,1]\), so the valid subproblem selection [1m[0m\(x^k=1\) for all [1m[0m\(k\) never satisfies the coupling equation. Thus last-iterate recovery from arbitrary Lagrangian minimizers can fail even with zero duality gap and an attained optimal multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even at an attained dual optimum with zero gap, arbitrary subproblem minimizers may remain infeasible; selecting the same nonfeasible minimizer defeats last-iterate recovery.
assumptions_latex: The recovery rule selects an arbitrary minimizer of \(L(\cdot,\lambda^k)\).
The multiplier sequence is fixed at the dual optimum \(\lambda^k=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k=1\) is Lagrangian-minimizing for every \(k\) but violates \(x=0\), so last-iterate primal recovery fails.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind fits Primal-Recovery Failure, and the example correctly shows that arbitrary Lagrangian minimizers at an attained dual optimum need not be primal feasible. It lacks a cited source and contains invalid `[1m[0m` artifacts.

children.title: Scenario Decomposition for Conic Models
children.top_down_role: Conic-specific scenario formulations and coordination methods; probability modeling, scenario generation, and general stochastic-programming foundations remain outside this chapter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Closedness Boundary of Scenario Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex structure and its projection boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex \(K_s\), the partial-infimum function \(Q_s\) is convex wherever it does not take \(-\infty\); consequently \(c^\top x+\sum_sp_sQ_s(x)\) is convex for \(p_s\ge0\) on its well-defined domain. Closed cones alone do not guarantee that \(Q_s\) is closed, finite, or attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic recourse is convex under the proper-value regime, but may be nonclosed, infinite, or unattained.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_s\) is convex.
No scenario value equals \(-\infty\) on the stated convex-function domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_s\text{ is convex, while closedness, finiteness, and attainment require additional assumptions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Closedness Boundary of Scenario Recourse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent first-stage value-function representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(Q_s(x)=\inf\{q_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s+T_sx-h_s\in K_s\}\), using \(+\infty\) for infeasibility and \(-\infty\) for unboundedness below. Wherever the finite weighted extended-real sum is defined, partial minimization gives \(\inf_{Ax-b\in K_0}\{c^\top x+\sum_sp_sQ_s(x)\}\). Recovery of an extensive-form optimizer requires attainment of the needed scenario infima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating recourse variables gives a first-stage problem with weighted scenario value functions.
assumptions_latex: The weighted extended-real sum is defined at the considered point.
Optimizer recovery requires attainment of each relevant scenario infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Function Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact deterministic-equivalent structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stack \(u=(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{|S|})\), \(K=K_0\times\prod_sK_s\), and \(\bar c=(c,p_1q_1,\ldots,p_{|S|}q_{|S|})\). Then the extensive form is \(\inf\{\bar c^\top u:\mathcal Mu-\bar b\in K\}\), where each scenario row touches only \(x\) and its own \(y_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extensive form is one product-cone program with block-angular sparsity.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
All maps and cones are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Angular Product-Cone Form
Two-Stage Extensive-Form Conic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario, two-stage conic formulation with first-stage decisions shared across scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let scenarios be indexed by \(s\in S\), with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). A two-stage extensive-form conic model is
\[\inf_{x,(y_s)}\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{s\in S}p_s q_s^\top y_s: A x-b\in K_0,\; W_s y_s+T_sx-h_s\in K_s\ \text{for every }s\in S\right\},\]
where \(K_0\) and every \(K_s\) are closed convex cones. The single variable \(x\) enforces identical first-stage action across all scenarios, while each \(y_s\) is scenario-specific recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extensive form combines one shared first-stage decision with probability-weighted, scenario-specific conic recourse decisions and constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
\(K_0\) and \(K_s\) are closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is common to every scenario, whereas each recourse vector \(y_s\) may depend on \(s\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source supports the extensive-form convention or formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space geometry of finite scenario copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(\langle x,y\rangle_p=\sum_sp_sx_s^\top y_s\), define \(N=\{x:x_s=z\ \forall s\}\). Then \((P_Nx)_s=\bar x=\sum_sp_sx_s\), and \(N^{\perp_p}=\{y:\sum_sp_sy_s=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus is the diagonal subspace; weighted projection replaces every copy by the weighted average.
assumptions_latex: All copies lie in one Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Subspace and Weighted Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic Representability of the Copied Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of conic form under copying and consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X_s=\{x_s:\mathcal A_sx_s-b_s\in K_s\}\), the copied model is conic over \(\prod_sK_s\) with linear consensus equalities, and \(\operatorname{proj}_z\{(z,x_s):x_s\in X_s,\ x_s=z\ \forall s\}=\bigcap_sX_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario copying preserves conic form and introduces no relaxation when consensus is enforced.
assumptions_latex: Every \(X_s\) is finitely conic representable.
Consensus identifies the intended common components.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Representability of the Copied Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent finite equality systems for consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(x_s=z\) is equivalent to \(x_s=x_{s_0}\) for all \(s\ne s_0\), and to equality on the edges of any connected scenario graph. A disconnected graph enforces consensus only within components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A central variable, a reference scenario, or any connected equality graph imposes the same consensus.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite.
Edges identify complete copies in the same space.
knowledge_statements.title: Central and Pairwise Consensus Equivalence
Scenario-Copy Consensus Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-separable reformulation obtained by copying shared decisions and imposing consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scenario functions \(f_s\) and feasible sets \(X_s\), the shared-decision problem
\[\inf_{x}\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in\bigcap_{s\in S}X_s\]
has the scenario-copy representation
\[\inf_{z,(x_s)}\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_s\in X_s,\;x_s=z\ \text{for every }s\in S.\]
Projection of any feasible copied point onto \(z\) gives a feasible shared decision with the same objective, and replication of any feasible \(x\) gives a feasible copied point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared decision can be copied by scenario; equality of every copy to one consensus variable preserves feasible decisions and objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\).
Each \(f_s\) and \(X_s\) is defined on the same finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The shared and scenario-copy formulations have equal optimal values and mutually corresponding feasible solutions.

notation.meaning: scenario copy of the shared decision
scenario feasible set, possibly conic representable

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The consensus-copy equivalence is mathematically coherent and appropriately classified as a representation, but it has no inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Root and Parent-Child Conic Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete node-indexed convention for a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For root \(r\), impose \(A_rx_r-b_r\in K_r\). For every nonroot node \(n\), impose \(A_nx_n+B_nx_{a(n)}-b_n\in K_n\). One decision is assigned to each observed-history node, so all descendant scenarios share that decision before branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The root has its own conic constraint, while each later node is coupled to its parent.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite and rooted.
Every \(K_n\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_n\text{ is common to all paths passing through node }n.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Root and Parent-Child Conic Form

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent expected-cost conventions on a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_\ell\) be leaf probabilities, \(C_n(x_n)\) the incremental node costs, and \(\pi_n=\sum_{\ell:n\preceq\ell}p_\ell\). Then \(\sum_\ell p_\ell\sum_{n\preceq\ell}C_n(x_n)=\sum_n\pi_nC_n(x_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected path cost equals reach-probability-weighted node cost.
assumptions_latex: The tree is finite.
Each node cost occurs once on each path containing that node.

notation.meaning: Node n lies on the path to leaf ell.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Probability and Leaf-Probability Objective Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of node decisions and leaf copies with history equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Give every leaf \(\ell\) a stage-\(t\) copy \(x_{t,\ell}\), and equate copies whenever the leaves share their stage-\(t\) history. Each equality class is the descendant set of one stage-\(t\) node. Replacing each class by one node variable preserves path constraints and expected costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History equalities collapse leafwise copies exactly into one variable per scenario-tree node.
assumptions_latex: Nodes represent distinct observed histories.
Path and node forms use identical local data.

notation.meaning: Equality of copies with the same observed history.

knowledge_statements.title: Node and Path-Copy Formulation Equivalence
Multistage Scenario-Tree Conic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-based conic extensive form for a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal T=(N,E)\) be a finite rooted scenario tree, and let \(a(n)\) denote the parent of each nonroot node. A node-based multistage conic model has the form
\[\inf_{(x_n)}\sum_{n\in N}\pi_n c_n^\top x_n\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_nx_n+B_nx_{a(n)}-b_n\in K_n\quad(n\ne r),\]
with an analogous root constraint involving only \(x_r\). Here \(x_n\) is chosen after observing the history represented by node \(n\); hence all terminal scenarios passing through \(n\) use the same decision \(x_n\), which enforces nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage conic model assigns one decision to each scenario-tree node and couples it conically to its parent, automatically sharing decisions across identical histories.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is a finite rooted tree with node probabilities \(\pi_n\ge0\).
Every \(K_n\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node indexing enforces equality of decisions for scenarios sharing the same observed history.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The node-indexed representation fits the leaf, but the root constraint is only described as analogous and no source establishes the precise model convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic probability-consistency condition rather than a locally owned representation result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \pi_r=1,\qquad \pi_n=\sum_{m\in\operatorname{ch}(n)}\pi_m.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node's reach probability equals the sum of its children's probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The tree is finite and probabilities are normalized.
knowledge_statements.title: Reach-Probability Recursion

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf owns the complete root/parent-child node model, history-class equivalence, and node-versus-leaf expected-cost representation. Generic probability recursion is deferred to Probability-Weight Consistency; two-stage specialization, generic consensus, and malformed-history pathology are excluded.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp condition for selected pairwise equalities to enforce classwise agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If equality rows correspond to edges of a graph \(G=(C,E)\), then they enforce full agreement on \(C\) if and only if \(G\) is connected. In that case \(\operatorname{rank}(B_G\otimes I_d)=(|C|-1)d\); cycle edges are redundant. If \(G\) is disconnected, decisions may differ between connected components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise equalities suffice exactly when they connect every history class; cycles are redundant and disconnected systems are insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(|C|<\infty\).
\(x_s\in\mathbb R^d\) for all \(s\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker(B_G\otimes I_d)=\{\mathbf1_C\otimes u:u\in\mathbb R^d\}\iff G\text{ is connected}.

notation.meaning: oriented incidence matrix of the equality graph

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity and Redundancy Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-minimal explicit equality construction within finite history classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For history classes \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) and decisions in \(\mathbb R^d\), choose a spanning tree \(T_i\) on each \(C_i\), let \(B_i\) be its oriented incidence matrix, and set \(H=\operatorname{diag}_i(B_i\otimes I_d)\). Then \(Hx=0\) exactly when all decisions agree within each \(C_i\), and \(\operatorname{rank}H=d\sum_i(|C_i|-1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spanning-tree incidence matrix gives a row-minimal explicit nonanticipativity system.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set and history classes are finite.
All decisions in a class belong to the same space \(\mathbb R^d\).

notation.meaning: oriented incidence matrix of the spanning tree on class i

knowledge_statements.title: Spanning-Tree Incidence Construction
Explicit Nonanticipativity Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear equality condition for scenario-indexed decisions sharing an information history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each stage \(t\), let \(s\sim_t r\) mean that scenarios \(s\) and \(r\) have identical observations through stage \(t\). A scenario-indexed policy \(x=(x_{t,s})\) is nonanticipative exactly when
\[x_{t,s}=x_{t,r}\quad\text{for every }t\text{ and every }s\sim_t r.\]
After choosing one representative or a spanning tree within each equivalence class, these equalities can be collected without redundancy as \(Hx=0\). Any matrix \(H\) having this equality set as its nullspace is an explicit nonanticipativity matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decisions at a stage must agree across scenarios with the same observed history; selected pairwise equalities collect this requirement as a linear system.
assumptions_latex: All scenario decisions at a fixed stage lie in a common vector space.
The relation \(\sim_t\) partitions scenarios by observed history through stage \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy is nonanticipative if and only if \(Hx=0\).

notation.meaning: scenarios have identical histories through stage t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit equality condition and nullspace formulation fit the leaf and are internally consistent, but no source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted orthogonal decomposition into consensus and disagreement components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N=\operatorname{range}E\) and \(\langle x,y\rangle_D=x^\top Dy\), with \(D\succ0\). Then \[\mathcal N^{\perp_D}=\{q:E^\top Dq=0\},\qquad x=P_{\mathcal N}x+(I-P_{\mathcal N})x,\] where the two components lie in \(\mathcal N\) and \(\mathcal N^{\perp_D}\), respectively, and \[\|x\|_D^2=\|P_{\mathcal N}x\|_D^2+\|(I-P_{\mathcal N})x\|_D^2.\] Thus the disagreement residual vanishes exactly for nonanticipative \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every scenario vector uniquely decomposes into a consensus component and a weighted zero-average disagreement component.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) has full column rank.
\(D\succ0\).

notation.meaning: weighted orthogonal complement of the consensus subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Disagreement Decomposition
Consensus-Subspace Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspace and projector characterization of nonanticipative scenario decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be an explicit nonanticipativity matrix and define the consensus subspace
\[\mathcal N:=\ker H.\]
If \(E\) replicates one decision for each information-history class into all corresponding scenario coordinates, then \(\mathcal N=\operatorname{range}E\). Under a positive-definite scenario-weight matrix \(D\), the \(D\)-orthogonal consensus projector is
\[P_{\mathcal N}=E(E^\top D E)^{-1}E^\top D.\]
Consequently, \(x\) is nonanticipative exactly when \(x\in\mathcal N\), equivalently \(P_{\mathcal N}x=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipative decisions form the range of a history-replication map, equivalently the kernel of the equality matrix or the fixed-point set of a consensus projector.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) represents all required history-class equalities.
\(E\) has full column rank and \(D\) is positive definite.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The kernel, range, and weighted-projector characterization is coherent and correctly classified as a representation, but it lacks cited support.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when node labels omit earlier observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equivalence \(n_t(s)=n_t(r)\iff s\sim_t r\) requires nodes to encode complete histories. If nodes retain only the current observation, histories \((0,1)\) and \((1,1)\) can receive the same label despite being distinguishable; equating their decisions then imposes an equality not required by nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Current-observation labels cannot generally replace complete-history nodes.
assumptions_latex: Information through stage \(t\) includes all observations up to that stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete-History Encoding Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtration-compatible refinement of scenario-tree history classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(n_t(s)\) denotes the stage-\(t\) node reached by scenario \(s\), then \(n_{t+1}(s)=n_{t+1}(r)\) implies \(n_t(s)=n_t(r)\). Thus the stage-\(t+1\) history partition refines the stage-\(t\) partition, and every nonroot node has a unique parent representing the preceding history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree history classes refine with time, and the parent map consistently removes the newest observation.
assumptions_latex: Scenarios are root-to-leaf paths in a rooted tree.
Each node records the complete history through its stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested History Partitions
Scenario-Tree History Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between scenario equality constraints and node-indexed policies on a tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In a finite scenario tree, let \(n_t(s)\) be the node reached by scenario \(s\) at stage \(t\). Then the history relation satisfies
\[s\sim_t r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad n_t(s)=n_t(r).\]
A scenario-indexed family \((x_{t,s})\) satisfies all nonanticipativity equalities if and only if there exist node decisions \((u_n)\) such that
\[x_{t,s}=u_{n_t(s)}\quad\text{for every stage }t\text{ and scenario }s.\]
Thus explicit scenario equalities and node-indexed tree decisions describe the same policy space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two scenarios share a stage decision exactly when they reach the same tree node; nonanticipative scenario policies therefore correspond bijectively to node-indexed policies.
assumptions_latex: Each scenario is a root-to-leaf path in a finite scenario tree.
Nodes encode complete observation histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scenario-indexed nonanticipative policies and node-indexed policies are in bijective correspondence.

notation.meaning: decision assigned to tree node n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The history-node equivalence fits the terminal container and the stated finite-tree assumptions, but no inspectable source is cited.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional qualification for dualizing nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v=\inf\{F(x):Hx=0\}\), assume \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(v\) is finite, and \[0\in\operatorname{ri}(H(\operatorname{dom}F)).\] Then the Lagrangian dual \[\sup_\lambda\inf_x\{F(x)+\langle\lambda,Hx\rangle\}\] has value \(v\) and attains its supremum. If this relative-interior condition fails, weak duality remains valid but zero gap and multiplier attainment are not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior condition on the image of the effective domain gives zero duality gap and an attained nonanticipativity multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex on a finite-dimensional space.
The primal value is finite.
\(0\in\operatorname{ri}(H(\operatorname{dom}F))\).
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Strong-Duality Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic price space and redundancy under dualized consensus equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N=\operatorname{range}E=\ker H\). Every perturbation generated by equality multipliers has the form \[q=H^\top\lambda\in\operatorname{range}H^\top=\mathcal N^\perp,\] equivalently \(E^\top q=0\). Thus prices balance to zero within each replicated history class. The dual function depends on \(\lambda\) only through \(q\); if \(H\) has redundant rows, multipliers differing by an element of \(\ker H^\top\) are dual-equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity prices are zero-sum disagreement prices, and redundant equality rows create nonunique equivalent multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(\ker H=\operatorname{range}E\).
The spaces are finite dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q\in\mathcal N^\perp\iff E^\top q=0,\qquad H^\top\lambda=H^\top\lambda'\Rightarrow\lambda,\lambda'\text{ are dual-equivalent}.

notation.meaning: coordinate multiplier for the chosen equality system

knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Nonanticipativity Prices
Dualized Nonanticipativity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian dual representation of linear nonanticipativity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a proper convex objective incorporating all scenario-local conic constraints, and consider
\[v=\inf_x\{F(x):Hx=0\}.\]
Its nonanticipativity Lagrangian and dual value are
\[L(x,\lambda)=F(x)+\langle\lambda,Hx\rangle,\qquad d=\sup_\lambda\inf_x L(x,\lambda).\]
Weak duality gives \(d\le v\). If a standard conic constraint qualification holds for the primal formulation, then \(d=v\) and an optimal multiplier prices violations of the nonanticipativity equalities. When \(F\) is scenario-separable, the inner infimum separates by scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers attached to nonanticipativity equalities produce a lower-bounding dual problem whose inner minimization separates by scenario; conic regularity yields equality of primal and dual values.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(H\) is linear.
A conic constraint qualification is required for strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Always \(d\le v\); under the stated qualification, \(d=v\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Weak duality and scenario separation are plausible, but the strong-duality claim invokes an unspecified conic constraint qualification and has no supporting source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario L-shaped decomposition using one aggregate recourse optimality cut per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For Q(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x), solve a master in (x,\theta) whose cuts lower-bound Q. At a trial x^k, solve every scenario subproblem. If all recourse values are finite and g_s^k\in\partial Q_s(x^k), add
\[\theta\ge \sum_{s\in S}p_s\bigl(Q_s(x^k)+(g_s^k)^\top(x-x^k)\bigr).\]
If a scenario is infeasible and supplies a valid violated conic feasibility cut, add that cut instead. Maintain a master lower bound L_k and the best objective U_k of a recourse-feasible incumbent, and stop when U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method evaluates every scenario but adds one probability-weighted optimality cut; infeasible recourse is handled by valid feasibility cuts, and the incumbent-master gap is the stopping certificate.
assumptions_latex: S is finite, p_s\ge0, and \sum_sp_s=1.
Every generated optimality or feasibility cut is globally valid.
Master and scenario solves are exact for the stated gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon implies that the returned feasible incumbent is \varepsilon-optimal.

notation.meaning: Master lower bound and feasible-incumbent upper bound

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut L-Shaped Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes aggregated optimality information from feasibility-cut handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Scenario supports Q_s(x)\ge a_s+g_s^\top x imply
\[Q(x)\ge\sum_sp_s(a_s+g_s^\top x).\]
Thus single-cut refers to one aggregated optimality cut. Valid feasibility inequalities \phi_i(x)\le0 may remain separate; a nonnegative combination \sum_i\mu_i\phi_i(x)\le0 is valid for \mu_i\ge0 and cuts off a trial point only when its combined violation is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-cut decomposition aggregates scenario optimality supports; feasibility cuts may remain separate and can be aggregated only with validity-preserving coefficients.
assumptions_latex: Each constituent inequality is globally valid.
The aggregation coefficients of feasibility inequalities are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted optimality support is valid, and a combined feasibility cut is useful only when violated.
knowledge_statements.title: Scope of Single-Cut Aggregation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination in the Polyhedral Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite convergence when only finitely many relevant L-shaped cuts can arise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose X and all scenario recourse epigraphs are polyhedral, the problem has a finite attained optimum, all master and scenario problems are solved exactly, and every nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent violated cut from finite extreme-point and extreme-ray cut families. Then single-cut L-shaped decomposition terminates after finitely many cut additions at an optimum. General nonpolyhedral conic recourse need not admit such finite cut termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite polyhedral cut families give finite exact termination; general conic recourse does not inherit that guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The relevant optimality- and feasibility-cut families are finite.
A new violated cut is added whenever termination has not occurred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates after finitely many cut additions with an optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given first-stage set \(X\), cost \(c\), and convex recourse functions \(Q_s\), initialize a master with variable \((x,\theta)\) and valid lower cuts. At iteration \(k\), solve
\[\min\{c^\top x+\theta:x\in X,\;\theta\ge\alpha_j+g_j^\top x\ (j<k)\}\]
to obtain \(x^k\). Solve every scenario conic subproblem, obtaining \(Q_s(x^k)\) and \(g_s^k\in\partial Q_s(x^k)\), and add the aggregate cut
\[\theta\ge\sum_s p_s\bigl(Q_s(x^k)+(g_s^k)^\top(x-x^k)\bigr).\]

Nonanticipativity Lagrangian Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-separable relaxation of consensus constraints in a copied formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the copied convex problem
\[v=\inf\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s):x_s\in X_s,\;x_s=z\ \text{for all }s\right\}.\]
Dualizing \(x_s=z\) with weighted multipliers \(\lambda_s\) and eliminating \(z\) gives
\[d=\sup_{(\lambda_s):\,\sum_s p_s\lambda_s=0}\sum_{s\in S}p_s\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(f_s(x_s)+\lambda_s^\top x_s\bigr).\]
Thus evaluation of the dual objective decomposes into independent scenario problems. Weak duality gives \(d\le v\); equality holds under an applicable convex conic constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing scenario consensus with balanced multipliers yields independent scenario subproblems and a dual lower bound; standard convex conic regularity gives strong duality.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_s\) is proper, closed, and convex, and each \(X_s\) is convex.
Strong duality requires an applicable conic constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\le v\), and \(d=v\) under the stated regularity condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[

\[
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_kP_{N^\perp}x^k.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(\lambda=(\lambda_s)_{s\in S}\in N^\perp\), define
\[
q(\lambda)=\sum_{s\in S}\inf_{x_s}\bigl\{p_sf_s(x_s)+\langle\lambda_s,x_s\rangle\bigr\}.
\]
For every feasible \(x\in N\), orthogonality gives \(\langle\lambda,x\rangle=0\); hence
\[
q(\lambda)\leq \sum_{s\in S}p_sf_s(x_s).
\]
Taking the infimum over feasible \(x\) yields \(q(\lambda)\leq v_P\). Thus the scenario minimizers together with \(\lambda\in N^\perp\) provide a directly checkable dual-bound certificate; no primal consensus is required for validity of the bound.

Fix \(\rho>0\), choose \(z^0\in N\) and \(w^0\in N^\perp\), and for \(k=0,1,\ldots\) compute in parallel
\[

\[

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(z^k\in N\), \(w^k\in N^\perp\), and \(\rho>0\), let
\[
\phi_{s,k}(u)=p_sf_s(u)+\langle w_s^k,u\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert u-z_s^k\rVert^2.

Choose \(x_s^{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
