\]
then update
\[
z^{k+1}=P_Nx^{k+1},\qquad w^{k+1}=w^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).
\]
Terminate only when the consensus residual, multiplier residual, and declared subproblem errors meet their tolerances. With the stated summability condition, the perturbations are summable in the associated proximal iteration, so its limit points satisfy the primal-dual optimality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progressive hedging may use approximate conic scenario solves when their declared errors are controlled and summable, while retaining the usual consensus and multiplier updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Conic-Subproblem Progressive Hedging

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate, but the conversion from scenario objective errors to summable proximal perturbations and the resulting limit-point conclusion depend on a specific inexact splitting theorem. No authoritative locator supports the stated square-root summability rule or convergence version.

assumptions_latex: Scenario functions are proper, closed, and convex, and the nonanticipative problem has a primal-dual solution.
Each scenario update uses a consensus vector delayed by at most \(D<\infty\) updates.
Every scenario is activated at least once in every \(B<\infty\) consecutive global updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed bounded-delay activation rule defines an asynchronous progressive-hedging iteration; convergence additionally depends on a source-specific admissible relaxation range.

notation.meaning: Scenario activated at global update k.
Index of the consensus vector read at update k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay block-update formulation; no universal convergence range is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Maintain shared \(z^k\in N\) and scenario multipliers \(w^k\). At global update \(k\), scenario \(s_k\) reads \(z^{\tau_k}\), where \(k-D\leq\tau_k\leq k\), and computes
\[
\widehat x_{s_k}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_u\left\{p_{s_k}f_{s_k}(u)+\langle w_{s_k}^k,u\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert u-z_{s_k}^{\tau_k}\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
Replace only that scenario block by \(x_{s_k}^{k+1}=(1-\eta)x_{s_k}^k+\eta\widehat x_{s_k}\), retain the other blocks, form \(z^{k+1}=P_Nx^{k+1}\), and update the activated multiplier by its consensus discrepancy. Stop after a synchronization checkpoint at which all residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenarios update from possibly stale consensus information, subject to bounded delays and fair activation; convergence requires a relaxation range tailored to the asynchronous variant.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Progressive Hedging

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the activated multiplier update is described without an explicit formula, and the projection of a partially updated global vector may not represent the intended asynchronous implementation. A specific asynchronous progressive-hedging variant and admissible relaxation rule require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact termination certificate using consecutive PH iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the scenario subproblems at iteration \(k\) are solved exactly and define \(r_{\mathrm p}^{k+1}=x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\) and \(r_{\mathrm d}^{k+1}=\rho(z^{k+1}-z^k)\). If both residuals vanish, then \(z^{k+1}\in N\), \(w^{k+1}\in N^\perp\), and \(-w^{k+1}\in\partial F(z^{k+1})\), so \(z^{k+1}\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact scenario solves, simultaneous zero primal and dual PH residuals certify consensus and optimality.
assumptions_latex: The scenario objectives are proper, closed, and convex.
Scenario proximal subproblems are solved exactly.
Projection, norm, and multiplier scaling use the same product-space inner product.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Residual Iterate Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of small PH residuals without quantitative regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary proper closed convex problems, small consensus, successive-consensus, and scenario-stationarity residuals do not alone certify a prescribed objective gap. Such a conversion requires quantitative information such as an error bound, bounded multipliers, Lipschitz data, strong convexity with suitable regularity, or independently verified primal and dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small PH residuals are diagnostics, not a universal numerical objective-gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: No quantitative residual-to-solution error bound or independent objective bound is available.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Only Approximate-Certificate Boundary

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sf_s(x_s)\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(N\) is the nonanticipativity subspace, and subdifferentials are taken in the scenario product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((x,w)\) is a verifiable certificate of global optimality for \(\min_{y\in N}F(y)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex first-order optimality over a linear subspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-dual consensus certificate for convex progressive hedging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A pair \((x,w)\) is an exact progressive-hedging consensus certificate when
\[
x\in N,\qquad w\in N^\perp,\qquad -w\in\partial F(x).
\]
Equivalently, scenario feasibility and stationarity may be checked blockwise as \(-w_s\in p_s\partial f_s(x_s)\), while \(P_{N^\perp}x=0\) checks consensus and \(P_Nw=0\) checks dual compatibility. These relations imply
\[
0\in\partial F(x)+N_N(x),
\]
where \(N_N(x)=N^\perp\) for \(x\in N\). Hence \(x\) globally minimizes \(F\) over \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact consensus, a multiplier orthogonal to nonanticipativity, and scenario-wise convex stationarity together certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Progressive-Hedging Consensus Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind exactly fits the leaf, and the displayed consensus, dual-compatibility, and convex-stationarity conditions form a plausible sufficient optimality certificate. However, no source or locator is supplied, and the final normal-cone derivation is proof text that should not appear in the reviewed statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid stopping certificate for finite-tree nested Benders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k\) be the optimum of the root master built from globally valid lower cuts. Let a nonanticipative feasible policy produced at iteration \(k\) have exactly evaluated expected cost \(U_k\). Then \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\). Consequently, \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of that policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid root lower master and an exactly evaluated feasible policy bracket the optimum and provide the stopping gap.
assumptions_latex: All root-master cuts are globally valid lower cuts.
The incumbent is a feasible nonanticipative policy.
Its expected cost is evaluated exactly over the finite tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Root Policy-Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional finite termination of exact nested Benders with finite complete cut families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each node value function has a finite exact representation \[Q_n(u)=\max_{j\in J_n}\{\alpha_{nj}+\langle\beta_{nj},u\rangle\}.\] Assume exact forward and backward solves, no cut deletion or duplicate strict update, and that whenever the certified root gap is positive the pass generates at least one previously absent cut from the corresponding families. Then at most \(\sum_n|J_n\setminus J_n^0|\) strict cut additions occur before the certified root gap vanishes. Without a finite exact cut family or the gap-to-new-cut property, finite termination does not follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite exact cut families yield a finite addition bound only when every positive certified root gap forces a new missing cut.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and every \(J_n\) are finite.
Forward and backward subproblems and gap evaluations are exact.
A positive certified root gap forces addition of a previously absent exact-family cut.
Cuts are not deleted or repeated as strict updates.

notation.meaning: finite exact cut family at node n
initially present cuts at node n

review_flags: This bounds distinct strict cut additions, not forward passes or conic-solver work.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Cut Termination Regime

assumptions_latex: A finite scenario tree has convex conic stage subproblems and additive conditional costs.
For every child subproblem, strong conic duality holds at the trial state used to generate a cut.
The algorithm maintains lower approximations of all downstream value functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual solutions generate valid supporting cuts, and backward propagation produces nested lower approximations for the root problem.

notation.meaning: Cost-to-go function at tree node n.
Polyhedral lower approximation after iteration k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multistage Benders cuts from conic dual value functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree nested Benders using strong-duality cuts from convex conic descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize each nonterminal approximation \(\underline Q_n^0\leq Q_n\). A forward pass solves the root-to-leaf conic subproblems with \(Q_n\) replaced by \(\underline Q_n^k\), producing trial parent states \(\bar u_{a(n)}^k\). In reverse stage order, solve every child conic problem at its trial state and recover a dual value and subgradient \((\alpha_n^k,\beta_n^k)\) such that
\[
Q_n(u)\geq\alpha_n^k+\langle\beta_n^k,u\rangle.
\]
Update
\[
\underline Q_n^{k+1}(u)=\max\{\underline Q_n^k(u),\alpha_n^k+\langle\beta_n^k,u\rangle\}.
\]
Stop when the root upper-lower gap meets tolerance; return the incumbent policy and root lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward passes generate trial states; backward conic dual solves add valid supporting cuts to nested cost-to-go approximations until the root gap closes.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Conic Benders Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches nested conic Benders decomposition, but strong duality alone does not fully specify dual attainment and the affine parameterization needed to recover the asserted supporting cut. The source-specific forward/backward variant and construction of a valid root upper bound also require documentation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct indexing of stagewise consensus when terminal nodes may carry decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_d\) be the set of scenario-tree nodes at which a decision variable is defined. Stagewise consensus requires \(x_n^s=z_n\) for every \(n\in V_d\) and every leaf \(s\in L(n)\). Restricting the equations to nonterminal nodes is equivalent only when terminal nodes carry no decisions or each terminal decision has a single scenario copy. Otherwise terminal decision nodes must also be included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus is imposed at every decision-bearing history node; a nonterminal-only convention is valid only when terminal decisions are absent or unreplicated.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite.
\(V_d\) contains exactly the nodes carrying replicated decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Node Indexing Boundary

assumptions_latex: The finite scenario tree has node set \(V\), stages \(t(n)\), and positive node probabilities.
Each scenario copy \(x_n^s\) represents the decision at node \(n\) on a leaf scenario \(s\) passing through that node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equalities are exactly the stagewise nonanticipativity consensus condition.

notation.meaning: Scenario-specific copy of the decision at node n.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scenario-tree nonanticipativity by common history
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nodewise consensus for leaf-scenario copies sharing the same observed history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Stagewise scenario consensus holds if and only if, for every nonterminal tree node \(n\in V\), there exists a node decision \(z_n\) such that
\[
x_n^s=z_n\qquad\text{for every }s\in L(n).
\]
Equivalently, with conditional weights \(\pi_{s\mid n}>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in L(n)}\pi_{s\mid n}=1\), define
\[
z_n=\sum_{s\in L(n)}\pi_{s\mid n}x_n^s.
\]
Then consensus is characterized by \(x_n^s-z_n=0\) for all \(n\) and \(s\in L(n)\). Thus decisions coincide precisely among scenarios sharing the history represented by \(n\), without constraining decisions at distinct nodes of the same stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All leaf scenarios sharing a tree node must use one common decision there; scenarios at different nodes may choose differently despite sharing a stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Scenario Consensus

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits and the nodewise consensus equations are mathematically plausible. No source supports the exact convention restricting the condition to nonterminal nodes, which may omit terminal-node decisions in some scenario-tree models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic and weighted-projector properties of the tree transfer maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) conditionally average copies within each history class and \(R\) replicate node variables, with \(AR=I\). Then \(P=RA\) satisfies \(P^2=P\), \(\operatorname{range}P=\operatorname{range}R\), and \(\ker P=\ker A\). If the copy-space inner product uses weights whose normalized restriction to each history class equals the averaging weights in \(A\), then \(P\) is the corresponding orthogonal projector. Hence \(Px=x\) exactly for replicated nonanticipative copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication after conditional averaging is an idempotent projection onto replicated tree decisions and is orthogonal under compatible probability weights.
assumptions_latex: The conditional weights are positive and normalized in each history class.
For orthogonality, the copy-space inner product uses weights compatible with the conditional averages.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation-Replication Projector

assumptions_latex: A finite scenario tree has node set \(V\), leaf set \(S\), and positive conditional probabilities \(\pi_{s\mid n}\).
Each leaf scenario carries copies \(x_n^s\) for nodes on its root-to-leaf path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregation and replication maps connect leaf-scenario variables with node variables, and their fixed-point relation encodes nonanticipativity.

notation.meaning: Conditional aggregation from leaf copies to node decisions.
Replication of node decisions to descendant leaf copies.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional averaging and replication on a finite scenario tree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear interfaces between leaf-scenario and node-indexed tree representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the aggregation map \(A\) and replication map \(R\) by
\[
(Ax)_n=\sum_{s\in L(n)}\pi_{s\mid n}x_n^s,\qquad (Rz)_n^s=z_n\quad(s\in L(n)).
\]
Then \(AR=I\) on the node-variable space. The composition \(RA\) maps arbitrary leaf copies to their historywise conditional averages, and
\[
x=RAx
\]
holds exactly when the leaf copies satisfy nodewise nonanticipativity. Node-local conic constraints and costs can therefore be evaluated after replication, while scenario-generated quantities can be returned to the tree through conditional aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional averaging sends leaf-scenario copies to tree nodes, replication sends node decisions back to leaves, and their fixed points are precisely nonanticipative decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Aggregation Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the aggregation-interface leaf, and AR=I with fixed points of RA encoding nodewise consensus is plausible under the stated positive conditional weights. An authoritative locator is still required for these maps and the asserted conic-model interface interpretation.

children.title: Scenario Decomposition Consistency for Conic Models
Extensive-Form Representation
children.top_down_role: Integrated scenario-conic representations retaining all scenario blocks in one model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated product-cone representation retaining all scenario blocks and exact nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let x_s\in H_s, A_s:H_s\to G_s, b_s\in G_s, c_s\in H_s, and let K_s\subseteq G_s be a closed convex cone. For finite S, probabilities p_s\ge0, and a nonanticipativity subspace N\subseteq\prod_sH_s, the extensive form is
\[\inf_x\left\{\sum_sp_s\langle c_s,x_s\rangle:A_sx_s-b_s\in K_s\ (s\in S),\ x\in N\right\}.
\]
The scenario constraints are equivalently one block-diagonal affine constraint in \prod_sK_s; every scenario copy and coupling equality remains explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extensive form stacks all scenario conic blocks into one product-cone model and imposes nonanticipativity explicitly.
assumptions_latex: S is finite and \sum_sp_s=1.
The displayed spaces and linear maps are dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed program is a single conic product-space representation of the finite-scenario model.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Scenario Conic Extensive Form

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\), and each scenario feasible set is \(X_s=\{x_s:A_sx_s-b_s\in K_s\}\) for a closed convex cone \(K_s\).
\(N\) is a linear nonanticipativity subspace of the scenario product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed single conic program is the extensive-form representation of the scenario model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block-diagonal extensive form with linear nonanticipativity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario linear conic extensive form with explicit nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scenario costs \(c_s\), the extensive form is the single product-cone program
\[
\begin{aligned}
\inf_{(x_s)_{s\in S}}&\quad \sum_{s\in S}p_s\langle c_s,x_s\rangle\\
\text{subject to}&\quad A_sx_s-b_s\in K_s,\quad s\in S,\\
&\quad x=(x_s)_{s\in S}\in N.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently, the scenario conic constraints form one block-diagonal constraint in the product cone \(\prod_{s\in S}K_s\), while membership in \(N\) couples blocks that share the same information history. Every variable and constraint copy is retained explicitly in this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extensive form stacks all scenario conic blocks into one product-cone program and imposes nonanticipativity as an explicit coupling subspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Extensive-Form Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind correctly fits the terminal container and the displayed block-diagonal conic extensive form is standard. Nevertheless, source_refs is empty, and compatible spaces and dimensions for x_s, A_s, b_s, c_s, and K_s are not explicitly introduced.

children.title: Decomposed-Model Representation
children.top_down_role: Scenario-separated representations coordinated through master or consensus structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario blocks coupled solely by exact nonanticipativity consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let H=\prod_{s\in S}H_s, let X_s\subseteq H_s be the scenario feasible sets, and let N\subseteq H be the nonanticipativity subspace. The decomposed primal representation is
\[\inf\left\{\sum_sp_sf_s(x_s):x_s\in X_s\ (s\in S),\ x\in N\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, for any linear map B with \ker B=N, its only cross-scenario constraint is Bx=0. Dualizing this constraint gives
\[L(x,\nu)=\sum_sp_sf_s(x_s)+\langle\nu,Bx\rangle,\]
whose infimum separates by scenario for fixed \nu.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decomposed model retains independent scenario blocks and isolates nonanticipativity in one linear consensus interface; dualizing that interface yields separable scenario evaluations.
assumptions_latex: S is finite.
Each scenario objective and feasible set depends only on x_s.
B is linear and \ker B=N.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \nu, \inf_{x_s\in X_s}L(x,\nu) separates over s.

notation.meaning: Consensus operator with kernel equal to the nonanticipativity subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Separated Consensus Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent weighted and unweighted multiplier conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equip H with \langle x,y\rangle_p=\sum_sp_s\langle x_s,y_s\rangle for p_s>0. Then x\in N iff P^p_{N^{\perp_p}}x=0. A multiplier \lambda\in N^{\perp_p} gives the pairing \sum_sp_s\langle\lambda_s,x_s\rangle. Under the unweighted product pairing, the identical functional uses \widetilde\lambda_s=p_s\lambda_s. Mixing the weighted projection convention with unscaled unweighted multipliers changes the dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted and unweighted consensus geometries are equivalent after matching multiplier rescaling, but their conventions cannot be mixed.
assumptions_latex: p_s>0 for every scenario.
Each H_s is finite-dimensional and N is a linear subspace.

notation.meaning: Orthogonality in the probability-weighted product inner product
Weighted projection onto the disagreement subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Probability-Weighted Consensus Geometry

assumptions_latex: The extensive model has finite scenario set \(S\), separable conic feasible sets \(X_s\), and nonanticipativity subspace \(N\).
The product space carries an inner product for which \(N^\perp\) is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposed representation consists of independent scenario blocks linked only through the consensus equation or its multiplier.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projections onto consensus and disagreement spaces.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: replicated scenario blocks coupled by a consensus operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replicated scenario-block model with consensus isolated as the sole coupling relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The decomposed primal representation is
\[
\inf\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_s\langle c_s,x_s\rangle:x_s\in X_s\ (s\in S),\ P_{N^\perp}x=0\right\}.
\]
Introducing \(\lambda\in N^\perp\) gives the separable partial Lagrangian
\[
L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{s\in S}\left(p_s\langle c_s,x_s\rangle+\langle\lambda_s,x_s\rangleight),\qquad x_s\in X_s.
\]
Thus, for fixed \(\lambda\), evaluation of \(\inf_xL(x,\lambda)\) separates by scenario. The only cross-scenario interface is the consensus residual \(P_{N^\perp}x\), which is returned to the coordinating procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decomposed model keeps each conic scenario block independent and exposes nonanticipativity as one consensus residual handled by coordination multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposed-Model Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits and the consensus equation and partial Lagrangian are plausible. No cited locator establishes the chosen product-space inner product or confirms that the displayed unweighted multiplier pairing is consistent with the probability-scaled objective and projection conventions.

children.title: Representation Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where extensive-form and decomposed representations preserve the same feasible outcomes and values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong Lagrangian duality for the consensus constraint under a precise relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let C=\prod_sX_s, let f(x)=\sum_sp_sf_s(x_s) be proper closed convex, and let N be the nonanticipativity subspace. Define
\[v_D=\sup_{\lambda\in N^\perp}\inf_{x\in C}\{f(x)+\langle\lambda,x\rangle\}.\]
If \operatorname{ri}(C\cap\operatorname{dom}f)\cap N\ne\varnothing and the primal value is finite, finite-dimensional convex strong duality gives v_D=\inf\{f(x):x\in C\cap N\}. Without such a qualification, exact primal representation equivalence remains valid, but equality or attainment of this multiplier dual is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior point satisfying consensus makes the nonanticipativity multiplier dual exact; primal reformulation equivalence itself does not need this assumption.
assumptions_latex: C and f are finite-dimensional, convex, and closed in the stated sense.
\operatorname{ri}(C\cap\operatorname{dom}f)\cap N\ne\varnothing.
The primal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity-Dual Equivalence Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconditional primal equivalence under exact copying and consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an extensive and a decomposed formulation use identical scenario-local feasible sets, objectives, probabilities, and an exact consensus constraint whose kernel is the extensive nonanticipativity subspace, then replication and aggregation give mutually inverse correspondences between their feasible outcomes. Objectives agree on corresponding points, so their extended-real infimal values are equal. This primal equality requires neither Slater feasibility nor attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact scenario copying and exact consensus preserve primal feasible outcomes and infimal value without a constraint qualification.
assumptions_latex: All scenario data and weights agree.
The decomposed consensus kernel equals the extensive nonanticipativity subspace.

notation.meaning: Extensive and decomposed primal infimal values

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Scenario-Replication Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of scenario-local recourse variables as extended-real value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[Q_s(x)=\inf\{q_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s-h_s+T_sx\in K_s\},\]
with Q_s(x)=+\infty when infeasible, one has
\[\inf_{x\in X,y_s}\left\{c^\top x+\sum_sp_sq_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s-h_s+T_sx\in K_s\ \forall s\right\}
=\inf_{x\in X}\left\{c^\top x+\sum_sp_sQ_s(x)\right\}.
\]
No attainment or Slater condition is needed for equality of infima. A reduced optimizer x^* lifts to an extensive optimizer exactly when every positively weighted Q_s(x^*) is attained by feasible recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating local recourse variables preserves the infimal value; lifting an optimizer additionally requires attainment of each relevant recourse infimum.
assumptions_latex: S is finite and p_s\ge0.
All values use the extended-real convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{ext}}=v_{\mathrm{value}}, with optimizer lifting characterized by recourse attainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Value Elimination Equivalence

assumptions_latex: The extensive and decomposed models use the same finite scenario copies, probabilities, conic feasible sets, objective, and nonanticipativity operator.
All transformations between node and scenario variables are exact linear replication or aggregation maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal representations are equivalent; equality with the multiplier-dual value additionally requires an appropriate conic constraint qualification.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact variable replication preserves primal feasibility and value; strong duality needs constraint qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates unconditional primal reformulation equivalence from qualification-dependent dual-value equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the extensive and decomposed formulations differ only by introducing scenario copies and the exact constraint \(P_{N^\perp}x=0\), then their feasible points correspond under replication and aggregation, their objectives agree on corresponding points, and
\[
v_{\mathrm{ext}}=v_{\mathrm{dec}}.
\]
This primal equivalence requires neither strict feasibility nor attainment. If, in addition, the resulting convex conic program satisfies a constraint qualification ensuring strong Lagrangian duality, such as an applicable relative-interior Slater condition, then
\[
v_D=v_{\mathrm{dec}}=v_{\mathrm{ext}}.
\]
Without that qualification, the two primal representations remain equivalent, but the nonanticipativity multiplier dual may have a strict value gap or fail to attain its supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact scenario replication preserves primal feasibility and value. Equality with the multiplier dual also needs a suitable conic strong-duality qualification.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is appropriate for an equivalence-regime leaf, and exact replication plausibly preserves the primal formulation. The additional dual equality is not reviewable because the multiplier dual is not formally defined and the phrase 'an applicable relative-interior Slater condition' does not state a precise hypothesis for the partially dualized problem.

children.title: Equivalence Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Modeling inconsistencies or closure effects that break representation equivalence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set failure caused by omitted nonanticipativity equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F_1=F_2=[0,1], N=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1=x_2\}, and \widehat N=\mathbb R^2. For f(x)=x_1-x_2, the extensive model has value 0, while the under-linked model has value -1 at (0,1).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting a required nonanticipativity equality can enlarge the feasible set and change the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Under-Linking Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure replacement can preserve an infimum while changing feasible outcomes and attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed convex set
\[C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R_+^2:xy\ge1\}\]
is rotated-cone representable and has projection \operatorname{proj}_xC=(0,\infty). Replacing this projection by its closure [0,\infty) introduces x=0. Minimizing x has infimum 0 in both models, but the projected model does not attain it and the closure-replaced model does.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a nonclosed projected feasible set can create spurious feasible optimizers even when the infimal value is unchanged.

notation.meaning: Closed lifted feasible set with nonclosed projection

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Closure Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value failure caused by inconsistent scenario weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two fixed feasible scenario outcomes with costs (f_1,f_2)=(0,1), probabilities p=(1/2,1/2) give value 1/2, whereas weights \widehat p=(3/4,1/4) give value 1/4. Unequal weights need not affect a model whose feasible scenario-cost vectors all have equal components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect weights can change the value, although unequal weight vectors are harmless on special feasible cost sets.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations have the same nonempty feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight-Mismatch Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp set and objective criteria for failure of primal representation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let F be the product of scenario feasible sets, let N and \widehat N be the extensive and decomposed linking sets, and let f and \widehat f be their objectives. The two primal models have identical feasible outcomes and objective values exactly when
\[F\cap N=F\cap\widehat N\quad\text{and}\quad f(x)=\widehat f(x)\ \text{on this common set}.\]
Thus \widehat N\ne N or unequal weight vectors alone does not prove instance-level failure; failure occurs when the feasible intersections differ or the induced objective functionals disagree on their common feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correspondence fails precisely through a changed feasible intersection or a changed objective on the common feasible set.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations use the same scenario-local feasible product F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of the two feasible intersections and objectives is the exact primal correspondence test.

notation.meaning: Linking set and objective used by the decomposed formulation

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Correspondence Failure Test
Equivalence Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when a scenario-separated conic formulation ceases to represent its extensive form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the extensive minimization model have scenario probabilities \(p_s\), scenario decisions \(x_s\), conic feasible sets \(F_s\), and nonanticipativity set \(N\). Its value is \(v_E=\inf\{\sum_s p_s f_s(x_s):(x_s)_s\in (\prod_s F_s)\cap N\}\). A decomposed model is equivalent only if it uses the same normalized weights and its linking constraints define exactly \(N\). Equivalence can fail whenever either \(\widehat p\ne p\) or \(\widehat N\ne N\): then its feasible set or objective differs, and there exist linear scenario costs for which its optimal value or optimizer differs from that of the extensive model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing scenario weights or the exact nonanticipativity set can alter the feasible region, objective, optimal value, or optimizer of the decomposed model.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Each \(F_s\) is a nonempty conic-representable set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\widehat p,\widehat N)\ne(p,N)\) is a boundary beyond which extensive–decomposed equivalence is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: Exact nonanticipativity set induced by scenario histories.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation or inspectable locator is supplied. Moreover, \(\widehat N\ne N\) does not itself imply that the feasible sets differ after intersection with \(\prod_sF_s\), and changed weights need not affect a particular model. The claimed converse and existence statement require a precise sourced formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact audit of probabilities and aggregated scenario masses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exact audit checks p_s\ge0, \sum_sp_s=1, agreement between every expectation coefficient and p_s after documented whole-expression scaling, and, for every aggregation cell C in a partition \mathcal P,
\[p_C=\sum_{s\in C}p_s.
\]
Passing these identities certifies weight consistency only; it does not certify nonanticipativity, scenario feasibility, or subproblem status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check nonnegativity, normalization, coefficient agreement, and mass conservation under grouping.
assumptions_latex: All relevant scenario coefficients and aggregation cells are enumerated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in\Delta_S and every aggregation preserves declared probability mass.

notation.meaning: Declared mass of aggregation cell C

knowledge_statements.title: Probability-Weight Audit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient consistency for a finite declared scenario law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let p_s\ge0 and \sum_sp_s=1. Every expression declared to be an expectation under this scenario law must use coefficient p_s on the contribution of scenario s. A common positive rescaling is equivalent only when the entire affected objective or constraint, including its bound, is scaled. Zero-probability scenarios contribute nothing to expectations, although constraints retained for them may still restrict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected objectives and constraints must use the declared scenario probabilities consistently; selective rescaling changes the represented model.
assumptions_latex: S is finite.
The scenario law and all expectation-based expressions are explicitly identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every expectation coefficient equals its declared scenario probability, up to a documented equivalent scaling of the whole expression.

notation.meaning: Declared probability mass of scenario s

knowledge_statements.title: Expectation-Weight Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mass-conservation rule for splitting or merging identical scenario atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If scenario s of mass p_s is replaced by identical copies s_1,\ldots,s_m having the same feasible data and contribution, the represented expectation is unchanged for every feasible decision exactly when p_{s_i}\ge0 and
\[\sum_{i=1}^mp_{s_i}=p_s.
\]
Identical scenarios may conversely be grouped with their masses summed. Assigning mass p_s to every copy multiplies its expected contribution by m unless that contribution is identically zero or the whole expression is equivalently rescaled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting or merging identical scenarios preserves the stochastic model exactly when their probability mass is conserved.
assumptions_latex: The split copies have identical scenario data and contributions.
All assigned masses are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i p_{s_i}=p_s is the exact refinement-invariance condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Refinement Invariance
Probability-Weight Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for finite-scenario objectives and scenario-aggregated conic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_s>0\) be the probability of scenario \(s\), with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). Probability-weight consistency holds when every decomposed aggregation that represents an expectation uses these same weights: the objective is \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s)\), and any expected vector quantity is \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s g_s(x_s)\). Multiplying all weights by a common positive constant preserves minimizers only when every affected objective term and bound is scaled compatibly; otherwise the decomposed model does not represent the stated probability law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every expected objective or constraint must use the scenario probabilities consistently; selective omission or rescaling changes the represented stochastic model.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
\(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat p_s=p_s\) for all \(s\in S\) in every expectation-based aggregation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically plausible and fits the container, but no citation or specific locator supports the probability-weight and compatible-scaling claims.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional kernel test for history consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each t, form an oriented graph containing a spanning tree within every equivalence class of scenarios having equal h_t. Let B_t be its incidence matrix and set B=\operatorname{diag}_t(B_t\otimes I_{d_t}). Then
\[Bx=0\iff x_{t,s}=x_{t,s'}\text{ whenever }h_t(s)=h_t(s').\]
Thus \ker B is exactly the nonanticipativity subspace. The test \|Bx\|\le\tau is only tolerance-qualified; extra within-class edges are redundant, while an edge between distinct classes is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spanning-tree incidence matrix within each history class gives a necessary-and-sufficient linear nonanticipativity test.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set and stages are finite.
Decisions in each compared class have dimension d_t.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Nonanticipativity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact information-filtration consistency for scenario-indexed decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each decision stage t, let h_t(s) be the information observed before the stage-t decision in scenario s. Nonanticipativity is
\[h_t(s)=h_t(s')\Longrightarrow x_{t,s}=x_{t,s'}.
\]
Equivalently, one may introduce a variable z_{t,h} for each stage-history node and impose x_{t,s}=z_{t,h_t(s)}. Equalities may be omitted only when implied transitively; joining distinct history classes imposes an incorrectly stronger information structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario decisions coincide exactly for scenarios having the same information history when the decision is made.
assumptions_latex: The history maps represent the model's information filtration.
Compared decisions have compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{t,s}=z_{t,h_t(s)} for every t and s.

notation.meaning: Information history available before the stage-t decision
Decision attached to a stage-history node

knowledge_statements.title: History-Based Nonanticipativity
Nonanticipativity Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact history-based consistency condition for scenario-indexed decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each decision stage \(t\), let \(h_t(s)\) denote the information history observed before the stage-\(t\) decision in scenario \(s\). Nonanticipativity consistency requires
\[h_t(s)=h_t(s')\ \Longrightarrow\ x_{t,s}=x_{t,s'}\]
for every pair \(s,s'\) and every \(t\). Equivalently, there is one decision variable \(z_{t,h}\) for each stage-history node such that \(x_{t,s}=z_{t,h_t(s)}\). A decomposed formulation is consistent only when its consensus or linking constraints impose precisely these equalities, neither omitting required equalities nor equating decisions with distinct available histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario decisions must coincide exactly when the scenarios share the same information history at the decision stage.
assumptions_latex: Decisions are made before observing information revealed after stage \(t\).
The history map \(h_t\) represents the model's information filtration.

notation.meaning: Information history available at stage t in scenario s.
Decision associated with history node h.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The history-based nonanticipativity condition is standard and appropriately classified, but it has no citation or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate reporting for exact scenario-subproblem statuses at one master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\), let \(Q_s(x)\in\overline{\mathbb R}\), and assume \(p_s>0\). Report finite recourse exactly when every \(Q_s(x)\in\mathbb R\). If some value is \(+\infty\) and none is \(-\infty\), report infeasible recourse; if some value is \(-\infty\) and none is \(+\infty\), report unbounded-below recourse. If both signs occur, report a mixed status and do not assign a scalar value to \(\sum_sp_sQ_s(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite, infeasible, unbounded, and mixed scenario outcomes must be distinguished; simultaneous positive and negative infinity has no scalar aggregate value.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s>0\) for every represented scenario.
All scenario subproblems are evaluated at the same master decision \(x\).
Scenario statuses are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)\in\mathbb R\iff Q_s(x)\in\mathbb R\ \forall s\); mixed \(+\infty\)/\(-\infty\) values leave \(Q(x)\) undefined.
knowledge_statements.title: Total Scenario-Status Reconciliation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on aggregate labels when scenario solves lack exact certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If any scenario status is unresolved or supported only by a nonzero-tolerance diagnostic, the aggregate status is unresolved unless another exact scenario certificate already establishes a one-sided aggregate conclusion under the reconciliation convention. In particular, unresolved results cannot support a finite aggregate value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate finite label requires exact finite status for every scenario; inconclusive scenario diagnostics remain inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: Exact and approximate solver statuses are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists s\text{ unresolved}\Longrightarrow\text{finite aggregate status is not certified}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved Scenario Status Boundary
Scenario-Subproblem Status Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status reconciliation for scenario conic subproblems at a fixed master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a master decision \(x\). For each scenario \(s\), let \(Q_s(x)\) be the infimum of its conic subproblem, using the extended values \(+\infty\) for infeasibility and \(-\infty\) for unboundedness below. Status consistency requires the decomposition to report: finite recourse only when every \(Q_s(x)\in\mathbb R\); infeasibility when some \(Q_s(x)=+\infty\); and unboundedness when some positive-probability scenario has \(Q_s(x)=-\infty\), unless another scenario is infeasible and the combined extended-value expression is undefined. No finite aggregate bound may be asserted from unresolved, inaccurate, or mutually incompatible scenario statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregate status must faithfully reflect every scenario subproblem; finite recourse requires all scenario values to be finite.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s>0\) for every represented scenario.
All scenario subproblems are evaluated at the same master decision \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\in\mathbb R\) only if \(Q_s(x)\in\mathbb R\) for every \(s\).

notation.meaning: Extended-real optimal value of scenario s at master decision x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the aggregate-status convention. In particular, simultaneous \(+\infty\) and \(-\infty\) scenario values require a formally specified aggregation convention before the reported status is reliable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of local conic and information feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Global feasibility requires \(x\in(\prod_sX_s)\cap N\). In general, membership in \(\prod_sX_s\) does not imply membership in \(N\), and membership in \(N\) does not imply the scenario-local constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passing every scenario's conic checks does not establish information feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Local constraints and nonanticipativity are separate intersections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\prod_sX_s\not\Rightarrow x\in N,\qquad x\in N\not\Rightarrow x\in\prod_sX_s.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Local Feasibility Is Insufficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact product-space test for incompatible scenario decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the required closed subspace \(N\), define \(r_{NA}(x)=x-P_Nx=P_{N^\perp}x\) and \(\nu_{NA}(x)=\|r_{NA}(x)\|=\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\). Then \(x\) is nonanticipative exactly when either residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity violation is distance from the required consensus subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a closed linear subspace.
Projection and norm use one inner product.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity-Violation Residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value relation after deleting required information equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_E=F_D\cap N\), where \(F_D\) retains only scenario-local constraints. For minimization of the same objective, \(F_E\subseteq F_D\) implies \(v_D\le v_E\). Equality holds if a relaxed optimum lies in \(N\), but strict inequality can occur, as in the deferred two-scenario counterexample.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping nonanticipativity makes a minimization bound optimistic and sometimes strictly too low.
assumptions_latex: Only nonanticipativity constraints are removed.
The objective and minimization sense are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimistic-Value Boundary from Dropping Nonanticipativity
Nonanticipativity Violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-scenario example showing the value error caused by omitted nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider two equiprobable scenarios with scalar decisions \(x_1,x_2\in[0,1]\) made before the scenario is observed. The extensive model imposes \(x_1=x_2=x\) and minimizes
\[\tfrac12x_1-\tfrac12x_2.\]
Every extensive-form feasible decision has objective zero, so \(v_E=0\). If the nonanticipativity equality is omitted, the decomposed model chooses \(x_1=0\) and \(x_2=1\), attaining \(v_D=-\tfrac12\). Thus independent scenario optimization produces a strictly optimistic value even though each scenario decision separately satisfies its local conic-representable interval constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting a required equality lets scenarios choose incompatible decisions and can create a strictly optimistic decomposed value.
assumptions_latex: Both scenario decisions occur before scenario revelation.
The objective is minimized.

notation.meaning: Optimal value after separating scenario decisions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is self-contained, correct, and fits the failure container, but the required citation and specific locator are absent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite test for whether implemented weights differ from intended weights only by a harmless common scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\widehat p=p/(\mathbf1^Tp)\) and \(\widehat q=q/(\mathbf1^Tq)\). Then \(\widehat p=\widehat q\) if and only if \(q=\alpha p\) for some \(\alpha>0\). If \(d=\widehat q-\widehat p\ne0\), the scenario constants \(f_s=d_s\) expose the mismatch through \(\sum_s(\widehat q_s-\widehat p_s)f_s=\lVert d\rVert_2^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize both weight vectors; equality certifies harmless common scaling, while a nonzero difference supplies costs that expose the mismatch.
assumptions_latex: p,q\in\mathbb R_+^S
\mathbf1^Tp>0,\quad\mathbf1^Tq>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat p=\widehat q\iff q=\alpha p\text{ for some }\alpha>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Scenario-Weight Audit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact model-independent boundary between common objective scaling and relative scenario reweighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p,q\in\mathbb R_+^S\) be nonzero. Replacing \(\sum_s p_sf_s(x)\) by \(\sum_s q_sf_s(x)\) changes every family of scenario costs only by one fixed positive objective scale if and only if \(q=\alpha p\) for some \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only multiplication of every scenario weight by the same positive constant is harmless for every scenario model.
assumptions_latex: p,q\in\mathbb R_+^S
\mathbf 1^Tp>0,\quad \mathbf 1^Tq>0
knowledge_statements.title: Universally Harmless Scenario Rescaling
Probability-Scaling Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Example in which inconsistent scenario scaling reverses the optimal decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a common scalar decision satisfy \(x\in[0,1]\), with scenario costs \(f_1(x)=x\) and \(f_2(x)=-2x\), and probabilities \(p_1=0.9\), \(p_2=0.1\). The correctly weighted expected cost is \(0.9x-0.2x=0.7x\), whose unique minimizer is \(x=0\). If a decomposition omits the probabilities and sums the scenario costs equally, its objective is \(x-2x=-x\), whose unique minimizer is \(x=1\). Hence inconsistent probability scaling can change both the optimizer and the reported bound despite unchanged scenario feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the true probabilities by equal scenario weights can reverse the optimizer even when all scenario feasible sets remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The common decision is nonanticipative.
Both formulations minimize their displayed objectives.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numerical counterexample is correct and appropriately classified, but no citation or specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for agreement of all scenario copies under strictly positive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p_s>0\), \(\sum_s p_s=1\), define \(\bar x=\sum_s p_sx_s\) and \(r^2=\sum_s p_s\lVert x_s-\bar x\rVert_2^2\). Then \(r=0\) if and only if \(x_s=\bar x\) for every scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With strictly positive weights, weighted disagreement vanishes exactly at full scenario consensus.
assumptions_latex: p_s>0\quad(s=1,\ldots,S)
\sum_s p_s=1
x_s\in\mathbb R^n
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Consensus Residual Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limitation of using a probability-weighted residual to test agreement of every scenario copy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_j=0\) for some scenario, the weighted residual can vanish while \(x_j\ne\bar x\). Strict positivity of every included weight is therefore necessary for this residual alone to certify consensus of all copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-weight scenario is invisible to the weighted residual.
assumptions_latex: p_s\ge0
\sum_s p_s=1
p_j=0\text{ for some }j

notation.meaning: weight of the scenario invisible to the residual

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Weight Blindness
Scenario-Consensus Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based diagnostic for stalled nonanticipativity enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenario iterates \(x_s^k\) with probabilities \(p_s\), define the consensus point \(\bar x^k=\sum_s p_sx_s^k\) and residual \(r_k=(\sum_s p_s\lVert x_s^k-\bar x^k\rVert^2)^{1/2}\). Scenario-consensus stagnation occurs when there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and an index \(k_0\) such that \(r_k\ge\varepsilon\) for all \(k\ge k_0\), while the algorithm's step sizes satisfy \(\max_s\lVert x_s^{k+1}-x_s^k\rVert\to0\). The iterates then become stationary without approaching the nonanticipativity set, so convergence of local objectives alone cannot certify a feasible extensive-form solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus stagnates when scenario iterates stop moving while their weighted disagreement remains bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: All \(x_s^k\) lie in a common finite-dimensional normed space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual criterion is a plausible diagnostic, but its exact threshold-based definition is unsourced. The failure-boundary path also suggests failure_boundary rather than condition; an authoritative source is needed to settle both the convention and role.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite pairwise test that encoded decision-equality classes match true information histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every decision stage \(t\), let \(H^t_{ss'}=1\) exactly when scenarios \(s,s'\) have identical available histories, and let \(E^t_{ss'}=1\) exactly when the formulation equates their stage-\(t\) decisions. The encoding matches the histories if and only if \(E^t=H^t\) for every \(t\). An entry \((H^t_{ss'},E^t_{ss'})=(1,0)\) witnesses a split true-history class, while \((0,1)\) witnesses a spurious merge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare encoded decision equalities with true same-history relations at every stage; each mismatch identifies a split or merge.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set and decision stages are finite.
Nonanticipativity equalities are generated from the encoded history classes.

notation.meaning: true same-history incidence matrix at stage t
encoded decision-equality incidence matrix at stage t

knowledge_statements.title: History-Partition Consistency Audit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-stage consistency condition for a scenario tree with accumulating information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_t\) partition scenarios according to the information available when the stage-\(t\) decision is selected. If information is accumulated and not forgotten, then \(\mathcal P_{t+1}\) refines \(\mathcal P_t\), equivalently \(s\sim_{t+1}s'\Rightarrow s\sim_ts'\). Stage partitions violating this condition cannot be node partitions of such a scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With accumulating information, history classes may split but cannot merge across successive stages.
assumptions_latex: Information is accumulated and not forgotten between consecutive decision stages.

notation.meaning: partition by information available at decision stage t

knowledge_statements.title: Nested History-Partition Condition
Scenario-Tree History Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by linking decisions according to an incorrect scenario-tree history partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each stage \(t\), define the true history equivalence relation by \(s\sim_t s'\) exactly when \(h_t(s)=h_t(s')\). Let \(\widehat\sim_t\) be the relation encoded by the decomposition. If \(\widehat\sim_t\ne\sim_t\), then either a true history class is split, permitting anticipative decisions, or distinct true history classes are merged, imposing spurious equalities. In the first case the decomposed feasible set strictly enlarges for suitable local constraints; in the second it strictly contracts. Consequently, equality of extensive and decomposed feasible sets is not guaranteed unless the encoded and true history partitions coincide at every decision stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting a true history node permits anticipation; merging distinct history nodes imposes false equalities. Either error breaks model correspondence.
assumptions_latex: Scenario histories are defined at every decision stage.
Nonanticipativity is encoded solely through history-based equality classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\sim_t=\sim_t\) for every \(t\) is necessary for formulation-independent feasible-set correspondence.

notation.meaning: History equivalence relation encoded by the decomposition.
Information history of scenario s at stage t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partition-error distinction is plausible and fits a failure boundary, but no locator supports the stated necessity across all formulations. The conclusion depends on nonanticipativity being encoded solely by those equality classes.

children.title: Conic Decomposition Master-Subproblem Certificates
children.top_down_role: Unified certificate architecture connecting master bounds, subproblem status, coupling consistency, primal recovery, aggregate completion, and independent validation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Exactness of Restricted-Master Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering and tightness criteria for masters built from nested valid recourse cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_J=\inf_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\max_{j\in J}q_j(x)\}\), where \(q_j\le Q\) on \(X\). If \(J\subseteq J'\), then \(L_J\le L_{J'}\le v^*\). If a restricted-master minimizer \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\max_{j\in J}q_j(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\), then \(L_J=v^*\) and \(\bar x\) solves the original problem. By contrast, tightness of a retained cut merely at some original optimizer does not ensure exactness, because the restricted master may attain a smaller value elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid cuts cannot decrease the lower bound. Exactness follows when a restricted-master optimizer is also a point of recourse equality; touching an original optimizer alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Every retained cut globally underestimates \(Q\).
The relevant infima are finite, and the stated restricted-master minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\subseteq J'\Rightarrow L_J\le L_{J'}\le v^*\); if \(\bar x\in\arg\min L_J\) and \(\max_{j\in J}q_j(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\), then \(L_J=v^*\).

notation.meaning: Restricted-master minimizer used in the exactness test.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Exactness of Restricted-Master Bounds
Restricted-Master Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound certificate from finitely many globally valid recourse cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(v^*=\inf_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+Q(x)\}\). Suppose each retained cut \(q_j:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(q_j(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). If the restricted master
\[L_J=\min\{c^\top x+\theta:x\in X,\ \theta\ge q_j(x)\ \text{for all }j\in J\}\]
has an attained finite optimum, then its optimizer, objective value, and verifiable global cut-validity statements form a lower-bound certificate. Indeed, \(\max_{j\in J}q_j(x)\le Q(x)\) pointwise, so the restricted master underestimates the original recourse objective and \(L_J\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite master containing globally valid recourse underestimators certifies a lower bound on the original minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty.
Every retained cut is a global underestimator of \(Q\).
The restricted-master minimum is finite and attained.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound argument and certificate classification are mathematically sound, but no authoritative citation with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Approximation Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound certificate obtained by replacing a conic feasible set with a verified outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\), where \(F=\{x\in X:G(x)\in K\}\). Let \(K\subseteq K_k^{\mathrm{out}}\), with the inclusion certified by the construction of the outer approximation, and define \(F_k^{\mathrm{out}}=\{x\in X:G(x)\in K_k^{\mathrm{out}}\}\). Then \(F\subseteq F_k^{\mathrm{out}}\). If \(L_k=\min_{x\in F_k^{\mathrm{out}}}f(x)\) is finite and attained, the outer solution together with the verified inclusion certifies \(L_k\le v^*\). Adding valid separating cuts shrinks \(F_k^{\mathrm{out}}\) and produces nondecreasing lower bounds while preserving validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing over a certified outer approximation gives a lower bound; valid separating cuts can tighten it monotonically.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(K\subseteq K_k^{\mathrm{out}}\).
Each added cut is valid for every point of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Outer approximation of the cone K.
Feasible set induced by the outer cone.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outer-approximation lower bound and monotonicity claim are correct under the stated inclusions, but the required source and locator are absent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate Dual Feasibility Is Not an Unqualified Bound Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for a proposed Lagrangian lower bound with a stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v^*=\inf\{c^\top x:Ax-b\in K\}\), let \(y\in K^*\) and \(r=c-A^\top y\). Every primal-feasible \(x\) satisfies \(c^\top x\ge b^\top y+r^\top x\). Thus \(b^\top y\) is certified when \(r=0\). If \(r\ne0\), a verified \(\ell\le\inf_{x\in F}r^\top x\), where \(F=\{x:Ax-b\in K\}\), instead certifies \(b^\top y+\ell\le v^*\). Without such domain information, a small stationarity residual alone does not certify \(b^\top y\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact stationarity equation requires a certified correction over the primal feasible set; a small residual alone is not a rigorous lower-bound certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r=0\Rightarrow b^\top y\le v^*\), while \(\ell\le\inf_{x\in F}r^\top x\Rightarrow b^\top y+\ell\le v^*\).

notation.meaning: Verified lower bound on the residual linear form over F.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Dual Feasibility Is Not an Unqualified Bound Certificate
Lagrangian Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a finite-dimensional conic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the conic program
\[v^*=\inf\{c^\top x:Ax-b\in K\},\]
where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. If \(y\in K^*\) satisfies \(A^\top y=c\), then for every primal-feasible \(x\),
\[c^\top x=(A^\top y)^\top x=\langle y,Ax\rangle\ge\langle y,b\rangle=b^\top y.\]
Thus the pair of verifiable conditions \(y\in K^*\) and \(A^\top y=c\), together with the scalar \(b^\top y\), is a Lagrangian dual lower-bound certificate. Its validity requires neither primal attainment nor strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-cone vector satisfying stationarity certifies its dual objective as a lower bound on every primal feasible value.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The primal objective is minimized.
\(y\in K^*\) and \(A^\top y=c\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weak-duality certificate has the correct sign convention and fits the certificate container, but no citation or inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information required for a universal additive recovery from a regularized-master value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\inf_{x\in X}\phi(x)\) and \(M_R=\inf_{x\in X}(\phi(x)+R(x))\). Any verified constant \(\Delta\) satisfying \(R(x)\le\Delta\) for every \(x\in X\) yields \(M_R-\Delta\le L\), without requiring \(R\ge0\). The value \(M_R\) alone admits no universal finite additive correction when no finite upper bound on \(R\) is available: on \(X=\{x_0\}\), choosing \(R(x_0)=T\) gives \(L=M_R-T\) for arbitrary \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified global upper bound on the regularizer yields the additive correction; nonnegativity is unnecessary, while the regularized value alone gives no universal correction.
assumptions_latex: The displayed infima are well-defined in the extended-real sense.
For the positive implication, \(R(x)\le\Delta<\infty\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Verified uniform upper bound on the regularizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Correction Boundary for Regularized Masters
Regularized-Master Bound Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers a valid lower bound after adding a bounded nonnegative master regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_J=\inf_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\max_{j\in J}q_j(x)\}\), where every \(q_j\) underestimates the true recourse function \(Q\). Add a regularizer \(R_k:X\to[0,\Delta_k]\) and solve
\[M_k=\inf_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\max_{j\in J}q_j(x)+R_k(x)\}.\]
Because \(R_k(x)\le\Delta_k\), one has \(M_k\le L_J+\Delta_k\). Therefore \(M_k-\Delta_k\le L_J\le v^*\). The computed regularized-master value and a verifiable uniform upper bound \(\Delta_k\) on the regularizer constitute a recovered lower-bound certificate for the unregularized original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a certified uniform upper bound on a nonnegative regularizer restores a valid lower bound for the original problem.
assumptions_latex: \(q_j(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(j\in J\).
\(0\le R_k(x)\le\Delta_k<\infty\) for every \(x\in X\).
The displayed infima are not \(-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Certified uniform upper bound on the regularizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for a finite-dimensional conic subproblem at a fixed master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\) and let \(d=b-Bx\). Consider the primal subproblem \(\inf\{\langle c,y\rangle:Ay=d,\ y\in K\}\) and its dual \(\sup\{\langle d,z\rangle:c-A^*z\in K^*\}\). A pair \((y,z)\) is an optimality certificate when \(Ay=d\), \(y\in K\), \(s=c-A^*z\in K^*\), and \(\langle y,s\rangle=0\). These relations imply \(\langle c,y\rangle=\langle d,z\rangle\); weak duality then certifies that both points are optimal and that the subproblem value is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and zero complementarity give equal primal and dual values, certifying attained optimality of the fixed-master conic subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(A\) is linear and \(A^*\) denotes its adjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) and \(z\) are primal-dual optimal, with \(v(x)=\langle c,y\rangle=\langle d,z\rangle\).

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separating certificate for infeasibility of a fixed-master conic feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\), set \(d=b-Bx\), and consider \(Ay=d\), \(y\in K\). A vector \(z\) satisfying \(A^*z\in K^*\) and \(\langle d,z\rangle<0\) is an infeasibility certificate. Indeed, every feasible \(y\) would satisfy \(\langle d,z\rangle=\langle Ay,z\rangle=\langle y,A^*z\rangle\geq0\), contradicting the strict inequality. Thus checking cone membership, the adjoint product, and one scalar inequality certifies that the subproblem has no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-cone separator whose pairing with the right-hand side is negative certifies infeasibility of the conic subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(A\) is linear and \(A^*\) denotes its adjoint.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal recession certificate for unboundedness below of a feasible conic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the subproblem \(\inf\{\langle c,y\rangle:Ay=d,\ y\in K\}\), a pair \((y^0,r)\) is an unboundedness certificate when \(Ay^0=d\), \(y^0\in K\), \(Ar=0\), \(r\in K\), and \(\langle c,r\rangle<0\). For every \(t\geq0\), conicity and convexity give \(y^0+tr\in K\) and \(A(y^0+tr)=d\), while \(\langle c,y^0+tr\rangle=\langle c,y^0\rangle+t\langle c,r\rangle\) tends to \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point plus a cone recession direction with negative objective slope certifies that the subproblem is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unboundedness Need Not Admit a Negative-Slope Recession Ray
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnecessity boundary for the standard feasible-base-point plus recession-ray certificate over nonpolyhedral cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{(u,v,w):u\geq0,\ v\geq0,\ 2uv\geq w^2\}\) and consider \(\inf\{w:u=1,\ (u,v,w)\in K\}\). For every \(w\in\mathbb R\), \((1,w^2/2,w)\) is feasible, so the value is \(-\infty\). Yet any \(r=(r_u,r_v,r_w)\in K\) with \(r_u=0\) has \(r_w=0\); hence no feasible recession direction has negative objective slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpolyhedral conic subproblem can be unbounded along a curved feasible path while having no negative-slope recession direction.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the three-dimensional rotated second-order cone.
The equality fixes \(u=1\), and the objective minimizes \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{w:u=1,\ (u,v,w)\in K\}=-\infty\), but no \(r\in K\) satisfies \(r_u=0\) and \(r_w<0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\unlhd K\), set \(V=\operatorname{span}F\), and suppose every \(u\in K\) satisfying \(Au=d\) belongs to \(F\). A facially reduced optimality certificate consists of \(y\in F\) and \(z\) such that \(Ay=d\), \(q=P_V(c-A^*z)\in F_V^*\), and \(\langle q,y\rangle=0\), where \(P_V\) is orthogonal projection onto \(V\) and \(F_V^*=\{v\in V:\langle v,u\rangle\geq0\text{ for every }u\in F\}\). These conditions certify optimality over the reduced face and, by the stated face-containment hypothesis, over the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and complementary dual slack on a valid reduced face certify optimality for the original subproblem when every original feasible point lies in that face.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Slater Condition on a Valid Reduced Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of reduced-face dual certificates after a face containing the original feasible region has been validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\unlhd K\), \(V=\operatorname{span}F\), and suppose \(\{u\in K:Au=d\}\subseteq F\). If some \(\bar u\in\operatorname{ri}F\) satisfies \(A\bar u=d\) and \(\inf\{\langle c,u\rangle:Au=d,\ u\in F\}\) is finite, then the reduced dual over \(F_V^*\) attains the same value. Consequently, every attained primal optimum \(u^*\) admits \(z\) with \(q=P_V(c-A^*z)\in F_V^*\) and \(\langle q,u^*\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strict feasibility on a valid containing face gives zero gap and reduced-dual attainment, so every attained primal optimum has a reduced-face KKT certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space and \(F\unlhd K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Slater Condition on a Valid Reduced Face
Indeterminate Subproblem Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak infeasibility shows why failure to obtain standard status certificates is not a status certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the semidefinite system \(X\succeq0\), \(X_{11}=0\), and \(X_{12}=1\), positive semidefiniteness would force \(X_{12}=0\), so the system is infeasible. Nevertheless, \(X(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1/t&1\\1&t\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) for \(t>0\), and its distance to the affine constraints tends to zero as \(t\to\infty\). Hence the cone and affine space are disjoint but have zero distance, so no strict separating certificate of the usual form need exist. Absence of optimality, strong-infeasibility, and recession certificates therefore leaves status indeterminate without facial reduction or extended certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly infeasible semidefinite system can approach feasibility arbitrarily closely while admitting no strict separator, making ordinary certificate failure inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) ranges over real symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices.
Distance is measured using any norm on this finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system is weakly infeasible, and failure to find a strict separator does not certify feasibility.

notation.meaning: positive-semidefinite sequence approaching the affine system

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural characterization of the feasibility status that ordinary strict separation cannot resolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ay=d\), \(y\in K\), let \(C=A(K)\). The system is feasible exactly when \(d\in C\), weakly infeasible exactly when \(d\in\operatorname{cl}C\setminus C\), and strongly infeasible exactly when \(d\notin\operatorname{cl}C\). Equivalently, weak infeasibility means infeasibility together with \(\operatorname{dist}(d,C)=0\), whereas strong infeasibility has positive distance and admits strict separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak infeasibility occurs precisely when the right-hand side lies in the closure, but not the image, of the conic constraint map.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty convex cone in a finite-dimensional normed space.
\(A\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\in\operatorname{cl}(A(K))\setminus A(K)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \{y\in K:Ay=d\}\text{ is weakly infeasible}.

Linking-Multiplier Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agreement condition for duplicated multipliers of a shared linking constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose decomposed blocks use local copies \(\lambda_s\) of the multiplier for the shared equality \(\sum_{s\in S}L_sy_s=h\), while the master uses \(\lambda\). Linking-multiplier consistency is the predicate \(\lambda_s=\lambda\) for every \(s\in S\). Equivalently, every block Lagrangian contains the same linking price through \(L_s^*\lambda\). If only restrictions to subspaces \(U_s\) affect block stationarity, the minimal condition is \(L_s^*(\lambda_s-\lambda)=0\) for every block; full equality is the canonical certificate when multiplier copies share one ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All block copies of a shared linking multiplier must equal the master multiplier, or at least induce identical adjoint prices on their blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and each \(L_s\) is linear.
All \(\lambda_s\) and \(\lambda\) belong to the linking constraint's dual space.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Multiplier Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility between the master price and each conic pricing subproblem's dual stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block \(s\), let the pricing problem be \(\inf\{\langle c_s+L_s^*\lambda,y_s\rangle:A_sy_s=b_s,\ y_s\in K_s\}\). A pricing multiplier \(z_s\) is consistent with master price \(\lambda\) when \(q_s=c_s+L_s^*\lambda-A_s^*z_s\in K_s^*\). For a returned column \(y_s\), certificate consistency additionally requires \(A_sy_s=b_s\), \(y_s\in K_s\), and \(\langle q_s,y_s\rangle=0\). Thus the reduced-cost functional used by the oracle is exactly the one induced by the master multiplier, with no sign, scaling, or stale-price discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricing certificate is consistent when its reduced-cost slack uses exactly the current master price and satisfies conic primal-dual complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(K_s\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A_s\) and \(L_s\) are linear maps with defined adjoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_s\) and \(z_s\) satisfy the primal-dual optimality relations for the pricing problem parameterized by \(\lambda\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient Pricing Functionals Depend Only on the Induced Adjoint Price
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability of a master multiplier from its objective functional on the ambient variable space of one pricing block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the ambient block objective y_s\mapsto\langle c_s+L_s^*\lambda,y_s\rangle, two master multipliers \lambda and \widehat\lambda induce the same linear functional on every ambient y_s if and only if L_s^*(\widehat\lambda-\lambda)=0. Thus the ambient pricing functional identifies the master multiplier only modulo \ker L_s^*. If observations are restricted to a proper feasible affine set, additional multiplier differences may be observationally invisible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the ambient block space, pricing sees a master multiplier only through its adjoint image; restriction to the feasible set may reveal still less.
