knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Face Multiplier Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual compatibility condition when a conic subproblem is solved over a reduced face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_s\unlhd K_s\) be the face used by subproblem \(s\), and let \(V_s=\operatorname{span}F_s\). A multiplier certificate is cone-face consistent when its slack \(q_s\) restricts to an element of the face dual \(F_s^*\), the stationarity equation holds on \(V_s\), and \(\langle q_s,y_s\rangle=0\) for the certified \(y_s\in F_s\). Two ambient slacks \(q_s\) and \(\widetilde q_s\) encode the same reduced-face multiplier exactly when \(q_s-\widetilde q_s\in V_s^\perp\). Requiring \(q_s\in K_s^*\) is stronger and is necessary when the certificate must also be valid without facial reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-face multiplier must be dual feasible and complementary on that face; ambient representatives may differ only by vectors orthogonal to its span.
assumptions_latex: \(K_s\) is a closed convex cone and \(F_s\unlhd K_s\).
\(y_s\in F_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_s|_{V_s}\in F_s^*\), \(\langle q_s,y_s\rangle=0\), and equivalent representatives differ by \(V_s^\perp\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dantzig-Wolfe reconstruction when a block feasible set has both generating points and recession rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Y_s=\operatorname{conv}\{p_s^j:j\in J_s\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_s^k:k\in R_s\}\). If \(\theta_{sj}\ge0\), \(\rho_{sk}\ge0\), and \(\sum_{j\in J_s}\theta_{sj}=1\), then \(\widehat y_s=\sum_j\theta_{sj}p_s^j+\sum_k\rho_{sk}r_s^k\in Y_s\). Consequently, such weights together with satisfaction of all master linking equations certify primal feasibility. Ray weights are not included in the convex normalization; treating a recession ray as a normalized point column need not preserve affine block constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered block combines normalized feasible point columns with nonnegative recession columns; only point weights sum to one, and the aggregate must satisfy all linking equations.

Column-Combination Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal recovery certificate from a convex combination of generated block columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every block \(s\), let generated columns \(y_s^j\in K_s\) satisfy \(A_sy_s^j=b_s\). Weights \(\theta_{sj}\geq0\) with \(\sum_j\theta_{sj}=1\) define \(\widehat y_s=\sum_j\theta_{sj}y_s^j\). The weights and columns form a column-combination feasibility certificate when the master linking equations \(\sum_sL_s\widehat y_s=h\) hold. Convexity gives \(\widehat y_s\in K_s\), and linearity gives \(A_s\widehat y_s=b_s\); hence the reconstructed block vector is feasible for all local conic constraints and the global linking constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders-Incumbent Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a master set \(X\) and scenario recourse systems \(A_sy_s=b_s-B_sx\), \(y_s\in K_s\). A Benders incumbent \(\widehat x\) is certified feasible by recourse witnesses \((\widehat y_s)_{s\in S}\) when \(\widehat x\in X\) and, for every scenario, \(A_s\widehat y_s=b_s-B_s\widehat x\) and \(\widehat y_s\in K_s\). If the model also has linking equations \(L\widehat x+\sum_sL_s\widehat y_s=h\), these must be checked as part of the certificate. The displayed witnesses directly establish feasibility of the corresponding extensive-form conic model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual identity and the limit of approximate Lagrangian primal recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha_k\ge0\) with \(\sum_k\alpha_k=1\), define \(\widehat y_s=\sum_k\alpha_k y_s^k\) and \(r^k=\sum_sL_sy_s^k-h\). Then \(\widehat r=\sum_sL_s\widehat y_s-h=\sum_k\alpha_k r^k\). Thus cancellation can give \(\widehat r=0\) even if no stored iterate is globally feasible. Conversely, \(\|\widehat r\|\le\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon>0\) gives only approximate coupling feasibility and does not certify a nearby exactly feasible point without a verified error bound or explicit feasible correction.

Every stored iterate satisfies all unrelaxed local constraints.

Then \(L\le p^*\le U\), and the global gap decomposes as \[U-L=\sum_{i=1}^m(U_i-L_i).\] Thus the collection of block certificates, together with the asserted separability, is an aggregate completion certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Balance Does Not Imply Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for substituting comparative residual balance for absolute feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \tau\ge1 and M>0, the pair (\rho_p,\rho_d)=(M,M) is \tau-balanced, although both residuals can be arbitrarily large. Hence residual balance alone certifies neither primal nor dual feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Balance Does Not Imply Feasibility
Primal-Dual Residual Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric ratio test preventing one scaled feasibility residual from dominating the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_p,\rho_d\ge0\) be scaled primal and dual residuals, and fix \(\tau\ge1\). The residuals are \(\tau\)-balanced when \[\rho_p\le\tau\rho_d\quad\text{and}\quad\rho_d\le\tau\rho_p.\] If both are positive, this is equivalent to \(\tau^{-1}\le\rho_p/\rho_d\le\tau\). If exactly one residual is zero, balance fails; if both vanish, balance holds. Balance is a diagnostic condition and does not replace separate feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual scaled residuals are balanced when neither exceeds the other by more than a prescribed factor.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_p,\rho_d\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\|Ax-b-s\|\) and \(D=\|b\|+\|Ax\|+\|s\|\), and uniformly rescale the affine equation by \(\alpha>0\). Moreover, \(\rho_p(\alpha)\to0\) as \(\alpha\downarrow0\), while \(\rho_p(\alpha)\to N/D\) as \(\alpha\to\infty\) when \(D>0\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adopt the positive-dual convention \(K^*=\{y:\langle y,s\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }s\in K\}\). If a certificate reports \(s\in K\) and \(y\in K^*\), polarity consistency requires \(\langle y,s\rangle\ge0\). For the primal problem \(\min c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(s=Ax-b\in K\), dual stationarity \(A^{\mathsf T}y=c\) gives the primal-dual gap \[c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle y,s\rangle\ge0.\] A negative displayed gap therefore signals incompatible signs, cone polarity, or failed membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the positive-dual convention, feasible primal and dual slacks pair nonnegatively, and that pairing equals the primal-dual objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(s=Ax-b\in K\).
\(y\in K^*\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}y=c\).

children.title: Boundary-Membership Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Numerical ambiguity for quantities near primal or dual cone boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Membership Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes tolerance-based acceptance from exact cone membership near a closed cone boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, let \(\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\delta>0\) bound the unknown error by \(\|x-\widehat x\|\leq\delta\). Membership is ambiguous at resolution \(\delta\) precisely when
\[
B(\widehat x,\delta)\cap K\neq\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
B(\widehat x,\delta)\cap(\mathbb R^n\setminus K)\neq\varnothing.
\]
In particular, if \(\widehat x\in\partial K\), every ball of positive radius centered at \(\widehat x\) contains a point outside \(K\); hence a residual or distance test accepting \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,K)\leq\delta\) does not by itself certify exact membership of the unknown \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical point is membership-ambiguous when its error ball meets both the cone and its complement; a small cone-distance residual then cannot certify exact membership.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(\|x-\widehat x\|\leq\delta\) with \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(\widehat x,\delta)\cap K\neq\varnothing\) and \(B(\widehat x,\delta)\cap K^c\neq\varnothing\) imply that exact membership is unresolved.

notation.meaning: Closed norm ball of radius delta around the reported point.
Distance from x to K in the chosen norm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives sufficient error-ball margins resolving membership away from the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and suppose \(\|x-\widehat x\|\leq\delta\). If \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,K)>\delta\), then \(x\notin K\). If \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,K^c)>\delta\), then \(x\in K\). When neither strict margin holds, these tests alone need not resolve membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict distance margin from the cone or its complement makes the error ball certainly outside or inside.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is closed.
\(\|x-\widehat x\|\leq\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,K)>\delta\Rightarrow x\notin K,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,K^c)>\delta\Rightarrow x\in K.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Inside and Outside Margins
Face-Membership Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validation for membership in an exposed face of a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone and let \(y\in K^*\). The set \(F_y=K\cap y^\perp\) is an exposed face of \(K\). For any candidate \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
x\in F_y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in K\ \text{ and }\ \langle y,x\rangle=0.
\]
Thus the pair consisting of a valid cone-membership certificate for \(x\in K\) and an independently evaluated equality \(\langle y,x\rangle=0\) certifies face membership. Under numerical tolerances, the inequalities \(\operatorname{dist}(x,K)\leq\varepsilon_K\) and \(|\langle y,x\rangle|\leq\varepsilon_\perp\) certify only tolerance-level membership unless error bounds imply the exact conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in the exposed face defined by a dual vector requires both primal cone membership and zero pairing with that vector.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.

notation.meaning: Exposed face K intersected with the hyperplane orthogonal to y.
Set of vectors having zero inner product with y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validation for Finite Intersections of Exposed Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends face-membership validation to finitely many dual-cone exposing vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone and \(y_1,\ldots,y_p\in K^*\). Then \[K\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^p y_j^\perp=K\cap\left(\sum_{j=1}^p y_j\right)^\perp.\] Thus the intersection is an exposed face, and \(x\) belongs to it exactly when \(x\in K\) and \(\langle y_j,x\rangle=0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite intersection of faces exposed by dual-cone vectors is exposed by their sum.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(y_j\in K^*\) for every \(j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Checker Rejection Is Not a Problem-Status Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates rejection of a submitted witness from conclusions about the underlying problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V(D,w)\in\{\mathrm{accept},\mathrm{reject}\}\) be a sound verifier: acceptance implies the status claimed by witness \(w\). Soundness alone supplies no converse. Therefore \(V(D,w)=\mathrm{reject}\) establishes only that \(w\) failed this verifier; it does not show that the claimed status is false or independently certify infeasibility, unboundedness, or suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checker failure rejects the submitted certificate but does not determine the optimization problem's true status.
assumptions_latex: The verifier is sound but need not be complete.
The conclusion concerns the submitted witness.

notation.meaning: Verifier applied to original data D and witness w.

knowledge_statements.title: Checker Rejection Is Not a Problem-Status Certificate
Independent Certificate Rechecking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recomputes a conic certificate from original data without trusting solver-reported residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input conic data \((A,b,c,K)\), a reported primal-dual tuple \((\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)\), claimed bounds \((L,U)\), and tolerances \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_K,\varepsilon_g)\). Using arithmetic independent of the producing solver, compute
\[
r_p=A\widehat x-b,\qquad r_d=A^*\widehat y+\widehat s-c,
\]
cone distances \(d_p=\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x,K)\), \(d_d=\operatorname{dist}(\widehat s,K^*)\), and the claimed gap \(g=U-L\). Accept only if \(\|r_p\|\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|\leq\varepsilon_d\), \(d_p,d_d\leq\varepsilon_K\), \(0\leq g\leq\varepsilon_g\), and recomputed objectives and decomposition identities reproduce \(L\) and \(U\) within their declared errors; otherwise output the failed checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent checker recomputes residuals, cone distances, objectives, bounds, and decomposition identities from original data, accepting only when every declared tolerance is satisfied.
assumptions_latex: The primal conic model and its dual use compatible data \((A,b,c,K)\).
All norms, arithmetic precision, and acceptance tolerances are fixed before rechecking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance requires every independently recomputed feasibility, cone-membership, gap, objective, and assembly check to pass.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the constraint operator A.
Claimed lower and upper objective bounds.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly specifies this independent rechecking interface.
standard_field_rationale: recomputation from original data is the standard verifier pattern for numerical optimization certificates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but no inspectable source supports this particular checker. The primal-dual model convention, the derivation of L and U from the tuple, and the declared-error rules needed to reproduce those bounds are not specified sufficiently to validate the algorithmic interface.

children.title: Invalid Master Bounds
children.top_down_role: Master-side bound defects implicated in decomposition certificate failure.

assumptions_latex: \(v^*\) is the finite optimal value of a minimization problem with objective \(f\).
\(L_M\) is claimed to be a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_M>v^*\) invalidates the master bound, and \(f(x)<L_M\) for a globally feasible \(x\) certifies invalidity.

notation.meaning: Objective function of the original minimization problem.
Lower bound claimed by the master problem.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats validity of decomposition master bounds.
standard_field_rationale: lower and upper bounds follow from the definition of a minimization optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the minimization convention in which the master problem supplies a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a minimization problem with objective \(f\), feasible set \(X\), and finite optimal value \(v^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), and let a master problem claim the lower bound \(L_M\). The bound is valid exactly when \(L_M\leq v^*\), and it is invalid when \(L_M>v^*\). Because \(v^*\) may be unknown, any globally feasible point \(x\in X\) satisfying
\[
f(x)<L_M
\]
is a directly checkable witness that the claimed master lower bound is invalid. More generally, a certified feasible upper bound \(U\) with \(U<L_M\) exposes the same failure. A master value obtained from cuts or relaxations is not a valid bound unless every ingredient used to derive it is itself globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, a master lower bound is invalid if it exceeds the true optimum; any certified feasible objective value below it witnesses the failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Master Bounds

children.title: Invalid Subproblem Bounds
children.top_down_role: Subproblem-side bound defects implicated in decomposition certificate failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Subproblem Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes invalid lower and upper bounds for a fixed minimization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a master decision \(z\) and let the associated minimization subproblem have finite value \(q(z)\). A claimed subproblem lower bound \(\ell(z)\) is valid only if \(\ell(z)\leq q(z)\), while a claimed upper bound \(u(z)\) is valid only if \(q(z)\leq u(z)\). Consequently,
\[
\ell(z)>q(z)\quad\text{or}\quad u(z)<q(z)
\]
constitutes an invalid subproblem bound. If both quantities are claimed as valid and \(\ell(z)>u(z)\), at least one claim is necessarily invalid. A dual value supplies \(\ell(z)\) only when dual feasibility and weak-duality hypotheses are verified; a primal value supplies \(u(z)\) only when primal feasibility is verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subproblem lower bound cannot exceed its value, and an upper bound cannot fall below it; a lower bound above an upper bound exposes invalidity.
assumptions_latex: The fixed-decision subproblem is a minimization problem with finite value \(q(z)\).
\(\ell(z)\) and \(u(z)\) are respectively claimed lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity requires \(\ell(z)\leq q(z)\leq u(z)\); hence \(\ell(z)>u(z)\) refutes the joint claim.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the subproblem at master decision z.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats decomposition subproblem-bound validation.
standard_field_rationale: the inequalities are the defining predicates for lower and upper bounds.

children.title: Cross-Level Bound Incompatibility
children.top_down_role: Structural conflicts between bounds produced at distinct decomposition levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Level Bound Incompatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects contradiction between certified master and assembled subproblem bounds in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v^*\) be the value of a minimization problem. Suppose the master level claims a global lower bound \(L_M\leq v^*\), while a feasible master decision together with validated subproblem certificates yields a global upper bound \(v^*\leq U_D\). The cross-level claims are compatible only if
\[
L_M\leq U_D.
\]
If \(L_M>U_D\), no real value \(v^*\) can satisfy both claims, so at least one master bound, subproblem bound, feasibility assertion, or assembly identity is invalid. With certified absolute errors \(e_M,e_D\geq0\), incompatibility is conclusive when \(L_M-e_M>U_D+e_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master and decomposed bounds are incompatible when the certified master lower bound exceeds the certified assembled upper bound, after accounting for validated errors.
assumptions_latex: \(L_M\) is claimed as a global lower bound for a minimization problem.
\(U_D\) is claimed as a globally feasible upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_M>U_D\), or \(L_M-e_M>U_D+e_D\) with error bounds, implies that the cross-level claims cannot all be valid.

notation.meaning: Upper bound assembled from feasible decomposition data.
Certified absolute errors on the two bounds.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers cross-level decomposition-bound consistency.
standard_field_rationale: simultaneous lower and upper bounds must enclose the same optimal value.

children.title: Certificate Failure from Bound Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Loss of certificate validity attributable specifically to conflicting bound information.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Failure from Bound Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when conflicting bounds invalidate a combined decomposition certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A minimization certificate claiming \(L\leq v^*\leq U\) and accuracy at most \(\varepsilon\geq0\) must satisfy
\[
0\leq U-L\leq\varepsilon.
\]
The certificate fails whenever independently validated bounds give \(L>U\), because their asserted intervals have empty intersection. It also fails as an \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate when \(U-L>\varepsilon\). For decomposed bounds \(L=\max_j L_j\) and \(U=\min_k U_k\), any pair \(L_j>U_k\) is a conflict witness. The failure identifies inconsistency, but without further evidence it does not determine whether the lower-bound derivation, upper-bound derivation, or cross-level aggregation is responsible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combined certificate fails if its lower bound exceeds its upper bound, or if their nonnegative gap exceeds the claimed accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and \(U\) are claimed bounds on the same finite minimization value \(v^*\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\) is the claimed absolute optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certificate validity requires \(0\leq U-L\leq\varepsilon\); violation refutes the combined claim.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly specifies failure of a combined decomposition certificate.
standard_field_rationale: an optimality certificate requires a nonempty bound interval of the claimed width.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Residual Bound with Assembly Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies how local residuals and assembly mismatch bound the global residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(r=\sum_{i=1}^mE_ir_i+\Delta\), then for compatible vector and induced operator norms, \[\|r\|\leq\sum_{i=1}^m\|E_i\|\,\|r_i\|+\|\Delta\|.\] Hence \(\|r_i\|\leq\varepsilon_i\) and \(\|\Delta\|\leq\varepsilon_{\rm asm}\) imply \(\|r\|\leq\sum_i\|E_i\|\varepsilon_i+\varepsilon_{\rm asm}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mapped local residual bounds and the assembly-error bound jointly bound the global residual.
assumptions_latex: Each \(E_i\) is linear.
The vector norms and induced operator norms are compatible.

notation.meaning: Induced operator norm of assembly map i.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Residual Bound with Assembly Error
Decomposed Residual Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares the global residual with the residual assembled from decomposition blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a global equality system be \(Ax=b\), with global residual \(r=Ax-b\). Suppose a decomposition reports local residuals \(r_i=A_i x_i-b_i\) and fixed assembly maps \(E_i\) such that exact consistency requires
\[
r=\sum_{i=1}^m E_i r_i.
\]
Define the mismatch \(\Delta=r-\sum_{i=1}^mE_i r_i\). The decomposed certificate is assembly-inconsistent when \(\Delta\neq0\); under a declared tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{asm}}\), it fails validation when \(\|\Delta\|>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{asm}}\). Small local residuals alone do not certify global feasibility if omitted coupling equations, incompatible shared-variable copies, or incorrect assembly maps make \(\Delta\) nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local residuals certify the global system only when their mapped sum reproduces the independently computed global residual within the declared assembly tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The global and local residuals are computed from the same candidate solution.
The assembly maps \(E_i\) are fixed by the decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left\|r-\sum_iE_i r_i\right\|>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{asm}}\) invalidates the assembled residual certificate.

notation.meaning: Map embedding local residual i into the global residual space.
Difference between global and assembled local residuals.

review_flags: No supplied locator defines residual assembly for this decomposition hierarchy.
standard_field_rationale: consistency requires two computations of the same residual to agree.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unshifted Approximate Cuts Need Not Be Valid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies invalid lower bounds caused by omitting a certified oracle-error shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q:Z\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) and suppose an affine model \(\ell\) satisfies \(q(z)\geq\ell(z)-\delta\) for all \(z\in Z\), where \(\delta\geq0\) is certified. Then \(\ell-\delta\) is a valid lower model. Unless \(q\geq\ell\) is independently established, the unshifted model can overestimate \(q\) by as much as \(\delta\), invalidating a master lower bound and producing a falsely small termination gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate lower cut must be shifted downward by its certified error unless the unshifted cut is independently valid.
assumptions_latex: \(q(z)\geq\ell(z)-\delta\) for every \(z\in Z\).
\(\delta\geq0\) is a verified uniform error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Unshifted Approximate Cuts Need Not Be Valid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified directional information required for lower- and upper-bound assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an exact oracle value \(q_i\), a certified lower response satisfies \(\underline q_i\le q_i\), while a certified upper response satisfies \(q_i\le\overline q_i\). Symmetric absolute-error control is unnecessary when only one bound direction is used. If \(q=\sum_iq_i\), then
\[
\sum_i\underline q_i\le q\le
otag\sum_i\overline q_i.
\]
An oracle response lacking a verified inequality in the required direction cannot certify the assembled bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-bound assembly needs certified underestimates, upper-bound assembly needs certified overestimates, and additive one-sided guarantees sum across blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(q=\sum_iq_i\).
Each one-sided inequality is independently verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall i)\;\underline q_i\le q_i\le\overline q_i\Rightarrow\sum_i\underline q_i\le q\le\sum_i\overline q_i\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower oracle value for block i.
Certified upper oracle value for block i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Zero Reported Gap from an Uncertified Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal false-completion example caused by an unverified oracle bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let p^\star=0, let a feasible incumbent give U=1, and let an inexact oracle report \widetilde L=1 without certifying \widetilde L\le p^\star. Then U-\widetilde L=0 although U-p^\star=1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertified oracle can make the reported gap vanish while the incumbent remains one unit above the optimum.
assumptions_latex: p^\star=0.
U=1 is a valid feasible upper bound.
\widetilde L=1 has no verified lower-bound guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: A Zero Reported Gap from an Uncertified Lower Bound
Uncertified Inexact-Oracle Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Excludes termination based on oracle values lacking validated error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a decomposition method uses inexact oracle values \(\widetilde q_i\) for exact subproblem values \(q_i\). An oracle result is certified only when it includes a verified finite error \(\delta_i\geq0\) satisfying \(|\widetilde q_i-q_i|\leq\delta_i\), or a one-sided analogue sufficient for the bound being formed. If termination is declared from a reported gap \(\widetilde U-\widetilde L\leq\varepsilon\), then completion is uncertified whenever no such error bounds are available. With additive certified errors \(e_U,e_L\), the defensible worst-case gap is
\[
(\widetilde U+e_U)-(\widetilde L-e_L).
\]
Thus termination also fails certification when this corrected gap exceeds \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact oracle cannot justify termination without validated error bounds; the reported gap must remain within tolerance after worst-case error correction.
assumptions_latex: The method claims absolute gap tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
Oracle errors may affect the reported lower or upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Completion is uncertified if finite verified oracle-error bounds are absent or if \((\widetilde U+e_U)-(\widetilde L-e_L)>\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Inexact value returned by oracle i.
Verified absolute error bound for oracle i.
Aggregated certified errors in reported bounds.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifies certified stopping with inexact decomposition oracles.
standard_field_rationale: interval error propagation requires widening lower and upper bounds in adverse directions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the statement makes a broad necessity claim about how every inexact-oracle result must be certified and how aggregate errors enter termination. A source is needed to fix the oracle model, one-sided error conventions, aggregation rules, and the exact stopping guarantee before this formulation can be accepted.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Frobenius Distance to the Positive-Semidefinite Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a norm-specific PSD-distance diagnostic for numerical certificate rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=X^{\mathsf T}=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)Q^{\mathsf T}\), let \(X_-=Q\operatorname{diag}(\max\{-\lambda_i,0\})Q^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[\operatorname{dist}_F(X,\mathbb S_+^n)=\|X_-\|_F=\left(\sum_{\lambda_i<0}\lambda_i^2\right)^{1/2}.\] A rigorous lower enclosure exceeding the declared tolerance rejects PSD membership at that tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Frobenius distance to the PSD cone is the Frobenius norm of the negative spectral part.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\).
Distance is measured in the Frobenius norm.

notation.meaning: Positive-semidefinite matrix formed from the magnitudes of the negative eigenvalues of X.

knowledge_statements.title: Frobenius Distance to the Positive-Semidefinite Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validated Spectral Enclosure for PSD Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts certified ordered-eigenvalue intervals into a Frobenius-distance enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) have ordered eigenvalues with certified enclosures \(\lambda_i(X)\in[\ell_i,u_i]\). Set \(a_i=\max\{-u_i,0\}\) and \(b_i=\max\{-\ell_i,0\}\). Then
\[
\left(\sum_i a_i^2\right)^{1/2}\le \operatorname{dist}_F(X,\mathbb S_+^n)\le \left(\sum_i b_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified ordered-eigenvalue intervals give rigorous lower and upper bounds on Frobenius distance to the positive-semidefinite cone.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\).
Each \([\ell_i,u_i]\) rigorously encloses the correspondingly ordered eigenvalue.
Distance is measured in the Frobenius norm.

notation.meaning: Lower and upper bounds on the magnitude of the negative part of eigenvalue i.

review_flags: The eigenvalue intervals must correspond to a common ordering; unordered interval collections do not justify componentwise aggregation.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Spectral Enclosure for PSD Distance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous acceptance, rejection, and indeterminate outcomes from certified numerical enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix the norms defining \(d_p=\operatorname{dist}(x,K)\) and \(d_d=\operatorname{dist}(s,K^*)\). Suppose certified enclosures
\[
d_p\in[\underline d_p,\overline d_p],\qquad d_d\in[\underline d_d,\overline d_d],\qquad |\langle x,s\rangle|\in[\underline c,\overline c]
\]
are available. Reject if a lower endpoint exceeds its tolerance; accept at the declared tolerances if every upper endpoint is within tolerance; otherwise return indeterminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified lower bounds justify rejection, certified upper bounds justify tolerance-level acceptance, and unresolved intervals require an indeterminate result.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The distance norms and tolerances are declared before validation.
Every displayed interval rigorously encloses the exact quantity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline d_p>\varepsilon_p\) or \(\underline d_d>\varepsilon_d\) or \(\underline c>\varepsilon_c\) implies rejection; \(\overline d_p\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\overline d_d\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\overline c\le\varepsilon_c\) imply tolerance-level acceptance; all other cases are indeterminate.

notation.meaning: Certified enclosure of an exact validation quantity.

review_flags: Tolerance-level acceptance is not an exact cone-membership or complementarity proof.
knowledge_statements.title: Tri-State Norm-Specific Cone Validation
Numerically Invalid Cone Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejects primal-dual cone certificates whose independently computed violations exceed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a closed convex cone \(K\), a reported primal-dual pair \((x,s)\) intended to satisfy \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and complementarity must be rejected at tolerances \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_c)\) if any independently computed condition
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,K)>\varepsilon_p,\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(s,K^*)>\varepsilon_d,\qquad
|\langle x,s\rangle|>\varepsilon_c
\]
holds. Passing these tests establishes only numerical validity at the stated tolerances. Exact cone membership requires exact arithmetic, interval enclosures, or another rigorous representation that resolves boundary uncertainty. For the semidefinite cone, the distance tests may be implemented through validated eigenvalue bounds rather than unverified floating-point eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical cone certificate is invalid when primal distance, dual distance, or complementarity exceeds tolerance; passing floating-point tests alone does not prove exact membership.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
The distances and pairing are recomputed independently under declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any displayed tolerance violation invalidates the numerical primal-dual cone certificate.

The norm defining cone distance is unspecified, and validated eigenvalue bounds do not by themselves define a cone-distance computation without a chosen matrix norm and an explicit error rule.
